Among the benefits of the staff: ﴿And I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep⁠﴾ (Ta-Ha), i.e., I strike the leaves of trees with it so that they fall and the sheep and livestock eat them, because the shepherd walks with it in the desert, where the animals graze on the ʿidhy, which is the natural vegetation that no one has planted and which is watered only by rain. If this grass runs out, the shepherd turns to tall trees and knocks down their leaves for the sheep to eat, and he needs the staff to perform this task.

So: his saying ﴿I lean upon it⁠﴾ (Ta-Ha) is for his own rest, and ﴿I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep⁠﴾ (Ta-Ha) is for serving the flock. In it is the management of provision for the livestock and for people. Herding sheep and managing them is a training in governing the whole nation; therefore Allah did not send any prophet except that he herded sheep, so that he might learn from managing livestock the management of humankind.

In the noble hadith: "Allah did not send any prophet except that he herded sheep, and I used to herd them for the people of Makkah for qararit (ʿqarariṭ)."⁽⁴⁾

When Musa – peace be upon him – sensed that he had lengthened his address to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, he summarized and said: ﴿And I have in it other uses⁠﴾ (Ta-Ha), i.e., benefits.

The scholars⁽⁵⁾ – may Allah reward them on our behalf with good – have sought to explore these other uses that Musa, peace be upon him, did not mention. They reflected on the condition of shepherds and the function of the staff in their lives, and found for it other benefits beyond what was mentioned.

Among these benefits: the primitive shepherd places his staff on his shoulder and hangs from it his food and drink. Some shepherds also use their time in hunting, so they need tools such as the bow, arrows, darts, and the pouch in which they collect their game. You see him place his staff on his shoulder crosswise, and hang these tools from both sides. When the sun's heat intensifies and he finds no shade, he plants his staff in the ground and throws his garment over it, making from it something like a tent or canopy that protects him from the heat. If he needs water, he goes to the well, and perhaps finds the water deep so that the bucket does not reach it, so he needs the staff, which he ties and uses to lengthen the rope, and so on, among other benefits.

Some scholars say: Musa, peace be upon him, was expecting that his Lord would ask him about these uses so that he could prolong the conversation with Him, but the Truth, glorified is He, did not ask him about that, because He was going to move him on to something more important than the matter of the staff. It is as if He said: "What you have mentioned, O Musa, is the staff's purpose with you; as for Me, I want to tell you of its purpose with Me."

¹ Al-istabraq: thick brocade, which is a natural silk, suitable for winter because it is warm, and for outer garments. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/18). ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said in his interpretation of this verse (Ar-Rahman 45): "These are the linings; how then would you see the outer surfaces?"
² Ar-rafraf: wide or thin silk garments, and here it is a metaphor for bliss, i.e., on beautiful green silken cushions. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/271)
³ Al-ʿabqari: these are the rugs that have colors and designs (Lisan al-ʿArab – root: ʿ-b-q-r).
⁴ Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2262), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2149), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (4/441): "Suwayd, one of its narrators, said: that is, each sheep for qararit. That is, the qirat, which is a part of the dinar or the dirham."
⁵ Among them is Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "When I reached the top of the well, I joined the rope to the staff; when the heat of the sun struck me, I planted it in the ground and cast over it what would shade me; when I feared some creeping thing of the earth, I killed it with it; and when I walked, I placed it on my shoulder and hung from it the bow, the quiver, and the pouch. And I fought the beasts of prey off the sheep with it." (See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4360, 4361)

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He said: "Throw it down, O Moses!"﴾ (19).

Cast it on the ground. Here the throwing is one of training and practice for meeting Pharaoh. Here the staff departed from its usual nature, which Moses (peace be upon him) knew, so it was no longer for leaning on and driving off the sheep. Rather, it passed from the kind of wood to the kind of animal, so it became a serpent. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So he threw it down, and behold, it was a serpent, moving swiftly (20).﴾

This is a major shift in the matter of the staff. For the proof of the miracle, it was possible for the staff, which is a dry piece of wood, to turn into a green tree. But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, makes this miracle come to Moses, because he will need it later. Had the staff turned into a green tree, it would have remained in its place; but when it turns into a serpent, it is a moving creature, going here and there, and this is what Moses will need in his coming battle.

Moses cast his staff, ﴿Then behold, it was...﴾ (Ta-Ha, 20). Idha (then behold, sudden) here is the sudden particle (idha al-fuja'iyya), as you say: "I went out, and behold, a lion was at the door." When Moses cast the staff, it quickly transformed, though it was dry and withered, into a serpent, and a serpent that moves swiftly, not inert and dead. Is this not a surprise?

It is natural that Moses, peace be upon him, should be afraid of what he saw, so his Lord reassured him, and He said: ﴿He said: "Take it, and fear not. We shall return it to its former state."﴾ (Ta-Ha, 21).

Its meaning: hold it in your hand, and We will return it at once ﴿to its former state﴾ (Ta-Ha), that is, as it was, a dry, stiff staff in your hand. And He said: ﴿Do not fear...﴾ (Ta-Ha), because of the signs of fear that appeared on him. He reported his fear in another verse: ﴿So Musa felt a fear in his soul﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:67).

This matter was a training and a trial for Musa (peace be upon him). The staff has a role in his mission: it will be his miracle in his contest with Fir'awn (Pharaoh), when he strikes the sea with it¹, and in his call to the Children of Israel, when he strikes the rock with it and water gushes from it².

The Qur'an treats this story in different snapshots. Sometimes it says of the staff that it was like a serpent (thu'ban), sometimes it says: ḥayya (a snake). And at other times it says: jann (a swift serpent). Therefore some have objected to these differences: which of them was the staff?

The truth is that these are different depictions of the staff when it turned into something else. From the aspect of its deadly strength it is a ḥayya; from the aspect of its bulk it is a thu'ban; and from the aspect of the lightness of its movement it is a jann. All these qualities were in the staff, and when you gather all these snapshots, they give you the complete picture of the staff after it had become a snake.

Thus the verses of the Qur'an complement one another to draw the intended image of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He.

¹ He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff, and it parted, and each part became like a huge mountain﴾ (ash-Shu'ara' 26:63).
² And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Musa asked water for his people, We said: Strike the rock with your staff, and there gushed forth from it twelve springs...﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:60).

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And draw your hand in to your side; it will come out white, without harm, as another sign﴾ [20:22].

The hand is well known, and the janah (wing) belongs to a bird; its counterpart in a human being is the forearm, beginning from the upper arm (ʿadud). When the Almighty enjoined us concerning parents, He said: ﴿And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy...﴾ [17:24], meaning: be humble toward them, and do not be arrogant over them.

In another place, the Exalted said: ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white, without harm...﴾ [28:32].

The jayb (bosom) is the neckline of the shirt. It was called jayb because in the past people would place the purse in which they kept money, or other things, inside the garment, so that it would be far from the hand of the thief. When a person needed something in his pocket, he would put his hand through the neckline of the shirt to reach the pocket, and so the neckline was named a jayb.

This is one of the manifestations of the coherence between the verses.

The meaning here: close the palm of your right hand and insert it through the neckline of your shirt to beneath your left upper arm, ﴿it will come out white, without harm﴾ [20:22]: that is, the moment your hand comes out, you will find it white, having light, luster, sheen and radiance.

It is known that Musa (peace be upon him) was dark-complexioned, as the Prophet (ﷺ) described him when he was asked to describe the messengers he met during the Night Journey and Ascension. He said: "As for Musa, he was a man of adam (dark-brown) complexion, tall, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah."

That is, very dark-complexioned and very tall, since ṭiwāl means taller than ṭawīl.

Hence the whiteness and radiance of the hand against the darkness of his complexion was a sign from the signs of God; had Musa been fair-skinned, the whiteness of his hand would not have appeared.

His saying ﴿without harm﴾ [20:22] means: without sickness, for whiteness on dark skin may be a disease, God forbid, such as leprosy, for example. So He negated that.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿as another sign﴾ [20:22] means: a miracle. But He said nothing about the first sign, which indicates that the staff was the first sign and the hand the other sign.

¹ Al-adama: darkness of complexion. Al-adam among people: one who is dark. Ibn al-Athir said: adama among people is intense darkness. It was also said: it derives from adamat al-ard, which is its color. He said: by it Adam, father of mankind, was named. (Lisan al-Arab, root ʾ-d-m)

² A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3394) and Muslim in his Sahih (165), Kitab al-Iman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Shanu'ah: a tribe of Yemen who are attributed to Shanu'ah, who was ʿAbd Allah ibn Kaʿb; his epithet Shanu'ah came from the enmity (shana' = hatred) that existed between him and his people. (Fath al-Bari 6/429)

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿That We may show you of Our greatest signs﴾ [20:23].

That is: We will show you the wondrous signs with Us, so that they may serve as a preface for you. When We command you to something of this kind, know that the One who commands you is a Lord who will never deceive you, will never forsake you, and will surely strengthen and support you. So do not be fearful, do not be anxious, and do not retreat.

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is preparing His Prophet Musa for an anticipated encounter with his enemy Fir'awn (Pharaoh), who claimed divinity.

Then, after this charge and practical experience, He says to him:

﴿Go to Pharaoh; indeed he has transgressed.﴾

Why did He send him to Pharaoh first, and not to his people? They said: Because Pharaoh had committed a monstrous act, claiming divinity, which is the summit of aggression, and then he enslaved the Children of Israel. So the situation must first be resolved with Pharaoh.

Accordingly, the miracle of the staff occurred in three situations:

The first: It was for Moses' training and drilling in this procedure. This time it was between Moses and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, as a training, so that when the time came to exercise it before Pharaoh, he would not be daunted by it or draw back, but would perform it with a steadfast and confident heart.

The second: It was with Pharaoh alone, as a means of terrifying him.

The third: It was with the magicians, as a means of gathering them together.

Each of these situations had a wisdom and a role, and there is no repetition in the matter, as some claim.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed he has transgressed (23)﴾ (Ta-Ha). Tughyan (transgression): exceeding the limit. Exceeding the limit occurs by taking what is not one's own and going to excess in that. Would that he had taken from his equals among the servants; rather, he took for himself what belongs to the attributes of God, Mighty and Majestic.

When Moses heard the name of Pharaoh, he recalled what had happened to him in Egypt, and that he had been raised in the house of this Pharaoh who claimed divinity, and how he would face him.

He also recalled the story of the man whom he struck and killed (1), and then he left it fearful and watchful. When Moses felt that the burden was heavy, he said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast (25)﴾.

(1) This is in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of unawareness of its people, and found therein two men fighting, one from his own faction and the other from his enemy. So the one from his faction called for his help against the one from his enemy, and Moses struck him and dispatched him...﴾ (al-Qasas) (15).

Es seems to be a request to translate; the passage is a tafsir commentary. I'll translate it faithfully.

It is as if he said: "O Lord, I will carry out Your commands; but I do not wish to undertake this task while my chest is constricted about it, because constriction of the breast toward a thing wastes energy and dissipates it, and it helps calamities gain access to the self."

Therefore Musa made this supplication: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:25], so that he might conserve his strength for carrying out this difficult task, which requires an effort commensurate with it. The meaning of that is that his breast was constricted at meeting Fir'awn, for the reasons that were mentioned.

Then he said: ﴿And ease for me my task﴾.

Because expanding the breast (sharh al-sadr) in this matter is not sufficient on its own. The expansion of the breast comes from the side of the agent, but the recipient may show fierce obstinacy and stubborn resistance. Therefore he said after it: ﴿And ease for me my task﴾ (Ta-Ha 26): that I may not encounter obstinacy and tyranny from Pharaoh. So the easing of the task comes from the side of the one receiving the action, after the expansion of the breast on the part of the agent.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 20, verse 27:

Because speech and the conveying of the message require eloquence (mantiq) and a tongue that flows freely with speech, and Musa (peace be upon him) had a speech impediment (ruttah) or a blockage (habsah) in his tongue, so that it did not flow in speech.

This speech impediment was also present in the tongue of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both). When the Prophet (ﷺ) would see al-Husayn laughing, he would say: "He inherited it from his uncle Musa."

And observe the precision of expression in His words: ﴿from my tongue﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:27). He did not say: "Untie the knot of my tongue." For that might be understood as defiance of Allah's decree in restricting his tongue. Rather, he does not object, and asks only for a portion of his tongue's ability, which enables him to carry out his task of conveying the message.

1 Al-ruttah: with a damma, hastiness in speech and lack of deliberation. It is said: it is changing the lam into a ya'. Al-art is one who has a knot and blockage in his tongue, so that his tongue does not obey him in speech. (Lisan al-'Arab, entry: r-t-t).

This is the reason for his request; were it not for it, he would not have asked for the loosening of the tongue, and "fiqh" is that they understand the speech and what is said about it.

Moses, peace be upon him, continues with what he sees as helping him to carry out his mission:

Wazeeran: that is, a helper and supporter.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wished to warn people about the Hereafter, He said: ﴿No! There is no refuge. To your Lord, on that Day, is the place of rest.﴾ (al-Qiyamah)

That is: there is no refuge and no helper to which one may flee except Allah. The wazir (vizier, minister) is named from (wazar), and a wazir is sought when the owner of a matter cannot carry it out alone, so he needs someone to help him in his affair. He is a true wazir if he is a sincere, trustworthy adviser who helps his companion honestly. But if he is a deceitful, base person who works for his own benefit, he is not a wazir at all; rather he is (wizr), a burden. From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.﴾ (Fatir)

In the noble Prophetic hadith: "The best of kings is a king for whom Allah has appointed a wazir: if he forgets, the wazir reminds him; if he intends good, even merely intends it, the wazir helps him; and if he wishes evil, the wazir restrains him..."

These are the marks of a sincere wazir for the subjects, as the policy of heaven has explained them, for every ruler has two inner circles: one that enjoins the good, and another that enjoins the evil, as the noble hadith has come.

If this is the policy of heaven, then what of the policy of men?

Anushirwan said: "Beware lest you understand that any of us can do without another. Each one has his task. If you excel in something, you are deficient in other things, which Allah has placed in others so that they may complete your deficiency. Livelihood is shared, but this sharing is imposed by necessity, not by favour. Otherwise, if others do not show you favour, what would you do?"

We have already given an example of people's need for one another. We said: What would happen if the sanitation workers or the street sweepers refrained from work for several days? But if the ministers were absent for several days, nothing would happen.

So: do not think that you are better than others, for each of them has a task he performs. If you are better than him in this, he is better than you in that, because the sum of each person's talents equals the sum of the others' talents. If you say: then why do differences exist among people?

They say: so that there may be a necessity for us to need one another. If all were equal, we would say to a group among us: "Be kind enough to sweep the streets on such a day," and they would not volunteer. But if need compels them to such work, they will hasten to it, as we now see in the most arduous professions and the hardest tasks that people shun and even despise: you see their practitioner coming to them eagerly, keen to perform them despite their hardship, and he even becomes angry if he does not find an opportunity to work. Why? Because it is the source of his strength and the sustenance of his dependents.

With this outlook, no one becomes arrogant or proud, and society achieves a balance of mutual reliance.

His saying: ﴿from my family﴾ (Ta-Ha 29): that is, so that he would be trusted by me.

This request from Musa, peace be upon him, points to a lofty etiquette of prophethood. Allah chose Musa for the message, so why would he associate his brother with this task? Musa does not wish to take pride in the message, or to be haughty with it, or to transgress; rather he wishes to carry it out in the most perfect manner. Therefore he seeks to complete his own deficiency through his brother, to help him convey his message. Had he wished to monopolise the message, he would not have made this request.

This is a model to be emulated. If you are charged with a task beyond your capacity, there is no fault in seeking help from others in it, for this is evidence of your sincerity toward the task you have been assigned.

1 On the authority of Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you is given a position of authority and Allah intends good for him, Allah appoints for him a righteous wazir: if he forgets, the wazir reminds him, and if he remembers, the wazir helps him." Recorded by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/159).

2 The wording of the hadith: "Allah never sent a prophet nor appointed a caliph except that he had two inner circles: an inner circle that enjoins him to good and urges him to it, and an inner circle that enjoins him to evil and urges him to it. Whoever is protected is the one Allah protects." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7198), and similarly Ahmad in his Musnad (3/39), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 30:

So he chose his brother Harun to assist him in the mission of the message.

Then he clarified the reason for that, saying in another verse: ﴿And my brother Harun is more eloquent in tongue than I﴾ (al-Qasas: 34):

Thus Musa and Harun complete one another, and each of them compensates for the deficiency in his brother. It is said that Harun, peace be upon him, excelled Musa in other matters: he had gentleness and forbearance, whereas Musa was hot-tempered and quick to anger. So Harun was for gentleness, and Musa was for severity.

This becomes clear when Musa returned to his people, having left them in the company of his brother Harun, and they had worshipped the calf, so his anger intensified, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾ (al-A'raf: 150):

Then he grew furious with his brother, seized him by his beard, and his harshness and severity became apparent. So what did Harun say? ﴿He said, "Son of my mother..."﴾ (al-A'raf: 150), seeking to soften him and remind him of a mother's tenderness and compassion: ﴿Do not seize my beard nor my head﴾ (Ta-Ha: 94), as if he were saying to his brother: strike me as you wish, but do not terrify me by seizing my beard and my head.

Therefore: the eloquence of Harun remedies the knot in the tongue of Musa, and gentleness remedies severity and hot temper. Also, Musa, peace be upon him, was dark-complexioned, curly-haired, with an aquiline(1) nose, whereas Harun was fair-complexioned, straight-haired, handsome in features and appearance, pleasing to the eye, so whoever was not drawn to Musa was drawn to Harun.

The Prophet (ﷺ) loved that revelation would descend upon him in the form of Dihya(2) al-Kalbi, and he, may Allah be pleased with him, was handsome, pleasing to behold, so Jibril, peace be upon him, would descend to him in that form to comfort him.

And Musa, peace be upon him, despite his brother Harun being distinguished by these qualities over him, did not harbor resentment toward his brother, nor did he regard him as superior to himself. Rather, he made his brother's qualities complementary to his own, all for the sake of carrying out the message and conveying it in its most perfect manner. He did not look to himself and his own success, but to the success of the mission which Allah had assigned to him.

This disposition ought to spread among people. If you see a good quality in another, or an aspect of perfection in another, then praise Allah for it, and know that its benefit will return to you, and it will compensate for what you lack. So do not harbor resentment toward him, for he will bear your shortcomings, and you will benefit from his goodness.

1. Aqna al-anf (qanaa): the middle of the bridge of the nose rose and its nostrils narrowed; he is aqna, and she is qanwa'. (al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, entry: qana)
2. A well-known Companion, whose first major engagement was the Trench. He was proverbial for beauty of form, and Jibril would descend in his likeness. He witnessed Yarmouk, settled in Damascus and lived in al-Mezzeh, and lived until the caliphate of Mu'awiya. (al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba by Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, 2/162)

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says that Musa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Strengthen my back through him﴾ (20:31).

Al-azr means strength. It is as though Musa, peace be upon him, knew that carrying the message to Pharaoh and to his people after him was a laborious undertaking, so he said to God: give me my brother to help me bear this hardship.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 32:

His saying: ﴿And make him a partner in my task﴾. That is, You, O Lord. It is not I who make him a partner, as a favour from me to him. Musa, peace be upon him, wanted the favour to come from God, and the charge (taklif) to come from God as well, so that Harun would not object or grow impatient when engaging in the call (da'wah).

For this reason, when they went to Pharaoh, they said: ﴿Indeed, we are two messengers of your Lord...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:47). Musa did not say, "Harun is a follower of mine," but rather he is exactly like him, a messenger sent by God. When Musa spoke, he spoke on behalf of himself and Harun.

Then when Musa invoked (against) his people: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ (Yunus 10:88).

The answer came from God: ﴿He said, "Your prayer has been answered, so go straight"...﴾ (Yunus 10:89), because the supplication came from Musa while Harun said "Amin" to it, and the one who says amen is one of the two who supplicate.

1 Tams (طمس) of a thing: its form changed or its trace effaced. The meaning of the verse: that is, send down upon it what would erase it and destroy it. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/406).

Then the Exalted Lord says, concerning Harun and Musa, that they said: ﴿That we may glorify You much, and remember You much.﴾ (20:33–34)

This is the reason for Harun's sharing with his brother in his mission: not seeking rest for himself, but so that their efforts combine in obedience to Allah, in glorifying Him and remembering Him.

Tasbih (glorification; declaring Allah free of imperfection): sanctifying Allah and declaring Him far above any deficiency, in His essence, His attributes and His actions. In essence, there is nothing like His essence: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ (42:11). Nor is there anything like Him in His attributes or in His actions. So do not say that Allah's hearing is like yours, or that His sight is like yours, or that His action is like your action.

The meaning is: "We glorify You and sanctify You with a sanctification that raises You to the level of the divinity that belongs to You, and we add nothing of our own."

His saying ﴿We glorify You much﴾ (20:33) means constantly. Glorification brings a pleasure into the one who glorifies, just as the obedience of the obedient brings a pleasure into his own self. The Prophet ﷺ said: "...and the coolness of my eyes has been made to be in prayer" (1).

The Prophet ﷺ used to turn to prayer whenever a matter distressed him (2).

1 Related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/128, 199, 285), al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/61), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/160), who said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not narrate it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik. The complete hadith: "Beloved to me of your world are women and perfume..." and so on.

2 From Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet ﷺ, whenever a matter distressed him, would pray." Related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (5/388) and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1319).

The passage repeats the text because it shares its subject with verse 33: Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says of Harun and Musa that they said: ﴿That we may glorify You much, and remember You much﴾ (33–34).

This is the reason for Harun's joining his brother in his mission, not seeking relief for himself, but so that their efforts would combine in obedience to God, in glorifying Him and remembering Him.

Tasbih (glorification, the affirmation of God's transcendence and sanctity, His being free of any imperfection) means sanctifying God and declaring Him free of all deficiency in His essence, attributes and actions. In essence: there is nothing like His Essence, as in ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (al-Shura 42:11). Nor is He like anything in His essence, His attributes or His actions. So do not say that God's hearing is like yours, or that His sight is like yours, or that His action is like your action.

The meaning is: We glorify You and sanctify You with a sanctification that raises You to the level of divinity that belongs to You, and we add nothing of our own to it.

As for His saying ﴿We glorify You much﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:33), it means constantly. The glorification thus produces a pleasure within the one who glorifies, just as the obedience of the obedient produces a pleasure within him, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "...and the coolness of my eye has been made to be in prayer."¹

The Prophet (ﷺ) would, whenever a matter distressed him, turn to prayer.²

¹ Recorded by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/128, 199, 285), al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/61), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/160), who said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik. The complete hadith: "Beloved to me of this world are women and perfume..." and the hadith continues.

² From Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) would, whenever a matter distressed him, pray." Recorded by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (5/388) and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1319).

Then you are the Guardian over us, watching over our actions. Will we perform them in the most perfect manner, or will we fall short in them?

Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿He said: "You have been granted your request, O Moses."﴾ (36)

Sa'l (su'l): that which is asked for, like "khubz" meaning "makhbuz" (baked bread). The meaning is: We have given you what you asked for, and indeed We gave you before you asked, and even before you knew how to ask.

(مننا) From the root *minnah* (a favour bestowed without return, as opposed to *jaza'*, a reward given in exchange for deeds): it is a gift given without any compensation, whereas *jaza'* is a gift given in return for work. ﴿And We bestowed a favour upon you another time﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:37). *Idhan* (إذن, "then, in that case"): this implies that there was a first time. However, the favour meant here is what happened through the revelation to the mother of Musa when he was an infant, so that was in reality the first favour. The phrase here, ﴿another time﴾, is an ordering of remembrance according to the sequence of the events.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 20, verse 38:

Then when was this favour?

"Idh" (when): meaning, at the time when We revealed to your mother what is revealed. This was the first favour upon you, when you were born in a year in which Pharaoh was killing the male children, so We showed you grace when We said to your mother: ﴿So when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear nor grieve; We will surely return him to you and make him one of the messengers.﴾ (al-Qasas)

And the meaning of ﴿what is revealed﴾ (Ta-Ha): that is, a great matter which you cannot fully comprehend, so that your soul would go off in every direction (in thought about it), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then there covered them of the river that which covered them.﴾ (Ta-Ha)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 39:

The Truthful, glorified is He, details this revelation to the mother of Musa, so He says, exalted is He: ﴿Throw him into the chest, then throw it into the river, and the river will cast it onto the bank, and an enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take him. And I cast upon you love from Me, and so that you may be raised under My eye﴾.

This is what We revealed to the mother of Musa.

Al-yamm (the river): the great body of water, whether salt or sweet. When the Truthful, glorified is He, spoke of Fir'awn, He said: ﴿So We drowned them in the yamm...﴾ (al-A'raf 7:136). The intended meaning there is the Red Sea. As for Musa, he was born in Egypt and his chest was thrown into the Nile, and Fir'awn's palace was on the Nile.

And by Allah... that is, what mother is this who would believe this statement: "If you fear for your child, then throw him into the yamm"? And how could she save him from a presumed destruction by casting him into a certain destruction?

Yet the mother of Musa did not hesitate for a moment in carrying out the command of Allah, and she did not retract. This is the difference between an inspiration from the Most Merciful and an inspiration from Satan. The inspiration of the Most Merciful: the soul finds no way to reject it, but receives it as an established matter. The inspiration of Satan does not dare to contest the inspiration of the Most Merciful. So the mother took the infant and threw him as her Lord had inspired her.

You notice in these verses that the verse of al-Qasas does not mention anything about the matter of the chest: ﴿So when you fear for him, then throw him into the yamm...﴾ (al-Qasas 28:7), just like that, directly.

They said: because the Truthful, glorified is He, spoke of the goal that causes fear, which is throwing into the yamm, and it is natural in a mother's tenderness that she devise for her child and work for his rescue, so she makes for him such a chest, and prepares it appropriately for floating on the surface of the water.

So the speech here is for the preparation and readying of the mother before the event, and there is a difference between address for preparation before the event and address at the time of the event. The motherhood would have an arrangement and means that help in salvation, so she made for him a box in which she placed a soft cradle and took precautions for the matter. Then the Truthful, glorified is He, reassures her about her child: ﴿And do not fear and do not grieve...﴾ (al-Qasas 28:7), so We will save him, because he has a mission with Me: ﴿We will return him to you and make him among the messengers﴾ (al-Qasas 28:7).

When the time of execution came, the command came in quick, successive phrases: ﴿That throw him into the chest, then throw it into the yamm, and the yamm will cast him onto the bank...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39).

Therefore, you find the context in the first verse calm and steady, suited to the stage of preparation, while in the execution the context came swift and successive, suited to the speed of execution. It is as if the Truthful, glorified is He, inspired to her: "Hasten to the matter that I had previously inspired to you." This is the final turn of this issue.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿will take him to the bank...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39), meaning: the waves will carry him and move him along, as if they had orders to enter him into the channel that leads to Fir'awn's palace.

So we have, then, three castings for Musa: the casting of mercy and tenderness into the chest, the casting of the chest into the yamm in execution of Allah's command, and the casting of the yamm of the chest at Fir'awn's palace.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿an enemy to Me and an enemy to him...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39): "an enemy to Me" means to Allah, exalted is He, because Fir'awn claimed divinity; "and an enemy to him" means to Musa, because he would stand against him and bring him to his limit.

In the verse there is an indication of the execution of His will, glorified is He. When He wills a thing, He decrees it, even through the hands of His enemies while they are heedless. Who could imagine or believe that Fir'awn, in his tyranny, arrogance, and slaughter of the male children of the Children of Israel, would be the one who takes Musa to himself, cares for him in his house, loves him, and finds acceptance in his soul?

Did Fir'awn pick him up at the beginning so that he would become an enemy to him, or did he pick him up so that he would become a son? As his wife Asiya said: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son, while they do not perceive﴾ (al-Qasas 28:9).

So: there was love, but it later led to enmity. It led to Musa becoming the enemy whom you raise yourself and protect so that the overthrow of your kingdom would be at his hands. Therefore Fir'awn will say: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?﴾ (al-Shu'ara' 26:18).

This matter of enmity was exploited by the skeptics regarding the Qur'an, who accused it of repetition in His saying: ﴿an enemy to Me and an enemy to him...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39). Then He said in another verse: ﴿So the family of Fir'awn picked him up so that he would become for them an enemy and a grief...﴾ (al-Qasas 28:8).

The one who reflects on the two verses finds that the enmity in the first verse is from the side of Fir'awn toward Musa and his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, while the enmity in the second verse is from the side of Musa toward Fir'awn. Thus the enmity is reciprocal, and this guarantees its fierceness and continuation, and this is the intent in this story.

If the enmity were from one side only, perhaps the other would forgive, and the enemy would be ashamed, and reconciliation would occur. The enmity between Musa and Fir'awn must be fierce, because it is an enmity over the summit issue, which is monotheism (tawhid).

But why did Musa's arrival in this state not draw Fir'awn's attention, so that he would ask about his story and investigate his matter? It is the will of Allah, which nothing can frustrate. So Fir'awn's wife loves him and says: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you...﴾ (al-Qasas 28:9). Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, says after it: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39):

So Asiya, the wife of Fir'awn, loved him when she saw him, and Fir'awn loved him when he saw him. This is love from Allah without a cause for love, because love among people has causes: you love a person because you feel affection for him, or because he is a relative or a friend, or because he did you a favor. Love may come from Allah without any of these causes, having no cause but the will of Allah.

So the meaning of ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39) is: there was nothing in you that necessitated love, and you did not have its causes, especially as Musa, peace be upon him, was dark-complexioned, curly-haired, hook-nosed, and "akhtaf" (having a narrow, pinched shoulder structure). It is as if this constitution came as a preparation for this love, and as an affirmation of the will of Allah, which subdued Fir'awn to love Musa, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a person and his heart...﴾ (al-Anfal 8:24).

Thus Allah turned the heart of Fir'awn and placed in it love for Musa, to pass this matter through this great fool, so that he would take his enemy and raise him in his house. Musa did not possess the handsomeness and beauty that draw hearts.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and so that you may be raised under My eye﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39), meaning: you would be raised under the eye of Allah and in His care. Although the reality is that he was raised in Fir'awn's house, the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, cares for him; if he encountered anything in his upbringing, his Lord, mighty and majestic, intervened to teach him and raise him.

Among these situations: Fir'awn was sitting with his wife Asiya, and with them young Musa was playing. Suddenly he grabbed Fir'awn's beard and pulled it hard, which angered him, so he ordered his killing. His wife intervened, saying: "He is still a child who does not understand anything; he does not know the date from the ember."

So they brought him a date and an ember to test him. Allah turned his hand away from the date toward the ember, to thwart the matter for this great fool. Moreover, Musa took it despite its heat until he put it in his mouth, so it burned his tongue, and this caused the knot in his tongue of which he complained later.

It is as if the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, reassures His Prophet Musa, peace be upon him: Do not fear; you are under My eye and in My care. If they do anything to you, I will intervene. In another verse He said: ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:41).

So I watch over you and protect you, because you have a mission with Me.

1 al-Tabut: the chest in which goods are kept. (Lisan al-'Arab, root: tbt) al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4368): (Muqatil said: the believer of Fir'awn's family is the one who made the chest and carpentered it, and his name was Hizqil, and the chest was of sycamore wood).
2 al-Sana' (fashioning): its meaning is creating and producing, and it occurs with intention, will, and planning. His saying, exalted is He, in the story of Musa: ﴿and so that you may be raised under My eye﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:39), meaning: you would be raised guarded by My care. And His saying: ﴿and I have chosen you for Myself﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:41), meaning: I taught you, raised you, and bestowed My favor upon you so that you would be My creation serving Me and carrying out the message I assign to you and have chosen you for. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/284).
3 That is: a source of joy for Me and for you. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/112). It was said: "May Allah cool your eye" means: may He bring you your wish so that your soul is satisfied and your eye is at rest, not looking toward anything else. (Lisan al-'Arab, root: qarr).
4 al-Katf: a defect in the shoulder, which is a separation in the upper part of a person's shoulder; al-akhtaf is one whose two shoulders are pressed together over the middle of his chest, which is ugly. (Lisan al-'Arab, root: katf).
5 Ibn 'Abbas said: He comes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak as a mawquf report and said: it is sahih, though they did not record it. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2/298): (Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, 'Ata', and others).

Then the Truthful, Exalted One says: ﴿When your sister walked and said, "Shall I direct you to someone who will take charge of him?" So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve. And you killed a soul, but We delivered you from distress and tested you with a trial. So you remained for years among the people of Madyan. Then you came here by decree, O Moses.﴾

So, Moses' sister had a role in his story, as God Almighty said in another place: ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him," so she watched him from afar while they did not perceive.﴾ (al-Qasas: 11)

The meaning is: she followed him after she knew he had been saved from the river, and she learned that he was in Pharaoh's house. Then God forbade him the wet-nurses, so he rejected the nursing women. Here his sister intervened to say: ﴿Shall I direct you to someone who will take charge of him...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40). This arrangement is something only God could bring about.

As for His saying: ﴿So We returned you to your mother...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40), when we survey the root (r-j-ʿ) in the Qur'an, we find it comes once intransitive, as in: ﴿And when Moses returned to his people...﴾ (al-A'raf: 150).

And it comes transitive, as in: ﴿So We returned you to your mother...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40), and in: ﴿So if God returns you to a group of them...﴾ (al-Tawbah: 83).

The difference between the intransitive and the transitive is that the intransitive "rajaʿa" means he returned by himself, while the transitive means someone else caused him to return. Return (rujūʿ) means that you go back to a state you were in and left; if you return by yourself, without motives compelling you to return, the verb is intransitive; if there were matters that pushed you to return, the verb is transitive.

Similar to this: "rajaʿaka" versus "arjaʿaka": "rajaʿaka" is the return that, on the surface, comes from you without motives from you; "arjaʿaka" means against your will.

As for His saying: ﴿that her eye might be comforted...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40): "taqarru al-ʿayn" means it becomes settled, because aspirations are either moral or sensory, and a person has hopes he strives to achieve; when they are achieved, we say: he no longer longs for anything.

Likewise with the sensory: the Arabs say of a beautiful thing: "qayyidu al-nawāẓir" (it binds the gazes), meaning it holds the eye so that it does not turn away, because a person does not turn from the beautiful unless he sees what is more beautiful. This is what they call "qurrat al-ʿayn" (the coolness of the eye): the good thing in which the eye settles, and does not seek any increase in beauty.

Then He says: ﴿And you killed a soul, but We delivered you from distress and tested you with a trial...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40): This is another favour of God Almighty upon Moses, peace be upon him. God's favours upon him are many, as He said: ﴿And We had already bestowed upon you another favour at another time﴾ (Ta-Ha: 37). So it was one time, but there were other times.

This matter of killing appears in His saying: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of unawareness of its people and found therein two men fighting, one of his own faction and the other of his enemy. The one of his faction called him for help against the one of his enemy, so Moses struck him and killed him...﴾ (al-Qasas: 15).

He left the city fearful, watching for people lest they pursue him and kill him. This is the meaning of: ﴿We delivered you from distress...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40), i.e., from being killed or from being seized. ﴿And We tested you with a trial...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40), i.e., We exposed you to many tribulations, then delivered you from them. The first of them: you were born in a year in which infants were killed; then your mother cast you into the river; then what happened with Pharaoh when you pulled at his beard.

Then He says: ﴿So you remained for years among the people of Madyan...﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40): God mentioned the period of his stay among the people of Madyan as one of His favours upon Moses, even though he was a hired worker there, and he said of himself: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾ (al-Qasas: 24).

In Madyan he became acquainted with Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, married his daughter, and had a son by her. Moses, in all of this, was a stranger to his homeland, far from his mother. When God willed him prophethood, He stirred in him longing for his homeland and to see his mother, and decreed his return. So He said: ﴿Then you came here by decree, O Moses﴾ (Ta-Ha: 40).

That is: according to a measure of Your choosing. God's decree is what moved in your heart the longing to return, and led you to walk the uninhabited road and bear the hardship of cold and the toil of travel. It was God's decree that stirred within you the thought of longing for your mother; so on the road back, and at Tuwa, you were on an appointment with election and prophethood.

Therefore, the poet who praised the caliph said to him:
*"He came to the caliphate, or it was for him a decree, / just as his Lord came to Moses by decree."*

¹ al-Qass: following the track. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/381): i.e., (follow his trace, take his news, and seek out his affairs in the regions of the city).

² Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Suddi that Pharaoh mounted a conveyance without Moses being with him; when Moses came, it was said to him: Pharaoh has mounted, so he mounted in pursuit. The midday rest (al-maqil, the time of noon heat) overtook him in a land called Memphis; he entered it at midday, when its markets were closed and there was no one in its roads, and it is the city of which God says: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of unawareness of its people...﴾ (al-Qasas: 15). (Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/397).

³ It is the city of Memphis, which now lies about 28 km south of Cairo, near Mit Rahina in Badrashin, Giza, and has the pyramids of Saqqara. Memphis was the first city in Egypt until the city of Alexandria was built; Memphis was a strong fortress, where weapons of war were manufactured and fleet vessels were built. (Dictionary of Ancient Egyptian Civilization – by George Posener and others – translated by Amin Salama – Egyptian General Book Authority).

⁴ Qatadah said: he stayed ten years. Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/579), attributed to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Wahb said: I stayed with Shuʿayb for twenty-eight years, of which ten were the bridal payment for his wife Safurah, daughter of Shuʿayb, and eighteen he spent with him until a child was born to him there.

⁵ Mujahid said: i.e., at an appointment. Qatadah said: according to the measure of the message and prophethood. Both cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/153).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says to Moses: ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾.

That is, I delivered you and protected you, because I am preparing you for a task with Me: to send you as a messenger with My method to Pharaoh and to your people.

The scholars tried to count the requests that Moses, peace be upon him, made of his Lord, and found them to be eight: ﴿He said, "My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech, and appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother, increase through him my strength, and let him share my task, that we may glorify You much and remember You much"﴾ (Ta-Ha).

Then they found that Allah, the Exalted, gave him eight more without his asking: ﴿When We inspired to your mother what is inspired: Put him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw him onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his. And I cast upon you love from Me, and that you be raised under My eye. When your sister walks and says, "Shall I direct you to one who will nurse him?" So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and not grieve. And you killed a soul, but We saved you from distress and tried you with a trial, and you remained years among the people of Madyan; then you came upon a decree, O Moses﴾ (Ta-Ha).

So if Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord for eight things, his Lord, mighty and majestic, gave him eight others without his asking, so that He combined for him giving in response to a request and giving out of generosity without a request. This is because if you ask Allah and He gives you, that shows His power to answer your request; but if He gives you without your asking, that shows His love for you.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in remembering Me.﴾(1)

﴿With My signs...﴾ (Ta-Ha 42): Here "the signs" means the dazzling miracles that will overwhelm Pharaoh. You will not go empty-handed. Rather, you will go with proof of the truth of the message you are bringing to him. ﴿Do not slacken in remembering Me﴾ (Ta-Ha 42): al-tawani (slackness) means lethargy or shortcoming. "I have equipped you both with the appropriate preparation for this arduous task, so beware of being lax about it. If any shortcoming arises from you both, it is a shortcoming in performance, not in preparation."

The meaning of ﴿in remembering Me﴾ (Ta-Ha 42) is: "Let Me always be in your minds. I am the One who sent you, I am the One who strengthened you with miracles, I am the One who watches over you and keeps you in view, and I am the One who will reward you. So let this never be absent from you."

1. In the qira'ah (recitation variant) of Ibn Mas'ud: (wa-la tahina fi dhikri), and (in) My praise, My glorification and the conveyance of My message. (al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 6/4371).

Then the Truthful Lord says: ﴿Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.﴾

Is there any transgression greater than his claim to be a lord? And He, exalted, has said in another place: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh was haughty in the land, and indeed he was among the extravagant.﴾ [Yunus 10:83]. The musrif (extravagant, one who exceeds limits) is the one who goes beyond the bounds. He exceeded in his extravagance and claimed divinity, so he acted haughtily in the land, the haughtiness of a tyrant from among mankind over other humans who were oppressed.

This is Pharaoh's situation after he has transgressed. Who passed judgment on him as a transgressor? When you, a human being, pass judgment on him as a transgressor, it is a transgression proportionate to human capacities and abilities. But when the Blessed and Exalted Truth says of him: ﴿Indeed, he has transgressed﴾ (Ta-Ha 43), then he must have exceeded all limits and reached the peak of transgression, for it is our Lord who says it.

As for His saying: ﴿So speak to him gently, perhaps he may be reminded or fear﴾ (Ta-Ha 44): you must give him room to see your proofs and signs, and you must not confront him with harshness and severity. They have said: advice is heavy, so do not send it as a mountain upon him, and do not make him into a contender; and do not combine two hardships upon the one being advised: that you remove him from what he is accustomed to by means of what he dislikes. Rather, remove him from what he is accustomed to by means of what he loves.

This is a method of da'wah (calling to Islam) that is clear and established, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction﴾ (al-Nahl 125).

Because you are pulling him away from what he has become used to and accustomed to, and from what he loves of freedom and indulgence in desires and pleasures; then you bind him to the method. So let that be done with gentleness and kindness.

This is a policy that people now use in the field of medicine: after medicine was bitter, which the sick loathed, they have now arrived at coating the bitter medicine and encasing it in a sweet-tasting layer so that the process of swallowing is completed, and the medicine passes the zone of taste.

Likewise is the case with the bitterness of truth and advice: you must coat it with gentle, kind speech.

As for His saying: ﴿Perhaps he may be reminded or fear﴾ (Ta-Ha 44): "La'alla" (perhaps): an expression of hope. So how does the Blessed and Exalted Truth say ﴿Perhaps he may be reminded or fear﴾ (Ta-Ha 44) when He knows that he will not be reminded nor will he fear, and that he will die a disbelieving drowned one?

They said: because the Truth, glorified is He, wants Moses to enter upon Pharaoh as one confident that he will be guided, not as one despairing of his guidance, so that he will have the sufficient energy to debate with him and present proofs to him. But if he entered while knowing this outcome, he would be disheartened, seeing no benefit in his words, as they say: "They struck the one-eyed man in his eye, and he said: a loss, a loss."

So the Truth, glorified is He, knows what will be the matter of Pharaoh, but He wants to establish the proof against him: ﴿So that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾ (al-Nisa' 165).

As for His saying: ﴿may be reminded or fear﴾ (Ta-Ha 44): it is as if a human being, when he abandons the harshness of his thinking and the shroud of his desires within himself, must be guided by his nature to the existence of God, or be "reminded" of the realm of atoms (alam al-dharr) and the covenant that God took from him on the day He said: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we bear witness﴾ (al-A'raf 172).

And the one of whom the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah (natural disposition); then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian(1)."(2)

So if a person reflects and strips himself of his desires, he must be guided to the existence of God. But the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, made room for heedlessness, and sent the messengers to remind; therefore He said: ﴿messengers bearing good news and warning﴾ (al-Nisa' 165), and did not say: "initiating."

As for the matter of belief in God, it should have been clear and known to people: that there is faith in a Creator God, Capable, and that they only await what He demands of them and what He commands them to worship. What should you do? And what should you leave? This is the task of the messengers.

We have already given an example of a man whose ways were cut off in a vast desert, finding no water or food, until he approached destruction; then sleep overcame him and he slept, and when he awoke, behold, a table with varieties of food and drink. By God, before he extends his hand to the food, would he not ask: who brought it to him?

Likewise is the human being: he arrived in a cosmos prepared to receive him: earth, sky, sun, moon, crops, waters, and air. Is it not fitting for him to ask: who created this wondrous universe? If you reflected on the good that came upon you in this world, you would arrive at faith.

So the meaning of ﴿may be reminded﴾ (Ta-Ha 44): that is, of the past blessings, so he believes in the Bestower; ﴿or fear﴾ (Ta-Ha 44): fears the coming punishment, so he believes in God, to whom affairs return in the Hereafter.

1 Majusiyya (Magianism) is a creed that holds to two principles, light and darkness; they claim that good is from the action of light and evil is from the action of darkness. It is said: "tamajjasa al-rajul" and "tamajjasu": they became Magians; and "majjasu awladahum": they made their children so. (Lisan al-Arab – root: m-j-s).
2 A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4775), and Muslim in his Sahih (2658), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.
3 Al-sahra' al-dawiyya: when its edges are far and it is level and wide. (Lisan al-Arab – root: d-w-y).

Then the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted says of the two of them: ﴿They said, "Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us or that he will transgress."﴾

Al-khawf (fear): a feeling within the soul that stirs reverence toward something. And what do the two fear? ﴿That he will hasten against us...﴾ (Ta-Ha 45). Yafruta (to hasten/exceed): meaning he goes beyond the limit. Its opposite is farrata (to fall short), meaning he neglects the matter. Hence they say: moderation is a virtue between excess (ifrat) and deficiency (tafrit).

From ifrat comes the saying: "a fars fari" (a horse that is fari') when it outruns others on the racecourse.

They also say: "he won the qasab of the race" (hāza qasab al-sabq). At the end of the racecourse they used to set up a reed (qasaba) fixed in the ground, and the rider who first reached and seized it was the winner. The horse being fari' means that it has exceeded the limit set for it, not merely that it has outrun another.

Therefore, when the Qur'an speaks of limits, it says once: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them...﴾ (al-Baqarah 229), that is: beware of overstepping the limit set for you. And another time it says: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them...﴾ (al-Baqarah 187).

Regarding what is permitted, He said: ﴿so do not transgress them﴾ (al-Baqarah 229), meaning halt at the limit and do not go beyond it. Regarding what is forbidden, He said: ﴿so do not approach them﴾ (al-Baqarah 187), because if you draw near to them you will fall into them.

So the meaning of ﴿he will hasten against us﴾ (Ta-Ha 45) is: he exceeds the limit, and perhaps he will hurry to kill us before we can say anything, so that his killing of us precedes our speech to him.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or that he will transgress﴾ (Ta-Ha 45): he will not be content with killing us, but will also plunge into the right of our Lord, or say something unbecoming, as he had previously claimed divinity.

It is a duty of those who call to others to not reach the point of plunging into the right of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with those they call. Therefore, Allah, Glorified is He, disciplines the believers in Him with the manners of da'wah in confronting these people, saying: ﴿And do not revile those who call upon other than Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge...﴾ (al-An'am 108).

(1) 'Adā 'alayhi ya'du 'adwan wa 'udwānan: he wronged him and attacked him, like i'tada 'alayhi. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/11). Ibn 'Abbas said regarding this verse: ("They (the polytheists) said: O Muhammad, either you desist from reviling our gods, or we will revile your Lord. So Allah forbade them from reviling their idols.") (cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 2/164).

Then the Truthful, the Exalted, says: ﴿He said: "Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing."﴾ [20:46]

That is, "I will not abandon you nor leave you alone. I am with you, hearing and seeing, because movement is either speech, which is heard, or action, which is seen. So be reassured, for We will protect you." And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they would be the ones who overcome.﴾ [37:171-173]

This is one of the sunan (divine laws) of Allah the Exalted. If you see some soldiers attributed to Allah the Exalted being defeated, know that they have loosened their commitment to being Allah's soldiers; otherwise, Allah's promise to His soldiers can never be broken.

The evidence for this is what happened to the Muslims at Uhud. It is true that the Muslims were defeated in that battle, because they deviated from the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and disobeyed him when he said to the archers: "Do not leave your positions under any circumstances,"(1) but as soon as they saw the first signs of victory, they left their positions and descended to collect the spoils, so Khalid ibn al-Walid came around behind them and inflicted defeat upon them. Even if the Muslims were defeated, Islam was victorious, for when they disobeyed the orders of their Messenger, they were defeated. By Allah, if they had won while disobeying, would any command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) have stood firm afterward?

In the verse before us, the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, reassures them so that they do not fear. The power of Allah will protect them, and He will intervene if the matter requires it, as He intervened in the matter of the date and the ember, when he (Moses) was a small child in the house of Pharaoh.

(1) Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/209) within a long hadith about the battle of Uhud, from the narration of Musa ibn Uqbah, and in it: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed fifty men from the archers and placed them near the enemy's cavalry, and appointed over them 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr, brother of Khawwat ibn Jubayr, and said to them: 'O archers, when we take our positions in the battle, if you see the enemy's cavalry move and the enemies of Allah retreat, do not leave your positions. I charge you that none of you should leave his place, and protect us from the cavalry.' He gave the order to him and he conveyed it. And from their direction came the attack that befell the Prophet (ﷺ) that day and what afflicted him."

Then the Exalted Lord says to them both: ﴿So go to him and say, "We are two messengers of your Lord. So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace be upon him who follows guidance."﴾

We note here that they did not confront him with his claim to divinity all at once. Rather, they pointed to the station of lordship: ﴿messengers of your Lord..﴾ (20:47). This is a powerful shock that shakes Pharaoh. Then they moved on to another matter, namely the case of the Children of Israel, whom Pharaoh had been subjugating to his service, torturing them and oppressing them.

﴿So send with us the Children of Israel..﴾ (20:47): we have come to take our people and rescue them from this torment. ﴿We have come to you with a sign..﴾ (20:47): that is, a miracle. ﴿from your Lord..﴾ (20:47): so they repeated this phrase to him once more.

The Exalted Lord had taught them how to enter upon Pharaoh and how to speak with him about a matter that does not touch his arrogance and his divinity.

The Children of Israel are the remnant of Joseph, peace be upon him, and his brothers, when they came to Egypt in the days of the Aziz (1) who brought Joseph near and placed him over the treasuries of the land, as the Exalted said in the story of Joseph: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will take him exclusively for myself." So when he spoke with him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established and trusted in our presence (2)." He said, "Put me in charge of the storehouses of the land; indeed, I am a knowing guardian."﴾ (12:54–55).

As for His saying: ﴿And peace be upon him who follows guidance (20:47): this is not a greeting, because a greeting is given to one who is following guidance, and one prays for him with peace; if he is not like that, then it is the end of the speech.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to write it in his letters to al-Muqawqis, the great of the Copts, and to Heraclius, the great of the Romans, saying: "Submit and you will be safe; Allah will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the Aryisiyyin (3). And peace be upon him who follows guidance" (4).

(1) al-Aziz: the ruler of Egypt in the time of Joseph, and its minister. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: his name was Utfayr ibn Ruwaybih, and he was over the treasuries of Egypt. The king at that time was al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid, a man of the Amalekites (i.e., the Hyksos). (Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir, 2/473).
(2) i.e., great in our sight, firmly established in rank. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/232).
(3) Scholars differ concerning the meaning of al-Aryisiyyin, with several opinions; the soundest and most well-known is that they are the peasants and farmers, and the meaning is: upon you is the sin of your subjects who follow you and submit by your submission. This is the correct view, as explained by al-Nawawi in his commentary on Sahih Muslim.
(4) A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). It was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (hadith 7), Kitab Bad' al-Wahy, and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (1773), Kitab al-Jihad wal-Siyar, in a long hadith from Ibn Abbas concerning the mention of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) letter to Heraclius, the great of the Romans.

Musa and Harun said to Pharaoh: ﴿Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is for whoever denies and turns away.﴾

So here he gave him the final matter: it came to us in revelation that whoever denies and turns away will have punishment. And the meaning of ﴿it has been revealed to us﴾ (Ta-Ha) is: from your Lord.

When Pharaoh heard this statement, he wanted to enter with them into labyrinths that would occupy them, and prolong the argument so that he could arrange his thoughts and see what he would say:

﴿He said: "Who, then, is the Lord of you both, O Musa?"﴾

The address was directed to the original leader in this mission, who is Musa (peace be upon him).

(1) It may be that Pharaoh had objected to Musa's speech because he knew that Musa was not eloquent of tongue and that his speech was barely understood, owing to the impediment in his tongue. For this reason he said: ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ (Surah az-Zukhruf).

Meaning of "Who gave everything its creation and then guided [it]" (Ta-Ha 20:50): that is, everything that exists was created by God for a task, and its creation came suited to the task for which it was created. "Then guided [it]": that is, He indicated to everything how to carry out its task and made it easy for it.

God, glory be to Him, "gave everything its creation." The word "creation" (khalq) is used to mean the created thing, and the created thing is something that must have matter; it must have a form and shape, a color and a smell, and components with which to perform its task.

When God, glory be to Him, wills to create a thing, He decrees for it all of these things: He supplies the eye so that it can see, the nose so that it can smell, the tongue so that it can taste, and then He guides every thing to the matter intended by it for the completion of its task, without any intervention in that from anyone.

Consider that man, who is himself a creature subject to the Supreme Creator, can make, for example, a time bomb and set it to a time, so that it performs its task afterward automatically without the maker being connected to it.

God, the Exalted, created everything and empowered it to perform its task in the most perfect manner, by automatic, instinctive performance. The animals that we accuse of stupidity, and call "beasts" (bahaim), are in reality not so. God, may He be exalted, has given us an example of this in the matter of the raven that God sent to teach the son of Adam how to conceal his brother's nakedness, as He said: ﴿Then God sent a raven scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's corpse. He said, "Woe is me! Was I unable to be like this raven and conceal my brother's corpse?" And he became of the regretful﴾ (Al-Ma'idah 5:31).

How did the raven do this deed? It did it by the instinct that God placed in it. And if you reflect on the donkey, which is used as a proverb for stupidity: when you want it to cross a canal, for example, you see it look at it and measure its distance. If it can cross it, it leaps without hesitation; and if it is beyond its capacity, it draws back, and no matter how much you beat it or force it to cross, it does not advance. This is natural instinct.

Therefore you find that creatures not endowed with choice do not err, because they are governed by instinct, and they have no intellect that calls them to desire, and no choice between alternatives, like the electronic computer which gives you exactly what you have put into it, neither more nor less. Man, however, can alter the truth and conceal what you want from him, because he has an intellect that discriminates: "Say this, and do not say that." This is what God distinguished man by from the rest of creation.

Likewise, you see that an animal, when sated, refuses food, and you cannot get it to eat a single stalk of clover no matter how you try; whereas man, the possessor of intellect and desire, says to you: "Show me the colors, and it shows you the corners" (a colloquial saying). So there is nothing to stop him, after eating to the point of satiety, from tasting various kinds of sweets, fruit, and the like.

In this verse God, the Exalted, states that He: ﴿gave everything its creation, then guided [it]﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:50).

Take for example the ear, and how it is finely structured and suited to receiving sounds. On the outside of the ear there are folds and convolutions that receive loud sounds and thereby reduce their intensity until they reach the delicate eardrum calmly; otherwise the sounds would tear it and deafen. Likewise God made it to repel winds, so that when they blow, the ear does not find itself bare, exposed, and harmed.

And likewise the eye: how many signs of God are in it! God created it with measure. Among these signs: if its temperature rises above 12 degrees it is corrupted, and if the tip of the nose rises above 9 degrees it cannot perform its function. Yet there is an organ in the body whose temperature is 40 degrees, the liver, and the overall temperature of the human being is 37 degrees, which remains constant in cold regions where there is ice just as it does in hot regions; it neither rises nor falls except due to a cause or an affliction in the body.

So, everything in existence has been created by God with measure, wisdom and a manner suited to performing its task, as He said in another verse: ﴿Who created and proportioned, and who decreed and guided﴾ (Al-A'la 87:2–3).

The tongue, for example, has been given by God many taste buds, each of which tastes a particular flavor: one for sweet, one for bitter, one for spicy, and so on; all of them in this narrow space, adjacent and closely packed with a precise and miraculous measure.

The nose, with the sticky mucous matter that adheres and does not drip from you, and the fine hairs, so that the air of inhalation undergoes filtering and conditioning before reaching the two lungs; therefore the hairs inside the nose should not be cut, because they have a function.

The heart muscle with its atria and ventricles, and its inlets for blood and precisely fitted outlets, working mechanically, not stopping and not failing for 140 or 120 years, working automatically even while you sleep. What machine could perform this task?

When God, the Exalted, sent Moses and Aaron with a sign indicating their truthfulness to Pharaoh, their essential task was to take the Children of Israel and rescue them from Pharaoh's tyranny; the matter of faith came as a consequence. As for the core of Moses' mission, it was: ﴿So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:47).

When God, the Exalted, presents the question of faith, He presents it beginning with the proof of origin, which came in His saying: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided [it]﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:50). Because Pharaoh, who claimed divinity, must have had subjects who were worshipped by him, and they are creatures like him, and he took pride in his kingship and his wealth from the land of Egypt, its Nile and its bounties, until he said: ﴿Is not the dominion of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me...?﴾ (Az-Zukhruf 43:51).

So God, the Exalted, wanted to answer him: Do you have any part in the creation of these whom you claim as subjects?

And how similar the position of Pharaoh before this argument is to the position of Nimrod before the Prophet Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said to him: ﴿My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. He said, "I give life and cause death..."﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:258).

Nimrod found nothing but disputation and sophistry, so he resorted to the trick of the bankrupt: he brought two men and said, "I sentence this one to death and pardon that one." So when Abraham, peace be upon him, sensed from him evasion and dispute, he moved him to a matter from which he could not escape:

﴿Abraham said, "Indeed, God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." And the one who disbelieved was confounded. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:258).

So: the appeal to the question of the first creation is a proof that no one can refute. Even Pharaoh himself never claimed that he created anything; he merely acted arrogantly and proudly and claimed divinity over a deity he did not create, and he did not create himself, nor did he create the kingship in which he took pride.

And since the proof of original creation is the convincing proof, Pharaoh had no answer to it. Therefore, when he heard this matter, ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided [it]﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:50), he could not refute this proof, so he wanted to take the dialogue away from the matter of seriousness toward another matter that he could flee to, a secondary matter of no value: ﴿He said, "What then of the former generations?"﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:51).

Note: "bahata" (بهت): was astonished and bewildered. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/86). Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab (root: b-h-t): "he ceased and fell silent, bewildered by it."

Meaning: What is the matter with the earlier nations? But what does the first generations have to do with what we are discussing? The word al-bal (بال): it means thought, as we say: "it occurred to my mind" (خطر ببالي), i.e., to my thinking. Nothing comes into thought and the focus of awareness except an important matter.

But Moses quickly sensed Pharaoh's evasion and his attempt to flee from the main subject, so he closed the door on him. ﴿He said: "Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."﴾ (20:52)

This matter is not within my field of expertise, because the one who asks about the earlier generations is the one who will recompense them, and it is necessary that he know their condition and what they were upon of faith or disbelief, so that he may recompense them accordingly. So this is a question with no place: it is mere jesting, idle talk, and evasion. No one knows the condition of the earlier generations except Allah, for He, glorified is He, is the One who will recompense them.

The meaning of ﴿In a Book...﴾ (Ta-Ha, 52): that is, He has recorded them in a Book, which the angels who manage affairs (al-mudabbirat amran) look upon, so that they may carry out the duty for which Allah has appointed them. The Book is not meant to imply that Allah looks upon it and knows what is in it, for He, glorified is He: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ (Ta-Ha, 52).

Then Moses brought him back to the first matter, the matter of creation, but in a detailed form:

﴿He who made the earth for you as a cradle and threaded for you therein roads, and sent down from the sky water, and We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants.﴾ (20:53)

Mahdan (cradle): from tamhid, which is preparing a thing and making it ready for its task, as you do with your bed before you sleep. For this reason a child's bed is called mahd, because you prepare it for him, level it, and remove from it whatever disturbs or troubles him, so that he settles in his cradle and rests.

You must perform this task for him, because he lives by your instinct, unless his own instincts awaken to such matters so that he does them himself. Therefore, during this period, you are obliged to care for him, raise him and look after him.

So the meaning of ﴿He made the earth for you as a cradle...﴾ (20:53) is: He leveled it and prepared it so that it would be fit for your life and your livelihood upon it.

The meaning of preparing it as a cradle is not that He made it level. Rather, He leveled it for its function. Otherwise, there are mountains, elevations and valleys on the earth, and without them life upon it would not be sound for us. So its leveling requires making it suitable for living upon, whether by flatness, winding, elevation or depression.

For example, in flat areas you find roads that are level and straight, while in mountainous regions they are winding and twisting, because they cannot be otherwise. Their winding has the advantage that you do not face the sun for a long period, but alternate between facing the sun once and shade another time.

We have already given an example of the hook that we make of iron: if we made it straight, it would not perform its task. So its straightness lies in its being bent, and you say: "I leveled it so that it could perform its task." And if it were straight, it would not pull the thing it is meant to pull.

Therefore we say: leveling (taswiyah) is making a thing fit for its task, whether by moderation or by crookedness, whether by unevenness (amt) or by straightness.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿and threaded for you therein roads...﴾ (20:53): that is, paved roads that bring you to your needs with ease.

Salaka (threaded): means "entered" and is transitive. You say: "So-and-so took the road" (salaka fulan al-tariq).

He, exalted, said: ﴿What has threaded you into Saqar?﴾ (74:42), so those addressed are "threaded" into Saqar, meaning: entering it. And He said: ﴿Insert your hand into your pocket...﴾ (28:32), meaning: put it in.
