So its transitivity is either to the object that enters or to the place entered. Thus His saying: ﴿and threaded for you therein roads...﴾ (20:53) is transitive to the place entered, meaning: you transferred the addressees to the place entered; you entered, and the roads are the place entered.

Therefore the object is sometimes the one threaded and sometimes the place threaded through.

When you travel through desert roads, you find them varying according to the capacity for travel on them: some are narrow, just the width of one person's foot, and others are wide enough for loaded camels or vehicles. So He threaded for you roads that are diverse and varied according to the task you perform.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿And sent down from the sky water, and We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants.﴾ (20:53)

This too is part of the matter of creation, which no one can claim, because such a claim is refuted against its claimant. You, who claim divinity, bring forth for us something of this: show us a kind of plant, and you will not be able to, and thus the proof is established against him.

Just as sending down water from the sky is something no one has any work in, when plants come forth, we may have a role, such as plowing, sowing, watering and the like. But this work is drawn from the causes that God created for you. Therefore, when He spoke of water He said "sent down," in which no one has any part, and when He spoke of the bringing forth of plants He said "We brought forth," because many attributes converge in it that assist in the process of its emergence. The Truth, blessed and exalted, respects and values your causal work.

Read His saying: ﴿Have you considered what you plough? Do you cause it to grow, or are We the growers?﴾ (56:63-64). He affirmed for them an action and respected their effort. But as for what you plow: where did you get the seeds? If you trace the chain of earlier seeds, it ends in a plant that had no prior, just as if you traced the human chain, you would find it ends at a father who had no father except the One who created him.

And after you cast the seed into the earth and watered it, do you have any power over its sprouting and growth day by day? Did you hold it and pull it to make it grow? Or is it the power of the Able: ﴿He who created and proportioned (2), and who determined and guided (3)﴾ (87:2-3)?

Therefore He, exalted, says after it: ﴿Had We willed, We would have made it crumbled debris...﴾ (56:65). If this is your work, then guard it.

As happened with Qarun when he said of God's blessing: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have...﴾ (39:49).

Since the matter is so, guard it, O Qarun, with the knowledge you have. But when God caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling, that showed the falsehood of his statement.

We note in His saying: ﴿...made it crumbled debris...﴾ (56:65) that it is emphasized with the lam. Why? Because you have an appearance of work in the matter of sowing, which may tempt you and make you hesitate to accept. But when He spoke of water, He said:

﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Did you bring it down from the rainclouds, or are We the sender? Had We willed, We would have made it bitter...﴾ (56:68-70).

Without emphasis, because it is a matter that no one claims for himself.

His saying: ﴿pairs of various plants﴾ (20:53): He did not say merely "a plant," but "pairs," because God, exalted, wants things to multiply, and multiplication necessarily requires two: male and female. Just as humans multiply, so do the rest of creatures, because the Truth, blessed and exalted, created the earth and determined its sustenance in it, and these sustenances must suffice everyone who lives on this earth.

So if the earth becomes constricted and does not yield what suffices us, and people go hungry, then let us know that the shortcoming is ours, we humans, in reclaiming and cultivating the earth. Therefore, when a shortage of food occurred among us, we went out into the desert to reclaim it, and it has now begun to bear its fruits and we see its benefit. And now we know that we were heedless during the previous period, so we multiplied but did not increase the cultivated area around us.

Male and female are not only in plants, but in everything God created: ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ (36:36).

So pairing is in everything, whether you know it or not, even in inanimate things: there is the negative and the positive, and electrons and ions in the atom. Thus, as humanity multiplies, so does provision multiply.

His saying: ﴿of various plants﴾ (20:53): "shatta" is like "marda," the plural of "marid" (sick), so "shatta" is the plural of "shatit." It means many different and scattered things, not only in kinds, but within a single kind there is variation.

For example, if you go to the date market in the city of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, you will find many kinds, differing in shapes, tastes and sizes, all under one name: dates. And so, if you contemplate the rest of the kinds of cultivated produce.

1 Al-amt: difference in terrain in height and depth. God said: ﴿You will not see therein crookedness or unevenness﴾ (20:107). That is, on the Day of Resurrection you will not see in the earth any winding, deviation to the right or left, nor any difference in height and depth. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/30).
2 It is said: the Fire was called Saqar because it melts bodies and spirits; the word is Arabic, from their saying: "saqarathu al-shams," meaning: the sun melted it. (Lisan al-Arab, root s-q-r).

Then the Exalted, may He be blessed, mentions the reason for bringing forth vegetation: ﴿Eat and graze your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding (ulī al-nuhā).﴾

("Eat" ) indicates that the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, created life and created its necessities, the first of which is sustenance of food and drink. These necessities are arranged so that ownership corresponds with importance: food first, then water, then air.

You need food, and you can endure without it for a month, according to what your body stores of fat and flesh, from which the body feeds when food is lacking. For when you eat, you consume part of the food in your movement, and the remainder is stored in the form of fat, which is the storehouse of nourishment in the body. When the fat is exhausted, the body draws its nourishment from the flesh, then from the bone, which is the last storehouse of nourishment in the human body.

Therefore, when our master Zakariyya (peace be upon him) wished to express his weakness, he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened within me..﴾ (Maryam, 4).

Therefore you will often find that food is possessed, because you can endure it for a long time, which enables you to devise ways of obtaining it, or enables others to help you when they know you are confined and hungry.

As for water, you cannot endure without it for more than three days to ten; therefore water is rarely possessed by anyone.

As for air, you cannot endure without it for more than a single breath. So it is from the mercy of God toward His servants that air is not possessed by anyone; for if the owner of the air were to become angry with you and withhold it from you, you would die before he was pleased with you, and there is no time to devise a way of obtaining it.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and graze your livestock..﴾ (Taha, 53): because they too need sustenance. And He, Exalted, said in another verse: ﴿as a provision for you and your livestock (33)﴾ (al-Nazi'at). All of this converges on being a provision for the human being, for whom God subjected this whole universe.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding (54)﴾ (Taha).

Ayat: wonders. Al-nuhā (intellects, understanding): the plural of nahiyya, like qurab, the plural of qurba (a water-skin). Al-nuhā are the intellects, and God Exalted also called them al-albab (minds), and by them the process of deliberation in choices is accomplished.

Al-'aql (intellect) derives from al-'iqal, the tether with which an animal is hobbled so that it does not run away from you. Likewise, intellect was not created for you so that you may let it wander as you wish; rather, that it may restrain your instincts and govern them according to their purpose in your life. The instinct for eating, for example, is for the preservation of life, and in proportion to the capacity of the body; if it increases, it becomes gluttony that corrupts.

Curiosity has been placed in you to contemplate the universe and uncover its secrets and the signs of God within it, so you should not exceed that and spy upon the creation of God.

The intellects are also called al-nuhā because they forbid such excesses.

Therefore, a human being must have an intellect that restrains his instincts, so that they do not exceed the task for which they were made, and stops them at the limit required of them; otherwise they would run loose and rampage through the universe. A human being must have a restraining faculty that forbids him and says to him: No to the desires of the soul and its whims. Otherwise, how could you let loose the reins of your desires, when you are not alone in the universe? And what would the state be if others let loose the reins of their desires?

Intellect is also called lubb (kernel), to point you to the realities of things rather than their husks, so that you may be more far-sighted and deeper in thought regarding matters. When He commands you to give some of your surplus wealth to the poor, shallow thinking says: "No, how shall I toil and sweat to gather it, only then to give it to the poor man, who has done nothing?"

But when you delve deeply into understanding the wisdom of this matter, you find that the Real, blessed and exalted, has said to you: Give to the needy now while you are able, so that when you come to need, you will find someone to give to you. For the rich may become poor, the healthy may become sick, the strong may become weak; this is a cycle that turns among creatures and passes among them.

And when you look at the sharia's restriction of your desires, do not forget that it restricts others too by the same method and the same obligations. When it tells you not to look at the forbidden things of people while you are a single individual, it is in fact commanding all people not to look at your forbidden things.

Thus the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, made this instrument of intellect not so that we may run wild with it in the universe, but so that we may use it to govern the instincts and conduct, and guard them from the savagery of passions, so that society becomes balanced and its members are safe.

Otherwise, if you permit yourself to steal, then permit others to steal from you! Therefore, it is in your own interest that there be a legislation that restrains you, and a method that organizes your life and the lives of others.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 20, verse 55:

And Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth once again﴾.

We observe here that Musa, peace be upon him, presents to Pharaoh matters that do not concern Pharaoh alone, but rather prevent another Pharaoh from arising.

His words ﴿from it﴾ (Ta-Ha): i.e., from the earth, of which He had already said: ﴿Who has made for you the earth as a cradle﴾ (Ta-Ha 53).

Then He mentioned for us, together with the earth, three stages: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth once again﴾ (Ta-Ha 55).

In another verse He mentions a fourth stage, saying: ﴿In it you will live, and in it you will die, and from it you will be brought forth﴾ (al-A'raf 25).

Thus the stages become four: from it We created you; in it you live; you return to it through death; and from it We bring you forth through resurrection.

As for His words, Exalted is He, ﴿From it We created you﴾ (Ta-Ha 55): creation is of two kinds: primary creation (khalq awwali) and secondary creation (khalq thanawi). The primary creation was in Adam, peace be upon him, who was created from clay, i.e., from the earth. Then comes the secondary creation, which arises through procreation. Since the primary creation was from clay, everything that arises from it is considered likewise, because it is the first origin.

The matter may be directed in another way, and we may say: procreation is generated from the male's sperm-cells (mikrobat) and the female's ova (buwaydat al-untha), and these originate from food and drink, and their origin too is from the earth. So you are from the earth, either through an intermediary or without one.

Although this matter of creation is an unseen matter, the Creator has left in His universe minds that investigate and reflect upon the cosmos, and that give us evidence for the truth of this matter. When scientists analysed the clay of the earth, they found it to consist of sixteen elements, beginning with oxygen and ending with manganese; and when they analysed the elements of the human being, they found the same sixteen elements. Thereby analytical research confirms the truth of the matter of creation which the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, has reported.

As for His words ﴿And into it We will return you﴾ (Ta-Ha 55): this is a stage that is witnessed. Whoever among us dies, we bury in the earth; therefore the poet says:

If you tire of life, return to the earth, and you will rest secure from ailments (1)

After the structure of a person is dismantled by death, none hastens to cover him with dust except the closest of people to him. You see the woman whose only son has died, the one most beloved to her, and who could not bear to be parted from him for a single night, now cannot bear his presence; rather she hastens to bring him to his original mother (the earth).

This is because the body, after the soul has departed from it, swiftly turns into a carcass that is not endured even by his mother and the people closest to him. As for the earth, it embraces him and absorbs all the harm within him.

Among the wonders of the dismantling of the human structure by death is that it occurs in the reverse of its construction. When the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, spoke of the first creation of man, He said that he was created from dust, from clay, from black mud moulded (hama masnun), and from clay like pottery. We said that these are all stages of a single material; then afterward the soul is breathed into him, and life stirs within him.

If we reflect upon death, we find it in the reverse of this order, just as if you built a building of several floors, the last floor built would be the first to be demolished. Likewise, death for a human being begins with the removal of the soul, which was placed in him last; then the body stiffens and dries (yashdub) like clay, then decays, and stinks like black moulded mud; then the water in it evaporates, the remaining elements dissolve, and it turns back into dust.

Then He, Exalted, says: ﴿And from it We will bring you forth once again﴾ (Ta-Ha 55), i.e., another time, by resurrection on the Day of Judgment. This bringing forth has a special order that differs from the first bringing forth, because it begins with the return of the soul, and then the body is completed for it.

All these are cosmic matters presented to Pharaoh, perhaps to turn him from what he is upon of claiming divinity. Divinity requires one who is worshipped: a god is one worshipped and one who has worshippers. How then does he claim divinity, when he has no share in lordship (rububiyya)? Divinity and worship deserve none but the one who possesses lordship first. And in the proverbs: "He who eats my morsel hears my word."

(1) al-Wasab: pain and sickness; its plural is awsab. Al-Wasab is the constancy and persistence of pain. (Lisan al-Arab, root: w-s-b.)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 56:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We showed him all Our signs, but he denied and refused.﴾

Ayat (signs): wondrous matters, as we say: "So-and-so is an ayah in intelligence, an ayah in beauty, an ayah in generosity," meaning: marvelous in his field. We have already divided the signs of Allah into: cosmic signs, such as the sun and the moon; signs that establish the truthfulness of the messengers, which are the miracles; and the signs of the noble Qur'an, which are called the bearers of rulings.

However, the signs of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, are many and cannot be counted. So is it meant here that Pharaoh saw all the signs of Allah? No, because what is meant here is the relative signs (al-ayat al-idafiyyah), namely the nine signs that Allah made a proof for Musa and Harun and an evidence of their truthfulness, as He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs...﴾ (al-Isra', 101).

They are: the staff, the hand, the flood, the locusts, the lice(1), the frogs, the blood, the years (of drought), and the shortage of fruits. These are the signs that Allah showed to Pharaoh.

The totality in His saying ﴿all Our signs﴾ (Ta-Ha, 56) is a relative totality (kulliyyah idafiyyah). That is, all the signs specific to him, just as you say to your child, "I have brought you everything," and you do not mean that you brought him everything that exists, but rather it is a relative totality meaning everything you need.

Yet the outcome was ﴿but he denied and refused﴾ (Ta-Ha, 56). "Denied" means he attributed them to falsehood, and falsehood is a statement that has no reality behind it; his denial of Musa was the cause of his refusal. "Refused" means he abstained from believing in what Musa brought.

If we were to debate Pharaoh about his denial of Musa when he said: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided [it]﴾ (Ta-Ha, 50),

we would ask: Why did you deny, O Pharaoh? The Truthful One, glory be to Him, has said: "I created this universe with everything in it," and no one has come to refute this statement or claim it for himself. Even you, O one who claimed divinity, did not claim to have created anything. Therefore, this is a matter conceded to the Creator, mighty and majestic is He, which no one has disputed with Him. Thus you are a liar in your denial of Musa and in your refusal to believe in him.

1 Al-qummal: small insects that harm crops and trouble people. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/134) It is not the well-known head or body louse..

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿He said: "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?"﴾

The Egyptians lived in ancient times on the banks of the Nile; therefore they say: "Egypt is the gift of the Nile." When the water receded, they would sow the seeds and wait for them throughout the year. They had no work to occupy them, and this monotonous life made them accustomed to a degree of laziness. Yet they loved this place, and if you were to say to one of them: "Leave this land for a day or two," he would rise up against you and grow angry.

Therefore Pharaoh exploited his people's attachment to the land of Egypt, and he tried to incite those over whom he presents himself as a god, inciting them against Moses and Aaron. So he spoke this statement: ﴿"Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?"﴾ (Ta-Ha).

Here the people rose up, not out of concern for Pharaoh's threatened divinity, but in defense of their economic interests and what they benefit from on the banks of this blessed Nile, which does not withhold from them its flooding or its receding. The people used to call it "the one blessed in its mornings and evenings," flowing with its rising and falling like the course of the sun and the moon, and having its appointed time.

Thus Pharaoh shifted the field of dispute with Moses and Aaron onto his subjects. The matter became one between Moses and Aaron and Pharaoh's subjects, because he feared the words of Moses and the issues he would present; if the people understood them, they would expose his falsehood, turn against him, rebel against his rule, and reject his divinity over them. So he drew them in as a party to this dispute.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 20, verse 58:

Then the Truthful, Glorified One says: ﴿So we will surely bring you magic like it. So set between us and you an appointment which neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place equitable [to both].﴾

Pharaoh called what Moses brought "magic"; therefore he said: ﴿So we will surely bring you magic like it.﴾ (Ta-Ha). This naming is mistaken with respect to Moses, although it is correct with respect to the people of Pharaoh. So what, then, is the difference between what Moses brought and what the people of Pharaoh brought?

Magic does not change the reality of a thing; rather, the thing remains in its reality, and the magic affects the one who sees, so he sees things other than as they are. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people﴾ (al-A'raf). So when the magicians threw their ropes, they were ropes in reality, even though the onlooker saw them as snakes and serpents moving swiftly. As for the staff of Moses, when he threw it, it turned into a real serpent, as evidenced by the fact that when he saw it in that state, he was frightened of it.

And His saying: ﴿So set between us and you an appointment which neither we nor you will fail to keep﴾ (Ta-Ha) means: let us agree upon an appointment that neither of us will break. ﴿At a place equitable﴾ (Ta-Ha), i.e., level, because it will be a spectacle for all the people, so that the sight of the spectators is equal in it, such that the view is not blocked for anyone. Or "equitable" (suwa) means: equal with respect to us and you, as we say: "let us meet at the midpoint of the road, neither I nor you will be tired."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Said he: "Your appointment is the Day of Adornment, and let the people be gathered in the forenoon."﴾

It is known that an event (hadath) requires someone who causes it (muhdith), requires a place where it occurs, and requires a time in which it happens. We have already identified the ones causing this encounter: Musa and Harun on one side, and Fir'awn and his sorcerers on the other.

Fir'awn set the place when he said: ﴿a place midway.﴾ There remained the time needed to complete the event, so Musa set it when he said: ﴿Your appointment is the Day of Adornment...﴾, because an event is not completed except in a time and a place.

For this reason we do not say: "When is God?" or "Where is God?" The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is not an event, and "when" and "where" are created things of God, Exalted is He, so how could time or place limit Him?

As for Musa's words: ﴿Your appointment is the Day of Adornment...﴾, he did not say "Monday" or "Tuesday," for example. The Day of Adornment is a day when all the inhabitants of Egypt gather. It appears to be the day of the Nile's flood (wafa' al-Nil), when they go out in their finery, joyful at the Nile's overflow and its abundant blessings. Egypt still celebrates this day.

The judge would not issue a ruling on the land tax (kharaj) until he had looked at the Nile gauge (miqyas al-Nil). If he saw that it would irrigate the lands, he would set the tax; otherwise, he would not.

But why did Musa choose this particular day? Why did he not set any other day? Because Musa, peace be upon him, was fully confident of God's victory for him, and he wanted Fir'awn's disgrace to take place before this assembly and in the midst of this gathering. Such a gathering is an opportunity Musa would not waste, because on this day people's souls are happy and at ease, so they are closer in their gladness to accepting the truth than at any other time.

As for His saying: ﴿and let the people be gathered in the forenoon (duha)﴾, that is, ﴿in the forenoon﴾ meaning at the time when it is bright. The Day of Adornment could be early in the morning or at the end of the day, but Musa was firmly confident of victory and wanted this encounter to take place in the full light of day, so that everyone would witness it.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿So Pharaoh withdrew, gathered his scheming, then came﴾ (20:60).

"Withdrew" (tawalla): that is, he left Moses and went away to arrange his affair.

"Gathered his scheming" (fa-jama'a kaydahu): al-kayd (scheming) is the hidden planning against an opponent. Hidden planning here is not a sign of strength but a sign of weakness, because he has no power to confront openly. It is like one who slips poison to another because he is unable to face him.

So, scheming is a sign of weakness. For this reason we understand from His saying, exalted is He, about women: ﴿Indeed, your scheming is great﴾ (12:28), that it is not a proof of a woman's strength but a proof of her weakness. Just as their scheming is great, so their weakness is great.

The meaning of ﴿gathered his scheming﴾ (20:60) is that he turned his mind over the various kinds of scheming, to choose from among them what is most harmful to his opponent, as occurs in another verse concerning Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿So resolve upon your affair...﴾ (10:71).

It is as though the matter he was undertaking required several points of view: shall we do this, or shall we do that? Then he finishes this consultation with an opinion that encompasses all possibilities, so that nothing surprises him after he has guarded against every aspect.

The meaning, then, is: agree upon the clear plan that unites your opinions when the goal is achieved.

Among this is His saying in the story of Joseph, peace be upon him: ﴿And they resolved to put him in the depths of the well...﴾ (12:15). That is: they agreed upon this opinion and united on it, after one of them had said: ﴿Kill Joseph or cast him out to some land...﴾ (12:9). It is as though the final opinion was that they should put him in the depth of the well.

They were, in any case, of a prophetic lineage, in whose natures evil had not taken root. For this reason their evil diminished, from killing, to casting him into the wildernesses of the earth, to the least of these dangers: that they should throw him into the well. This is the attribute of the righteous. As for the wicked, in whose souls evil has taken root and deepened, their evil increases and grows. One of them says: "I want to meet so-and-so, and I will spit in his face, or strike him, or cut him up, or rather a bullet will finish him off," thus his evil is satisfied.

After that they hope for his rescue, saying: ﴿Some travellers will pick him up﴾ (12:10).

Then Allah, exalted is He, says concerning Pharaoh: ﴿then came﴾ (20:60), that is: he came to the appointment that had been set beforehand, in place and time.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, tells us about the events of that day, saying:

﴿Moses said to them, "Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment. Indeed, he fails who fabricates."﴾

When Moses saw the magicians, he wished to warn them of what they were about to undertake, and to give them the prohibitions that would restrain them. So he reminded them that they have a Lord who will hold them to account. This is like when you say to a person whom you see about to commit a crime: "If you do such-and-such, I will report you to the police, and you will be punished with such-and-such," and you remind him of the consequence of his crime.

﴿Do not fabricate a lie against Allah..﴾ (Ta-Ha 61). "Iftara" means: came with a fabrication (al-fariyyah), which is the deliberate intent to lie. ﴿Lest He destroy you with a punishment..﴾ (Ta-Ha 61). That is: He will uproot you with a punishment of this world before the punishment of the Hereafter. ﴿And he fails who fabricates﴾ (Ta-Ha 61). That is: he loses.

(1) "Yushhitakum" (يسحتكم): He will destroy you and uproot you. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/304).

Then the Truthful, Glorified One says: ﴿So they disputed among themselves about their affair, and kept their private counsel secret﴾ (20:62).

It appears that Moses's warning to them, when he said: ﴿Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment...﴾ (20:61) (Ta-Ha), had an effect on them and frightened them. ﴿So they disputed their affair...﴾ (20:62) (Ta-Ha).

They began to bargain over words and exchange opinions.

﴿And kept their private counsel secret﴾ (20:62) (Ta-Ha): they spoke in secret. This is evidence of their fear of Moses's words, and evidence of the readiness for good that was in them; but their final opinion came to continuing along the course to its end.

Scholars have paused at length over this verse, because it contains two readings: (inna hadhani) with the letter (inna) unstressed, and the other (inna hadhani) with (inna) stressed (shaddah).

The reading we follow is that of Hafs: ﴿Indeed, these two are certainly sorcerers...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:63). Here (inna) is a conditional particle when it precedes a verb, as we say: "If (in) Zayd visits me, I will honour him." It also comes as a negating particle meaning (ma), as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Those who divorce their wives by saying, "You are to me like the back of my mother," they are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them...﴾ (al-Mujadila 58:2).

So the meaning is: "Their mothers are not but those who bore them." Likewise in the verse ﴿Indeed, these two are certainly sorcerers...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:63), the meaning is: "These two are not but sorcerers," and the lam in ﴿lasaharan﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:63) is then in the sense of (illa), as if you had said: "These two are not but sorcerers."

The lam also comes in the sense of (illa) when, for example, we dispute over something, each of us claiming it for himself, and the judge says: "It belongs to Zayd, he has more right to it," as if he had said: "This thing is not but Zayd's." So the lam comes in the sense of (illa).

On the second reading, with the stressed (inna) ( inna hadhani lasaharan), the sentence is governed by a abrogating particle (harf nasikh) which puts the subject in the accusative and raises the predicate. You say: "Indeed Zayd is diligent" (inna Zaydan mujtahid). In the verse, however, with this reading, the noun (hadhani) comes in the nominative with the alif, because it is a dual, whereas the rule requires us to say (hadhayni).

How, then, is the stressed, abrogating (inna) to be explained when the noun after it is in the nominative?

They said: this is the dialect of Kinanah, one of the Arab tribes. Each tribe had its own particular dialect and well-known speech, and they say: the (ja'ja'ah) of Khuza'ah, the (tamtamaniyyah) of Himyar, the (talatulah) of Bahra', the (fahfahah) of Hudhayl, and so on.

When the Qur'an was revealed, it was revealed in the main language of Quraysh, because all the languages of the Arabs converged upon the language of Quraysh during the seasons of pilgrimage, poetry, trade and others. The language of Quraysh was therefore dominant among the languages of all these tribes, and for this reason the Qur'an was revealed in it. Yet the Truth, blessed and exalted, willed that the other tribes should also have a share, so some words of the Qur'an came in the various dialects of the Arabs, to show that the Qur'an is not for Quraysh alone, so that they should have supremacy over the Arabs, but that it came for all.

Among the tribal dialects in which the Qur'an was revealed is the dialect of Kinanah, which requires the dual to take the alif in all its cases: nominative, accusative and genitive. Their evidence in the books of grammar is the words of their poet:

"Alas for Salma, then alas, alas,
would that her eyes had come to us!
Hope is what we would have attained,
and the place of the anklet on her feet...
Indeed her father and her father's father
have reached the furthest point in glory."

He said "inna abaha" (indeed her father), and did not say "inna abihā," because the dual requires the alif.

So the Qur'an was not revealed in the language of Quraysh as a language of supremacy; rather, because it embraces the essence of the eloquence of all the dialects of the Arabian Peninsula. The language of Quraysh was refined in the seasons of poetry and literature at 'Ukaz, Dhu al-Majaz and elsewhere.

Returning to the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted: ﴿They said, "Indeed these two are certainly sorcerers who want to drive you out of your land with their magic..."﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:63) It appears that Pharaoh's summoning of his people against Moses and Aaron achieved its result, and his scheme took hold of their souls; so they repeat the very words of the great teacher Pharaoh, accusing Moses and Aaron of sorcery.

Their words: ﴿and they would take away your ideal way of life﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:63) mean: their ideal way of life.

That is: what the people had approved for living by, and the creed and path they had followed.

What is meant by "the ideal way" they followed is that they took one of their own as a god, whom they worshipped and whose command they obeyed. That is the "ideal way"! The word (muthla) means "the excellent," its masculine form being (amthal).
