And in another verse He said: ﴿Pharaoh said, "I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct"﴾ (Ghafir 40:29).

Meaning: be alert and sharpen all your minds, all your arts, and your movements in sorcery, so that the two of them (Musa and Harun) cannot achieve these two things: expelling you from your land, and eliminating your best way of life.

This is the saying of some of them to others: ﴿So gather your plot⁠—﴾ (Ta-Ha 64): let no one conceal any art of sorcery, and let each of us bring forward what he has. For it is the custom of the people of a craft that jealousy exists among them, so that none of them reveals all that he has at once, or tries to conceal what he has so that the other does not learn of it. But in such a situation they must join their efforts, for the moment is critical, and its trial will afflict everyone if we fail in this task.

And his saying: ﴿then come in ranks⁠—﴾ (Ta-Ha 64): meaning, gathered together as if you were one hand. This is more awe-inspiring for you and more effective in instilling terror into the hearts of your opponents, just as when we come together as one, no one can turn back, so each of us becomes a watchman over the others.

﴿And he has indeed succeeded today who gains the upper hand⁠—﴾ (Ta-Ha 64): aflaha (أفلح) means "he won," as in His saying, ﴿Successful indeed are the believers⁠—﴾ (al-Mu'minun 1). This word is derived from falaha al-ard (فلح الأرض), "he tilled the land," from which comes al-filaha (agriculture), because the farmer, when he plows, hoes and tends the land, it gives him its produce, so his activity in it is a blessed and auspicious activity.

Therefore, when the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wished to explain to us the multiplication of reward and recompense for charity and for doing good, He struck for us an example with sowing, saying, ﴿The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that sprouts seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing⁠—﴾ (al-Baqarah 261).

So if the earth, being created by Allah the Exalted, gives all this bounty, then what of the bounty of the Creator of this earth? Therefore He followed the parable with His saying, ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills⁠—﴾ (al-Baqarah 261).

Then the word falah (فلاح) became a designation for every kind of success, even if it had no connection with the land, because the ultimate purpose of all life's activities is to secure for a person the survival of his kind through food, and the earth is the source of all of this; thus it became a source of success.

And His saying: ﴿who gains the upper hand⁠—﴾ (Ta-Ha 64): meaning, who seeks to rise above his opponent. But does success belong to one who seeks to rise, or to one who has actually risen? Naturally, it belongs to one who has risen. Therefore, whoever has actually risen must sharpen his mind to seek to rise above his opponent, so that whenever the opponent rises, he seeks to rise over him, meaning: before he rose, he sought to rise.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says about the magicians: ﴿They said, "O Moses, either you throw first, or we will be the first to throw."﴾

Tulqi: tarmi (you throw). The meaning is that one of them would throw what he had prepared of magic, and Moses chose that they throw first.

Because if they cast their magic first, the staff would have a role only when Moses throws it. So he wanted the staff to have movement after it turns into a serpent, a snake, or a jann; otherwise, if he threw first, what would its function be?

God Almighty inspired the sorcerers of Pharaoh with this courtesy in their contest with Moses. They gave him the choice between casting first or them casting first, and God, blessed and exalted is He, comes between a person and his heart. He inspired them with this even though they were his opponents, and He made them speak in a way that supports the bearer of the everlasting miracle. So they said: ﴿Either you throw, or we will be the first to throw﴾ (Ta-Ha).

Moses, peace be upon him, chose to throw last, because of the experience he had undergone at Tuwa with his Lord, mighty and majestic, when his Lord said to him: ﴿Throw it, O Moses﴾ (Ta-Ha).

So when Moses threw his staff, it turned into a snake moving swiftly, and he himself saw its movement. But there was no trace in that experience of the staff swallowing anything. So if Moses had thrown first and the staff had turned into a snake or a serpent, what would distinguish it from the ropes of the sorcerers that turned before them into snakes and serpents?

Therefore, there must be something that distinguishes the staff of Moses as a miracle from the magic and trickery of the sorcerers. For this reason Moses chose to throw last, by inspiration from God, so that his staff would swallow what they were fabricating. What swallows must come after what is swallowed.

In terms of movement before the onlookers, there is no difference between the staff of Moses and the ropes and staffs of the sorcerers, for all of them move. What distinguished the staff of Moses is that it swallows what they produce by magic, follows their ropes and staffs, and leaps here and there. It has, then, an eye that sees, and then it swallows their magic into its belly, yet it remains as it is, its belly not swelling, for example. This is the locus of the miracle in the staff of Moses, peace be upon him.(1)

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then behold, their ropes and their staffs, by their sorcery, seemed to him to be moving﴾ (Ta-Ha). So the movement of the staffs and ropes is not real movement, but only imagination: ﴿It seemed to him...(66)﴾ (Ta-Ha): so he sees them moving, while they are not so.

God, exalted is He, said about these sorcerers: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people...(116)﴾ (al-A'raf). So they produced deceptive imaginary effects by whatever means were available. Some say, for example, that they placed mercury in them, so that when the sun heated it, it expanded, and the objects began to writhe and move. Whatever their means, they are merely illusions, while the sorcerer himself sees them as ropes in their true form.

This is the difference between the magic of the sorcerers and the miracle of Moses' staff.

Magic differs from tricks that rely on quickness of movement, sleight of hand, and deception, for magic is closest to reality in the eyes of the beholder, as God said: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic...(102)﴾ (al-Baqarah).

So it is a craft that is learned, which produces imagination through the subjugation of jinn; it is they who perform all these movements. Thus it is not tricks or nimbleness of movement, but a process with principles and rules that are studied and learned.

When the Creator, mighty and majestic, presents to us the matter of magic, that it is a subjugation of devils to serve the sorcerer, He gives each of them the ability to harm others: the sorcerer by magic, and the devils by what they have of the ability to take various forms and to pass through barriers, because the jinn were created from fire, and fire has a transparency that passes through a wall, for example.

As for man, he was created from clay, and clay has density. To bring this matter closer, we gave an example: suppose you are sitting behind a wall, and behind this wall there is an apple, say, of frozen clay. Does anything from the apple reach you? But if behind the wall there is fire, you will feel its heat through the wall. These, then, are distinctions that the Creator, mighty and majestic, gave to the devils, in addition to their seeing you from where you cannot see them.

Yet it was of the gentleness of the Almighty toward us that He made for us a protection against the devils. Blessed and exalted is the Truth: when the jinn take on various forms, these forms govern them. That is, if a devil takes the form of a human for you, that form has bound him, so if you were to shoot him with a bullet at that moment, you would indeed kill him.

Therefore, the devil fears you more than you fear him, and they do not appear to us except as a flash and a quick glimpse, lest the one who sees them have knowledge of this matter, catch hold of them, and at that point they will not escape from you.

The Prophet, peace be upon him, once seized a devil and said:(2) "I had intended to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque, so that the boys of Madinah could play with him, but I remembered the supplication of my brother Solomon: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me...(35)﴾ (Sad)."

So the Truth, glorified is He, gave them the distinction of taking whatever form they like, but He restricted them to the forms they take on. It is as if He says to them: If you abandon your nature and take on another form, then accept that this form will govern you, and that the weaker than you will have power over you; otherwise they would terrify and frighten people, and we would not be safe from their evil.

And likewise the case with the sorcerer himself: through magic and talismans he has the power to subjugate the jinn to do for him whatever he wishes. This is a distinction by which his power surpasses the power of others, and through magic he has an opportunity that is not available to other common people. There is no equality of opportunity between him and them.

God, mighty and majestic, wants His creatures to have equal opportunities in the movement of life. So He says to the sorcerer: Beware of supposing that what He has made easy for you, by subjecting to you one stronger than you so that he may do what you cannot, benefits you in anything, or that by magic you have taken an opportunity over others. Rather, the opposite is true: you will gain from your magic nothing but harm and misery, for magic is a trial for man just as it is a trial for the jinn.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And they do not teach anyone until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve...(102)﴾ (al-Baqarah).

The meaning of "trial" here is that we test the use of what God has prepared for him: will he use it for good or for evil? If you say: "I learn magic so that I may use it for good," we say: this is your statement at the time of undertaking; you cannot guarantee yourself at the time of performance. As we said previously regarding bearing the trust: you accept it at the time of undertaking, confident of your ability to discharge it when the time comes and secure in the soundness of your intention in bearing it, but at the time of discharge, something may arise that changes your intention.

As the Truth, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant.(72)﴾ (al-Ahzab).

So they chose subjugation over choice and bearing the trust, because they could not guarantee carrying it out.

God Almighty has given the sorcerers an excuse in His saying: ﴿And they do not teach anyone until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve...(102)﴾ (al-Baqarah).

It is as if the end of the sorcerer is disbelief, because he is a son of desires and changing states, unable to control himself so as to direct the power of magic toward good. Likewise, if God wanted to subjugate the strong for good: would He subjugate the obedient or the disobedient? He would subjugate the obedient, and an obedient jinn would never be pleased with this matter.

Thus the sorcerer can only subjugate the disobedient jinn, as God said: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies...(121)﴾ (al-An'am).

Therefore we observe that all who engage in this practice bear the marks of anger upon their countenance and the traces of sins and their ill omen on their faces; whoever sees them recoils from them. They live in the most constricted forms of living. You see the sorcerer take from this person and take from that one, cheating and deceiving people, yet you find him a beggar living in hardship, dying in disbelief, removed from the mercy of God, and even his children after him do not escape his ill omen. The Great God spoke truly when He said: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in burden.(6)﴾ (al-Jinn).

Also, in the lives of sorcerers there is a point we must notice: the sorcerers who make magic for people and deceive them, from where do they earn their living? From common people who understand nothing of magic. If his magic had succeeded, he would have enriched himself and would not need to reach out to this one, taking from him a few pounds, and asking that one for strange things, convincing him that his problem will only be solved by them.

And why did he not use his magic to steal from a treasury, for example, and spare himself this toil? If he says: "How, when they are the people's wealth, and seizing it is theft?" then let him go to the buried treasure (rikaz) and the hoards of the earth, for these are owned by no one.

Let us return to the sorcerers of Pharaoh. Whatever their magic was, was it of the kind of tricks, nimbleness of movement, and deception of onlookers? Or was it of the kind of magic that the devils taught from the time of Solomon, peace be upon him? In either case, it is magic that cannot stand before a dazzling miracle that came through Moses to establish his truthfulness.

(1) Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: the staff began to follow those ropes and staffs one by one, until nothing, small or great, of what they had thrown could be seen in the valley. Then Moses took it, and behold, it was a staff in his hand as it had been. Recorded by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/237).

(2) A hadith agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3423), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (541), Book of Mosques, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, and its complete form: "Indeed a powerful jinn (ifrit) escaped from me last night to cut off my prayer, but God gave me power over him, so I seized him and wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque so that you could all look at him. Then I remembered the supplication of my brother Solomon: 'My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me.'"

(3) Al-Suddi said: a man would set out with his family, come to a land and stop there, and say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the jinn, that I or my property or my children or my livestock be harmed." Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/428): "When the jinn saw that men sought refuge with them out of fear of them, they increased them in burden, that is, in fear, intimidation and terror, until they became more fearful of them and sought refuge with them even more."

(4) Rikaz: what is in the earth of minerals in their natural state (al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, root r-k-z). Ahmad ibn Hanbal held that it is everything that comes out of the earth, created in it from other than it, which has value, such as gold, silver, iron, copper, pitch, petroleum and the like. The evidence for the obligation of zakat on rikaz is his saying, peace be upon him: "In rikaz there is a fifth," i.e., 20%. See: Fiqh al-Sunnah (1/354–357).

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿So Moses sensed a fear within himself﴾ (20:67).

"Awjasa" (أوجس): from al-ijas (الإيجاس), which is the stirring of a frightening thing in the heart that does not pass on to the limbs. If it passes on to the limbs, it turns into a motor action (عمل نزوعي), such as fleeing or running. The motor action comes after the emotional sensation, which is why the verse continues with ﴿within himself﴾ (20:67) (Ta-Ha).

Moses, peace be upon him, felt fear when he saw the ropes and staffs of the sorcerers turning before the spectators into snakes and serpents. Perhaps the onlookers were satisfied with what they had seen, so they shouted against him and ended the situation on this basis before he could do anything. If you ask: why did he not throw his staff so that the matter would end? We say: because his commands came from God moment by moment, and He was with him, following him by hearing and sight, so the instructions came to him fresh and directly.

This is a ruling from God, the Mighty and Majestic. It comes to Moses in the form of a brief telegram: ﴿You are the highest﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:68). That is: you are the one who will be victorious and successful, so be at peace. Yet Moses' humanness still stirs in him: "Victorious, how?"

Here comes the practical, executive command after this theoretical promise, as though the Truth, glory be to Him, were following every movement of His Prophet Moses. He did not leave him to tackle this matter alone. Rather, He was with him, hearing and seeing, responding to what he hears with what fits it and to what he sees with what fits it. The Prophet always sharpens his hearing and his heart to whatever directives his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, sends down to him. For this reason, his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:46).

So the appropriate response will come to you in its time. Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, did not inform Moses of his mission with Pharaoh and then leave him to carry it out by himself. Rather, this matter was accomplished through direct directives from God, exalted is He. ﴿And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the trickery of a sorcerer, and the sorcerer does not succeed wherever he goes﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:69).

This is the basis of the miracle of Moses' staff: that it swallows up what they fabricated of magic. The phrase ﴿talaqqaf﴾ (Q. 20:69) gives you a quick, kinetic image, like the blink of an eye. You say "talaqqaftuhu" (I snatched it), meaning: I took it quickly and forcefully. This is the reason for the staff to snatch up what they made of magic: ﴿Indeed, they have only made the plot of a magician.﴾ (Q. 20:69) Kayd (plotting, a hidden scheming to overcome an opponent). But what can the magician's plotting, his tricks and his fabrications do in the face of the power of the Lord, blessed and exalted?

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And the magician does not succeed wherever he goes.﴾ (Q. 20:69) We have already discussed the matter of the magician's success: however much power he is granted to subjugate the jinn to do something beyond human capacity, that will not give him any advantage over others, and he will have no power over anything.

So beware lest you think that God has handed over your interests to these people. It is true that they do act, but harm and injury come only by the permission of God and under His care: ﴿And they cannot harm anyone thereby except by the permission of God.﴾ (Q. 2:102) This principle does not apply to the magician alone, but to all of existence, until the Hour arrives.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿So the magicians were thrown down prostrate. They said: "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses." (70)﴾

Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj (1)) said in this situation: "Wondrous is the matter of these people. They threw down their ropes and their staffs in disbelief and denial, and behold, they threw themselves down in thankfulness and prostration."

Yes, they entered as disbelievers, wicked, and they came out as believers, righteous (2). For they had come with all their cunning, and had gathered the elite of magic and its masters, those who know magic well, and the tricks and sleights of magicians could not deceive them. So when they saw the staff and what it did to their magic, no doubt entered them that it was a miracle far removed from what they practise of magic. Therefore they hastened and did not hesitate to declare their faith in Moses and Aaron.

This shows us that the innate faith-disposition (fitrah) within the soul may be obscured by desires, but when the innate faith-disposition awakens and the veil is removed from it, it hastens toward faith and is moved by it.

The magicians hastened to faith, and there was a desire in their souls for it, as evidenced by their later words: ﴿And what you compelled us to do of magic.. (73)﴾ (Ta-Ha). So they were compelled; they were also made subservient, as evidenced by their saying: ﴿.. Indeed, for us there will surely be a reward if we are the victors (113)﴾ (al-A'raf).

It is as if they did not take a fee for magic; but when this task was difficult, they asked a reward for it, for it was a battle upon which his standing among his people depended. As for their practice of magic to terrify people and to frighten whoever was tempted to go out and rebel against Pharaoh, that was compulsory labour (sukhrah) for which they did not charge a fee.

Therefore Pharaoh did not oppose his magicians in their request, but added another gift: ﴿And indeed you will be among the closest (114)﴾ (al-A'raf). That is: you will be the custodians of Pharaonic rule. He wanted to fire up their resolve and sharpen their determination, so that they would spare no effort in the art of magic in this battle.

So, their natural disposition and innate nature refuse this act, and they know it to be a lie and fabrication; but what could they do when their chief commands them to it, and even compels them, and requires them to teach others (3)? Why? Because magic, sorcery and fabrication are his capital and merchandise, which he strives to market; upon them his kingdom stands and his divinity is built.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the magicians were thrown down prostrate.. (70)﴾ (Ta-Ha): there is a difference between ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs.. (44)﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), which was their voluntary act, and ﴿The magicians were thrown down prostrate.. (70)﴾ (Ta-Ha), meaning not by their choice and not by their will. It is as if the force of truth surprised the awakening of the innate disposition, so they could do nothing but fall down prostrate to God. The "throwing" here is an involuntary act, without thought from them and without awareness, for the clear truth and the dazzling miracle of Moses' staff surprised them, since it was not magic, and they were the most knowledgeable of people in magic.

We observe in this verse that it came in the plural form: "the magicians were thrown down, they said: We believe," to show that they were one hand, not one of them deviating, which indicates that they were compelled and made subservient.

Moreover, the declaration of their faith came first through the visible act witnessed by all: ﴿So the magicians were thrown down prostrate.. (70)﴾ (Ta-Ha), then through the audible word: ﴿They said: "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses." (70)﴾ (Ta-Ha). In another verse: ﴿They said: "We believe in the Lord of the worlds (47), the Lord of Moses and Aaron (48)"﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

We know that Moses, peace be upon him, was the principal, then his brother Aaron was sent with him. When the Qur'an presented the magicians' position with Moses, it related their words: ﴿"We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses" (70)﴾ (Ta-Ha), and their words: ﴿"We believe in the Lord of the worlds (47), the Lord of Moses and Aaron (48)"﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

Therefore this matter became a subject of dispute among the opponents of Islam, who say: What exactly did the magicians say? Did they say the first or the second?

Imagine the multitude of magicians who attended this contest: their leaders and elite were seventy magicians, so what of their subordinates? Thus they were many (4). Is it reasonable, with this multitude and this crowd, that they should unite in movement and in speech? Or would each of them have his own reaction according to his perception of faith?

There is no doubt that they did not agree on one saying: some of them said: ﴿"We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses" (70)﴾ (Ta-Ha), and others said: ﴿"We believe in the Lord of the worlds (47), the Lord of Moses and Aaron (48)"﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

Likewise, among them was one of superficial expression, who said: ﴿"We believe in the Lord of the worlds (47), the Lord of Moses and Aaron (48)"﴾ (al-Shu'ara'), and did not perceive that Pharaoh had claimed divinity and said "I am your most high lord." Perhaps from his saying "the Lord of Moses and Aaron (48)" one might understand that it is Pharaoh, since he was the one who raised Moses when he was a child.

And another perceived this matter, so he was more precise in expression and removed Moses from this suspicion, saying: ﴿"We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses" (70)﴾ (Ta-Ha). He mentioned Aaron first, to whom Pharaoh had no connection in raising him and no favour upon him, and then mentioned Moses.

Therefore these are multiple sayings and different snapshots of a mass public whose movements are not controlled and whose expressions do not agree. The Qur'an related them as they were, so no one after that may say: if the first saying is correct, then the other is wrong, or the reverse.

Such a scene now resembles a sports match witnessed by thousands who comment on it: would their descriptions of this match agree?

We say: thus the snapshots multiplied and the sayings multiplied for one story, so that the Qur'an might convey to us everything that happened.

1 He is Ibrahim ibn al-Sarri ibn Sahl Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj, a scholar of grammar and language, born 241 AH and died in Baghdad 311 AH. In his youth he worked as a glass-turner (kharrat al-zujaj) and inclined toward grammar; he tutored al-Qasim, son of Ubayd Allah ibn Sulayman, vizier of the Abbasid caliph al-Mu'tadid. (al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 1/40).
2 Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umayr said: they were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs, righteous, at its end. (Cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 3/158).
3 Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what you compelled us to do of magic.. (73)﴾ (Ta-Ha), that he said: Pharaoh took forty boys from the Children of Israel and ordered that they be taught magic in the [Egyptian] tongue, and said: Teach them a teaching by which no one on earth will overcome them. Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 5/587.
4 The number of magicians was disputed. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: they were eighty thousand. al-Qasim ibn Abi Barrah said: seventy thousand. al-Suddi said: some thirty-odd thousand. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: twelve thousand. And from Ibn Abbas: the magicians were seventy men. (These sayings are cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/158)).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, recounts Pharaoh's reaction to what had happened. He says: ﴿Have you believed in him before I give you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.﴾

It is natural that Pharaoh should fly into a rage after hearing this from his magicians. He had gathered them to support him, but they abandoned him. Worse, they overturned his throne from its foundations by believing in a god other than his. Would that they had kept silent after abandoning him! Instead, they announced it openly, loudly and resoundingly: ﴿We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.﴾ (Ta-Ha)

﴿He said: "Have you believed in him before I give you permission…"﴾ (Ta-Ha): Despite the disappointment that struck him, he still clings to his Pharaonic status and his claim to divinity, and he flees from the humiliation that has befallen him. He wants to present the people with the image of a man who is steadfast and whom these events have not affected. So he said: ﴿Have you believed in him before I give you permission…﴾ (Ta-Ha), meaning: I am your chief who taught you magic. You should have respected my mastery, and I was going to give you permission.

The word ﴿آمنتم﴾ (āmantum, "you believed") derives from the root أ م ن (ʾ-m-n). It occupies a large place in the Noble Qur'an. Its original sense is: أمن فلان أمنا (amina Fulān amnan), meaning "he felt secure, he was at peace," so that nothing frightens him. This root appears in the triliteral form أمن (amina) and in the form augmented by a hamza, آمن (āmana).

This verb may take a direct object, as in the words of God Most High: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and secured them from fear.﴾ (Quraysh). That is, He made the people of Makkah secure from fear.

It may also take the preposition بـ (bi-), as in آمنت بالله (āmantu billāh, "I believed in God"), or the preposition لـ (li-), as in the words of God Most High: ﴿But none believed in Moses except a small portion of his people…﴾ (Yunus). Here آمن له (āmana lahu) means: he affirmed him in what he brought.

So we have: آمنه (āmanahu) means he gave him security; آمن به (āmana bihi) means he held it as a belief; and آمن له (āmana lahu) means he affirmed him.

Sometimes أمن and آمن have the same meaning, as in the words of our master Ya'qub (peace be upon him): ﴿Shall I entrust him to you except as I entrusted his brother to you before…﴾ (Yusuf).

Why did the form change from أمن to آمن?

They said: because his words ﴿…as I entrusted his brother to you before…﴾ (Yusuf) referred to a first experience, so the verb came in its bare form أمن, unlike the second time. The second time required a measure of caution in the matter, so he said ﴿Shall I entrust him to you…﴾ (Yusuf), adding the hamza for caution.

Thus the meaning of Pharaoh's words ﴿Have you believed in him…﴾ (Ta-Ha) is: you affirmed him, you accepted him as true.

Consider here the eloquence of the Qur'an in this expression: ﴿before I give you permission…﴾ (Ta-Ha). Who is saying it? It is Pharaoh, the one who commands and forbids among his people, now speaking of permission. There is a difference between command and permission. To command someone to do something means that you love what you command and that it is obligatory for you to carry it out. Permission, however, may be given for something one does not love or want. He now gives permission because he is no longer able to command.

Since you believed in him before I gave you permission, he must be your chief who taught you magic. Your loyalty to him meant that you respected this seniority and helped him to win.

This is Pharaoh's faulty explanation of the reality of faith. In his view, Moses surpassed them not because he was more skilled in the art of magic than they were, but because they had flattered him and colluded with him, since he was their chief and teacher.

Therefore he threatens them, saying: ﴿So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees…﴾ (Ta-Ha)

This threat and warning came as a punishment for them, because in his view they had defeated him and abandoned him in his decisive battle against Moses, peace be upon him. The meaning of ﴿on opposite sides﴾ (Ta-Ha) is that one thing comes against another. The discussion here concerns hands and feet, so the intended meaning is the right hand with the left foot, or the left hand with the right foot.

As for His words ﴿…and I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ (Ta-Ha): it is well known that crucifixion is done on trunks. For this reason some exegetes sought to escape this difficulty, saying that the particle في (fī, "in") here means على (ʿalā, "upon"). But this interpretation does not befit the highest style of Qur'anic exposition. We must first agree on the meaning of crucifixion (taṣlīb), which is that you bring the one to be crucified, and the wood or iron upright post for example, then you bind the person to this upright post with a strong binding, and tighten it firmly.

You may test this for yourself: tie, for example, a matchstick to your finger and tighten the binding firmly, and you will find that the matchstick enters the flesh. At that point you say: the matchstick is in your finger, not on your finger.

So His words ﴿…and I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees…﴾ (Ta-Ha): the particle في (fī) here retains its original meaning, to indicate emphasis on crucifying firmly, to the point that the crucified person enters into the trunk, as if he is not upon it but within it.

Then He says: ﴿…and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting﴾ (Ta-Ha). "Which of us": the intended parties are Pharaoh and Moses, or Pharaoh and the Lord of Moses who sent him. "More severe in punishment and more lasting": thus punishment is combined in severity with respect to its manner, and in duration and endurance over time. The Qur'an does not mention whether Pharaoh carried out his threat or not, and the closer view is that he did carry out what he threatened.

It would have been expected that Pharaoh's threat would strike fear into the hearts of the magicians and terrify them, so that they would at least try to apologize for what had happened. But nothing of this occurred; rather, they said something that enraged him even more:

al-Ithar (preference): giving one thing precedence over another within a situation of equality. You say: "I preferred so-and-so over so-and-so," when the two are in the same position; or when you have something and no one else has anything like it, then a poor person comes to you and you prefer him over yourself.

From this is the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need.﴾ (al-Hashr: 9).

As for their saying: ﴿We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us and over Him Who created us.﴾ (Ta-Ha: 72): because he (Pharaoh) had said ﴿And you will surely know whose punishment is more severe and more lasting﴾ (Ta-Ha: 71), meaning, "me or Musa?" In his view the contest was with Musa, so they wanted to confront him with this truth that had become clear to all of them: that the contest is not with Musa but with the clear signs of Allah with which Musa was sent. "We will never prefer you over the signs of Allah that have come to us plainly and clearly."

When the magicians saw the miracle of the staff, they became the most believing of the people, and the depth of their faith became evident when they said: ﴿We believe in the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ (Ta-Ha: 70). They did not say, "We believe in Musa and Harun." Thus their faith was sound and sincere from the very first moment.

We have already addressed this matter in the story of Sulayman with the Queen of Saba, when she said: ﴿And I submit with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Naml: 44). She and he are both submitters to Allah; she did not say, "I submit to Sulayman." There is a higher Lord, and all submit to Him.

Therefore, the magicians' saying to Pharaoh, ﴿We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us and over Him Who created us﴾ (Ta-Ha: 72), is a precise, conscious and wise expression. In it you do not notice the personal identity of Musa; rather, you notice the clear proof that Musa brought from Allah.

For this reason Allah Most High says: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist until there came to them the clear evidence﴾ (al-Bayyinah: 1), then He clarifies from whom the clear evidence came: ﴿a Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures﴾ (al-Bayyinah: 2).

So the ascent is from the Messenger, to the clear proof, to the One who gave the clear proof: these are three stages.

Al-bayyinat (the clear proofs): matters that are evident and that settle every dispute about them, so they do not admit argument and wrangling, because their proof is manifest and plain.

As for their saying: ﴿and Him Who created us﴾ (Ta-Ha: 72): meaning, "We will not prefer you also over Allah, Who created us." Or the phrase ﴿and Him Who created us﴾ may be an oath on what they say, as you say, "I will not do such-and-such, by Him Who created you," so you swear that you will not do this thing.

This is the basis for their not turning back from what they said, which is belief in the Lord of Harun and Musa.

Then they did not neglect to allude to the matter of Pharaoh's threats: ﴿Then I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees﴾ (Ta-Ha: 71).

Therefore they say: ﴿So decree whatever you will decree﴾ (Ta-Ha: 72), meaning: carry out what you have judged of cutting off hands and feet, or decree whatever other matters you decree, and do what you wish; these threats no longer frighten us. ﴿You can only decree concerning this worldly life﴾ (Ta-Ha: 72).

You are a human being who may die at any time, so you can only decide during the span of your life. Perhaps someone will come after you who is better than you, and he will not claim the divinity you claimed.

Suppose that whoever comes after you is like you: his life too will come to an end. And even if what you have set as a practice for people, claiming divinity, continues until the Day of Resurrection, and the tyranny of others extends after you, the matter will still end, even if only with the coming of the Hour.

As we said before: the pleasure of this world, however great it is, is threatened by one of two things: either you miss it or it misses you. But the pleasure of the Hereafter is lasting and eternal; it neither escapes you nor do you escape it.

1 Infakka (انفك): separated and parted from its former state. Allah Most High said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist...﴾ (al-Bayyinah: 1), meaning: they would not cease or separate from what they were in until the clear evidence came to them. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/87).

Then the Exalted says:

﴿Indeed we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic to which you compelled us. And Allah is better and more enduring.﴾ (20:73)

Since we have turned from faith in humans to faith in the Creator of humans, this is sound thinking on our part, and you may not blame us for it. Then they explain the basis of their faith: ﴿that He may forgive us our sins and the magic to which you compelled us..﴾ (20:73). So faith in Allah will benefit us; He will forgive us our sins, which are many, and will forgive us what you compelled us to do regarding magic. They practised magic under compulsion and performed it under force, so it was an act that did not match their nature, their makeup, or their innate disposition (fitrah).

How often are people compelled to do things they do not approve of, and carry out orders while not convinced by them, especially in the eras of tyrants and oppressors! We have heard much about jailers in detention centres: one of them would receive orders to torture so-and-so, and what could he do, knowing that the man is innocent and wronged, and his heart does not allow him to torture him? So he would enter upon the prisoner and say to him, "Scream at the top of your voice," pretending that he was beating him.

Then they say: ﴿And Allah is better and more enduring.﴾ (20:73). You will pass away; indeed, your whole worldly life will pass away at the hands of the tyrants who come after you, and nothing will remain but Allah. He, glorified is He, provides for all His creatures in this world through means (asbab), but in the Hereafter they will not live by means; rather by the Causer (al-Musabbib), Mighty and Majestic, without means.

Therefore, when a thing occurs to your mind, you find it before you; this is the bliss of the Hereafter, and the civilisations of this world will never reach it, however far their development advances.

Likewise, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and becomes beautiful, and its people suppose that they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day..﴾ (10:24), however much humans suppose that they are capable of everything in their worldly life, they are weak and cannot preserve what they have attained.

So, make Allah, blessed and exalted is He, constantly in your mind; He will be your compensation for everything you lose, and be ashamed that He should see you while you disobey Him. A hadith qudsi has been transmitted: ("If you believe that I do not see you, then the flaw is in your faith; and if you believe that I see you, then why have you made Me the most insignificant of those who look at you?!")(1).

When one of the knowers ('arifin) was asked, "How did you spend your life?", he said: "In four things: I knew that I am never free from the gaze of Allah the Exalted for the blink of an eye, so I was ashamed to disobey Him; I knew that I have a provision that will not pass me by, and Allah has guaranteed it to me, so I was content with it; I knew that I have a debt that no one else will pay on my behalf, so I busied myself with it; and I knew that I have a term that hastens toward me, so I hastened to it."

One of the knowers explained these four, saying: "Make your watchfulness (muraqabah) toward the One from whose gaze you are never free; make your gratitude toward the One whose blessings never cease to reach you; make your obedience toward the One from whom you can never be independent; and make your submission toward the One whose dominion and authority you can never leave."

Thus these eight sayings comprise the entire religion.

(1) Research in the books of hadith has shown that this hadith is not established with this wording. Rather, a portion of it is established on the tongue of some of the knowers ('arifin). It appears in the book Hilyat al-Awliya' (8/142): a man said to Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, "Fear Allah lest Allah become the most insignificant of those who look at you." It also appears in Jami' al-'Ulum wa'l-Hikam (1/36): one of the knowers said, "Fear Allah lest He become the most insignificant of those who look at you..."

Then the sorcerers who had declared their faith presented the grounds for this faith, saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.﴾ (20:74).

His saying: ﴿Whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal...﴾ (20:74): That is, a criminal who committed a crime. A crime is to break one of the laws of the Truth, Exalted is He, as humans do in their laws, where they set a punishment for whoever deviates from these laws. However, this crime should be specified and announced to the people, so that when someone falls into the crime, the warning has been given and the excuse has been established (fa-qad a'dhara man andhar, "he who has given warning has made his excuse").

Thus: no one can be punished except for a crime, and there is no crime except by a text (nass).

His saying: (yati, "comes"): that is, he is the one who will come despite his criminality and despite the torment that awaits him. But why did they address him with the word "criminality"? Because he said: ﴿Then I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees...﴾ (20:71), while they had done nothing more than speak the word of truth. So which of us, then, is the criminal?

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.﴾ (20:74):

Because death would relieve them of the torment; therefore they wish for death, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!" ...﴾ (43:77), so his response comes: ﴿Indeed, you will remain.﴾ (43:77).

There is a difference between torment and death. Death is the ending of life, and after death there is no pain, whereas torment does not arise except with life, because it is the pain of a living being.

Therefore, when the Truth, Blessed and Exalted is He, addressed this matter in the story of Solomon, peace be upon him, and the hoopoe, and Solomon said: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter him...﴾ (27:21), then torment is one thing and slaughter is another, because slaughter is the ending of sentient life.

The meaning of: ﴿He will neither die therein nor live.﴾ (20:74) is that there is a stage and a cycle between death and life, in which he does not die and so find rest, nor does he live a life free from torment. Their dwelling in Hell is in this stage, which is neither death nor life.

Thus it seems they were pointing, with their words, "Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal..." (Ta-Ha 20:74), to Pharaoh, whereas now they point to themselves and to the path of faith they have taken: ﴿And whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds...﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:75).

So they combined faith and righteous action, because faith is the inner wellspring from which the impulsive movements proceed in accordance with the method in which one has believed. Otherwise, what benefit is there in believing in something without working for it? The Qur'an often combines those who believed and did righteous deeds.

As for His saying: ﴿Then for them are the high ranks (al-darajat al-ula)﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:75): "the ranks" means the ranks of Paradise. Paradise has ranks, some above others, whereas the Fire has levels (darakat), some beneath others.

Al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, made Paradise into ranks because its people differ in their deeds(1), just as they differ even in a single deed, since the measure of sincerity in an action varies.

Therefore it came in a report (athar): "People are in peril, except those who have knowledge; those who have knowledge are in peril, except those who act; those who act are in peril, except the sincere; and the sincere are in great peril."

And al-ʿUlā is the plural of ʿulyā (higher). So what are the high ranks?

1. Ibn al-Mubarak related in al-Zuhd (p. 33) (no. 99), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya (4/247), from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "Indeed Allah causes a people to enter Paradise and gives them until they tire of it. Above them are people in the high ranks. When they look at them, they recognize them and say: 'Our Lord, our brothers, we were with them. Why have you favored them over us?' It is said: 'Far from it! They used to go hungry when you were full, thirst when you were quenched, stand in prayer when you slept, and remain awake when you lowered your eyes...'"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 20, verse 76:

ʿAdn: that is, residence (iqamah). One says ʿadana fi al-makan: he resided in the place. So the meaning is gardens prepared for your residence. There is a difference between preparing a place for residence and preparing a place for a passerby, just as the preparation and luxury of a place differ according to the one who prepares it and his capabilities. An ordinary person prepares a place different from the one a great man prepares, so what then of a place that your Lord—Mighty and Majestic—has prepared for you with His power and capabilities?

And His saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever﴾ (20:76):

We know that water is one of the most important requisites of life in this world. By it the earth brings forth vegetation, in it nutritive elements dissolve, and without it no life can stand on the face of the earth. When the Truth, glorified and exalted, sends down rain from the sky, the one upon whom the rain falls may not benefit from it; it may fall, for example, on a mountain. The Nile, on whose water we live, where does it come from? From Ethiopia and elsewhere.

Therefore the Creator—Mighty and Majestic—made the phrase ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ (20:76) a symbol of greenery, freshness, growth, and a happy, pleasant life. Even a person who does not need food, for instance because he is full, finds pleasure in looking at green nature and what it contains of crops, roses and flowers. Crops are not only for eating but for looking at as well. Even if you eat three times a day, food is nourishment for the body, while you enjoy and take delight in a beautiful view whenever you look at it. Looking is a pleasure for the soul and a joy for the self.

As if the Truth—blessed and exalted—is saying to us: do not limit your benefit from God's blessings to what you possess, saying, for example: "I will not eat this fruit because it is not mine," for there is another pleasure: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and ripens﴾ (6:99). So before you eat, look; looking is a pleasure and a continuous nourishment.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ (20:76): because the phenomenon of rivers flowing in this world is a means of greenery, fertility and ripening. And ﴿beneath them﴾ (20:76) means: the water is inherent in them and springs forth from them, not flowing to you from another place where it may be withheld from you or you may be deprived of it.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says in another verse: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ (9:100). So beneath them are flowing rivers, but their source and origin is from another place.

The flowing is attributed to the river, not to the water, for emphasis, since the river is the channel in which the water flows.

Then He says: ﴿wherein they will abide forever﴾ (20:76). This is the true guarantee of bliss, for the bane of blessings is that they cease, either by your losing them or by them losing you. But the bliss of Paradise God, exalted is He, has safeguarded from this bane; it is eternal and everlasting, neither ceasing nor being taken away from its people.

﴿And that is the recompense of one who purifies himself﴾ (20:76): zakah is applied to purity and to growth. Purity is that a thing is pure in its essence; growth is that it possesses a quality of increase so that it grows beyond what you see it to be.

As you see, for example, the artificial rose and the natural rose in a garden: the natural rose has moisture, freshness, a pleasant fragrance, various colours and growth, all of which are essential attributes of the rose, unlike the artificial rose, which remains fixed in one state.

This is the difference between the making of humans and the making of the Creator of humans. Therefore God's making is more enduring and longer-lasting, and God the Mighty spoke truly when He said: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ (23:14).

You notice that He did not withhold from you the attribute of creating; for you used the means and exercised thought, so you have some share of creating, but your Lord is the best of creators, because you create from something He created; you create from something existing, whereas He creates from nothing. You create a lifeless, inert thing, whereas He creates a living, growing thing that reproduces by its own nature.

From here the wealth you give to the poor is called zakah, because it purifies what remains and makes it grow. Among the wonders is that God called what is paid out of wealth zakah and growth, and called the increase of usury a erasure (mahq).

So the meaning of ﴿And that is the recompense of one who purifies himself﴾ (20:76) is: he purified himself from sins, then developed his self. The meaning of development is the ascents of the believer through the degrees of arriving at the Truth; he is a believer at the beginning, but his faith increases, grows and ascends day after day. Whenever his faith increases, his nearness to his Lord increases, and God's overflowing bounties upon him increase. Purification of things precedes their development, because averting harm takes precedence over attracting benefit.

Thus: he purified himself means he first cleansed it, then he developed it second. It is like one who wants to trade: he must first bring pure capital from lawful sources and then grow it; you do not bring capital defiled and then grow it with its defilement.

Whenever a person develops his faith, he rises in its degrees, and so he will have the highest degrees in the Hereafter.

¹ Aynaʿ al-thamar: it ripened, matured and its time of picking arrived. Its adjective is yāniʿ, meaning ripe. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and ripens (wa yanʿihi)﴾ (6:99), that is, its ripening and the difference of its taste after ripening. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/373).

This was revelation to Musa (peace be upon him) after the battle had ended and the camp of faith had been victorious in it, whereas Fir'awn had lost one of the most important of his weapons and a great part of his dominance and tyranny.

Here Musa gathered the Children of Israel, who were the remnants of the descendants of the family of Ya'qub, to take them to the Promised Land. Swiftly, Fir'awn prepared his army and gathered his hosts, and set out behind them, following them to the seashore. Then Musa and his people found themselves besieged: the sea in front of them, and Fir'awn with his army behind them, and they had no way out of this predicament.

This is the judgment of human affairs when they are isolated from the Lord of mankind. But in the view of the believer, they have a solution, because his affairs are not isolated from his Lord and Creator. For when a believer is struck by a calamity, or touched by some harm, he looks and finds his Lord watching over him, so he turns to Him and finds rest in His protection.

Therefore they say: "There is no distress while You are Lord." As long as I have a Lord to turn to, there is no dilemma; the dilemma is for one who has no Lord to turn to.

We have given an example of this – and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: if a man has a pound coin in his pocket and it falls from him on the road, then if he has no other, he grieves; but if he has other money, he will find in it a replacement for what was lost. This reserve that you keep is your faith in Allah.

Here the command came from Allah, exalted is He, to Musa (peace be upon him) to bring him and his people out of this predicament: ﴿That go by night with My servants, and strike for them a dry path through the sea.. (77)﴾ (Ta-Ha).

Asri (أسر): from al-israʾ, meaning travelling by night, i.e., journeying; because it is more concealing for the traveller.

And His words ﴿bi-ʿibadi.. (77)﴾ (Ta-Ha), "with My servants": the word ʿabd (عبد) is pluralised as ʿabid (عبيد) and ʿibad (عباد), and the difference between them is that everyone in the universe is an ʿabid of Allah, the Exalted, because although they are free to choose in some matters, they are compelled in other matters. So whoever habitually and by choice opposes the method of Allah and has practised that, has compulsions such as sickness or death.

As for the ʿibad, they are the elite who chose Allah's will over their own will and His choice over their choice; for [regarding] His offer: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve.. (29)﴾ (al-Kahf), they left their own choice for the choice of their Lord.

Therefore Allah attributed them to Himself, saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants – you have no authority over them.. (42)﴾ (al-Hijr). And He said about them: ﴿Honoured servants (26)﴾ (al-Anbiya'). And He said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility.. (63)﴾ (al-Furqan).

The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And strike for them a dry path through the sea.. (77)﴾ (Ta-Ha): that is, dry and parched in the midst of the water.

And ḍarb (الضرب): the infliction of something by a striker with an instrument upon a struck object; from it is ḍarb al-ʿumla (ضرب العملة), meaning minting and stamping it, so that after being a piece of metal it becomes a circulating currency.

Musa struck the sea with his staff, and the sea split, and the water receded from a dry path suitable for walking on foot. This is a matter that human law cannot conceive of; therefore his Lord reassures him: ﴿Do not fear being overtaken.. (77)﴾ (Ta-Ha): that is, from Fir'awn overtaking you; ﴿nor fear [drowning] (77)﴾ (Ta-Ha): that is, drowning in the sea, because the path is struck, that is, prepared, levelled and suitable for this task.

This is another miracle of Musa's staff, which he cast down so that it became a moving serpent, and he struck the sea with it so that it split, and what was beneath the staff became a dry road, while what was around it became mountains: ﴿Every portion was like a great mountain (63)﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). It is also the staff with which he struck the rock, from which water gushed forth.

The context here does not mention anything of the dialogue that took place between Musa and his people when they fell into this straits; but it appears in another snapshot of the story, where Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So when the two groups saw each other, the companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are overtaken!" (61) He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me." (62)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

With the multiplicity of snapshots in the Qur'an, the general picture of the story is completed, and there is no repetition in that, as some imagine.

So before He revealed to him: ﴿strike for them a dry path through the sea.. (77)﴾ (Ta-Ha), the people said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken! (61)﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). He said: "No!" But how could he say it with the assurance of one confident, when what they feared was likely to befall them within a moment?

We say: because he did not say "No" from himself; he did not say it by the law of men, but by the law of the Creator of men: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me (62)﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). So I do not deceive you, and I am not isolated from heaven and the guidance of my Lord.

1 al-Tawd (الطود): the firm, high mountain. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/408)
2 al-Bajs (البجس): a split in a waterskin, a rock or the earth from which water springs forth. And infabaja al-ma' (انبجس الماء): it gushed out. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We revealed to Musa, when his people asked him for water, "Strike with your staff the rock," and there gushed forth from it twelve springs...(160)﴾ (al-A'raf).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts, and there covered them of the sea that which covered them.﴾

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Then there covered them of the sea that which covered them (78)﴾ (Ta-Ha). "Ghashiyahum" means: the water covered them. The event has been left vague to indicate its terror and awfulness, and that it exceeds all limitation and description, just as you say of a matter you cannot detail: "What happened, happened."

In another scene of this event, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, shows that Musa, peace be upon him, after he had crossed with his people in safety, wanted, by his own judgement and his inclinations of faith, to strike the sea once more so that it would return to its flowing state and Pharaoh would be unable to catch up with him. But the directives of his Lord had a different matter in view.

So Allah revealed to him: ﴿And leave the sea at rest (rahwan); indeed they are an army to be drowned (24)﴾ (al-Dukhan).

That is: leave it as it is, do not return it to its flowing course. Just as I saved you by the water, I will destroy your enemy by the water. Glory be to the One who saves and destroys by one and the same thing.

Footnote 1: "Rahw al-bahr rahwan": the sea became calm, so it is "rahin" (still). His saying: ﴿And leave the sea at rest (rahwan) ... (24)﴾ (al-Dukhan) means: leave it with its waves still, so that they are deceived and descend into it. Or: be calm, O Musa, at ease in the certainty of deliverance (al-Qamus al-Qawim, 1/279).

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And Pharaoh led his people astray, and did not guide them﴾ (20:79).

It has already been mentioned that Pharaoh said to his people: ﴿And I show you only the way of right guidance﴾ (40:29).

So where is the way of right guidance that Pharaoh spoke of, after Allah closed the sea over them? He drove them to destruction, and did not lead them along the path of salvation and guidance. Therefore you, [O Pharaoh], are a liar in your claim of the way of right guidance, for you led them astray and did not guide them, and you destroyed them and did not save them.

Then the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you at the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails.﴾

God, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed on the Children of Israel many favours and blessings that cannot be counted. The requirement of the worship by which He described them, ﴿that you bring out My servants by night…﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:77), was that they should carry out the method of their Lord and keep His blessing in mind in a way that never leaves their hearts, so that whenever their souls moved toward disobedience, they would recall a blessing of God upon them, and remember that they were not volunteering their faith, but were merely returning to God what He had bestowed upon them of blessings and graces.

Here the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, reminds them of some of His blessings, and addresses them with the most beloved form of address: ﴿O Children of Israel…﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:80). Israel means "servant of God," His sincere servant. It is as when you say to your companion, "O son of the good, pious man." So the Truth reminds them of their good origin, and attributes them to one of His prophets, as if to draw their attention that opposition and departure from the method are not befitting for you, since you are the lineage of this righteous man.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We delivered you from your enemy…﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:80), that is, from Pharaoh, who humiliated you, slaughtered your sons, spared your women, enslaved them in labour without wages, and did to you all manner of evils. Then ﴿and We made a covenant with you at the right side of the Mount…﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:80), so that you might take the sound method for the movement of life. Thus: We rescued you from harm, and made a covenant with you for a blessing.

﴿And We made a covenant with you…﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:80): "wa'ada" (to promise, make a covenant) is a form of mufa'ala (reciprocal form), which is not usually found except between two parties, like "shaːraka" (to share) and "khasama" (to quarrel). Was the promise then from both sides together: God, Mighty and Majestic, and the Children of Israel? The promise was from God, Exalted, yet the Qur'an did not say "We promised you," but rather associated the Children of Israel in the promise. This alerts us that when a person promises you something and you agree, it is as if you have entered into the promise.

"The right side of the Mount" is the place where the method of heaven was received; it is a remote place in the desert, with no crops and no water. Therefore their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, guaranteed them what would sustain them: ﴿And We sent down to you manna and quails﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:80).

Manna: a white substance resembling honey, falling like crystalline drops resembling dew on the leaves of trees; in the morning they gather it as sweet food. This blessing still exists in Iraq, for example, and a large industry is built upon it, the manna industry.

Quails (salwa): a bird resembling the common quail.

Thus the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, provided for them the means of life: this sugary substance, pleasant in taste, combining cream with bee honey, and a delicious bird, without effort or exertion on their part; they found it before them prepared and ready. It was expected of them to thank God for His blessing upon them, but they objected to it and said: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us of what the earth grows—its herbs, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, and onions.' He said: 'Would you exchange what is lower for what is better?'﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:61).

In Surat al-Baqarah, along with this blessing that accompanied them in the barrenness of the desert, another blessing is mentioned: ﴿And We shaded you with the clouds and sent down to you manna and quails…﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:57), that is, We shielded you from the glare and heat of the sun as you travelled through this desert.

We notice the difference of context here ("nazzalna") and in al-Baqarah He says ("anzalna"). That is because the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, treats the subject in different shots from all its angles: His saying "anzalna" indicates the first transitivity of the verb, and it may come once; whereas "nazzalna" indicates successive sending down.

The people of the countryside in our lands call "manna" a substance inclining to dark red, which then turns black and falls upon plants; but it is not a blessing, rather it is considered one of the harmful blights of plants.

1 Al-Manna: dew that descends from heaven resembling honey; it used to descend upon the Children of Israel effortlessly, without treatment, so they would wake to it and take it according to their wish. (Lisan al-Arab – root: m-n-n).
2 Al-Salwa: a white bird like the quail. (Lisan al-Arab – root: s-l-a). Said in al-Qamus al-Qawim li-l-Qur'an al-Karim (1/326): (It is the quail, a small bird of the gallinaceous order, plump-bodied, one of the migratory birds from Europe in winter to warm lands; those that survive return in early summer to their homeland in Europe. It is good food, its meat like pigeon's or even tastier; the people of al-Arish in North Sinai are famous for hunting it).
3 Istahya al-nisa': spared them and did not kill them. (Lisan al-Arab – root: h-y-y).
4 Al-baql: a herbaceous plant that is eaten or whose seeds are eaten, or: everything the earth turns green with. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/78).
Al-qitha': the cucumber, and it is well known to be larger and longer than the cucumber and different from it, though both are of one family. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/101).
Al-fawm: it is garlic, one of the appetizing foods; there are other opinions about it. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/92).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Eat of the good things We have provided for you, and do not transgress therein, lest My wrath descend upon you. And whoever has My wrath descend upon him has indeed fallen.﴾

Food, drink and air are the necessities of life which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guaranteed for us. The command to eat here is one of permissibility (ibahah), and it is not an obligation upon you to eat, except when you wish to abstain from food in a way that harms your life; then you are compelled to eat.

As for His saying: ﴿of the good things We have provided for you...﴾: He specified the good things, because provision (rizq) includes both what is good and what is not good. Provision is everything from which you benefit, even if it is unlawful, meaning that what you have obtained from the unlawful is also part of your provision, except that you hastened to it through the unlawful. Had you been patient with it and kept yourself chaste from it, you would have gained multiples of it in the lawful.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and do not transgress therein...﴾. In the verse of al-Baqarah, ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ (al-Nahl 16:118). So it seems that the cause of wronging oneself is that they transgressed in eating from the provision.

Tughyan (transgression) comes from "taghā al-shay'" when a thing exceeds its familiar limit from which one benefits. Among its uses is the flooding of water when it exceeds the limit that removes thirst and dryness, to the point that it drowns, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ (al-Haqqah 69:11). That is: it passed the limit at which one benefits and reached ruin and destruction.

So it is with any limit. But how can exceeding the limit occur in food and sustenance?

When Allah, blessed and exalted is He, created the earth, He measured in it its sustenance until the Day of Resurrection, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He placed therein its sustenance, measured in four days...﴾ (Fussilat 41:10).

So be reassured about this matter. When you see that the earth does not yield, do not accuse it; rather, accuse yourselves of negligence and idleness in cultivating and farming the earth, as Allah has commanded you: ﴿He produced you from the earth and settled you therein﴾ (Hud 11:61).

For a time we neglected this matter, until events surprised us with a large number and little support, so there was the going out to the desert and its cultivation.

Since the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, created our provisions and the necessities of our life, and made them suitable for this human being whom He honoured and made His vicegerent on earth, and made for this provision and these necessities limits that He set and explained, which are the lawful (halal), it is not fitting for you, after that, to exceed these limits and transgress in taking your food and drink.

We see even the machines that people have made: each has its own fuel, and if you give it other than that, it does not perform its task. For example, if you put diesel in an aircraft it will not move, because it is not the fuel suited to its nature.

So: your limits in the necessities of your life are the lawful. If we survey what Allah has made lawful and unlawful, we find that the original state of things is that they are lawful, and the abundant is what is permitted to you, while what is forbidden to you is the few, confined and identifiable.

Therefore the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you...﴾ (al-An'am 6:151). He did not say in another verse, for example: "Come, I will recite what Allah has made lawful for you," because that matter would be long and uncountable.

So: whenever your Lord gives you, He says: this is your lawful, pure provision, and from it come your fuel and the necessities of your life, and by it your survival and the vigour of your movement. Do not, then, pass from the lawful, despite its abundance, to the unlawful, despite its scarcity and its confinement to several kinds, which He has explained to you and warned you against.

Through nourishment the process of metabolism (al-ayd, meaning: demolition and construction) takes place in the body, and it is a continuous process at every moment of your life. So beware of building a single atom of your atoms from the unlawful, for that atom of the unlawful will continue to trouble you and press upon you so as to bring you down to its origin.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, Allah is Good and accepts only the good. Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, so He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and act righteously; indeed I am Knowing of what you do﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:51), and He said: ﴿O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:172)." Then he mentioned a man who prolongs the journey, dishevelled and dusty, who raises his hands to the sky: "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he is nourished with the unlawful; so how could that be answered?"

That is because the atoms of his construction are not harmonious, since they grew upon the fuel of what Allah had not made lawful for him.

Therefore you hear from some of the quibblers: since Allah created the pig, why did He forbid it? We say: you have understood that every created thing was created to be eaten, and this is not correct. Allah created petroleum, with which machines run; can you drink it as you drink a car?

So: there is a difference between a thing created for one purpose and you directing it to another. This is called ihalah, that is, transferring a thing to other than that for which it was made, and this is the transgression in sustenance, because you have moved the unlawful to the lawful.

Transgression may also come in another form: that you eat of the good things Allah has made lawful, but you obtain them by an illegitimate way, and you accustom yourself to idleness in lawful earning, so you take the effort of others and live as a burden upon them. Besides that you feed yourself on the unlawful, you also discourage others from movement, production and ownership. What benefit is there in a person labouring while another takes the fruit of his labour?

This kind of transgression has taken many forms in our societies. We can classify under it: usurpation (ghasb), abduction (khatf), theft (sariqah), embezzlement (ikhtilas), bribery (rashwah), breach of trust (khiyanat al-amanah), deceiving one who has hired you, and so on, from taking people's wealth falsely and without any right. Each of these transgressions has its own form.

Abduction (khatf) is that you snatch another's property while it is not within the grasp of its owner, and then you flee with it. If it was within his grasp and you overcame him and took it by force, it is ghasb, derived from "ghasab al-jild 'an al-shah," meaning to strip the hide from the sheep. If the property was taken secretly while in its keeping, it is theft (sariqah). If you were entrusted with property in your hands and took from it secretly, it is embezzlement (ikhtilas), etc.

So: Allah has made some things lawful for you and forbidden others to you. If a thing is lawful in itself, do not take it except by its right, so that each of us respects the work and movement of the other in life and his ownership of things. By this the movement of life is made upright, everyone is happy, we help the spender, and we restrain the lawless bully.

Islam has a sound method for eliminating unemployment, which some modern systems now adopt: the Shari'ah commands, to eliminate unemployment, that one dig a well and then fill it in; that is, dig it and refill it, then give the labourer who did it his wage. How so? You dig the well and gain nothing from it and then fill it in; what is the benefit? Why not give the labourer his wage without digging and without filling?

They said: so that he does not become accustomed to idleness and laziness, and so that he eats only from his sweat and effort; otherwise society would be corrupted.

There is another form of transgression in sustenance: that you use the strength which Allah made your sustenance for in beneficial movement of life, and yet you spend that strength which Allah bestowed upon you in disobedience to Him.

Thus transgression was the cause of ﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ (al-Nahl 16:118): that is, by punishment; ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾ (al-Nahl 16:118): that is, by transgression.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿...lest My wrath descend upon you﴾. The verb halla, yahullu, can mean "became lawful," as one says to a thief: "lawful for him is prison" (halala fihi al-sijn). It can also mean "alighted in a place," as one says "halla bi-al-makan," meaning he alighted there. So the meaning of ﴿lest My wrath descend upon you﴾ is: "become lawful," that is, it became due and incumbent upon you; or: "alight upon you." And the meaning may be more general than all of this.

Anger (ghadab) is a psychological emotion which produces a change in the body's chemistry, so you see the angry person's veins swell, his face reddens, and his features change; these are changes accompanying this emotion. Is the anger of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of this kind?

Certainly not, for He, exalted is He, has no changes. And if anger is proportionate to the angry one's power to punish, then what of when the anger is from Allah?

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And whoever has My wrath descend upon him has indeed fallen﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:81).

The root h-w-y has two usages. The first: hawa yahwi, meaning to fall from a height in a fall one has no will to prevent, as when one suddenly falls from a roof, for example. From this is the verse of the poet:

* "The bucket fell, its rope abandoned it" *

when the rope that brings up the bucket breaks.

The other: hawa yahwa, meaning to love.

So the meaning of ﴿has indeed fallen﴾ is: he fell to the bottom in a fall that leaves him no worth in life, or he falls in this world and continues to fall in the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿Then his mother is the Abyss (hawiyah)﴾ (al-Qari'ah 101:9). His mother, the source of his tenderness, is the Abyss; how then will it be with him when he falls into the Abyss?

All of these are admonitions and exhortations for the believer, which the Truth, glorified is He, makes clear to him so that he may build the movement of his life by their light and guidance.

Since man is subject to changes, not remaining in one state, moving between health and sickness, between wealth and poverty, everything in him is bestowed upon him and not intrinsic to him. Therefore beware of grieving when some blessing escapes you, for it will not remain or endure. Suppose you have reached the peak of bliss; what then do you await but that it will pass, as the poet said:

"When a thing is complete, its deficiency appears; it awaits decline once it is said to be complete."

So when a thing is complete for you, and you are a son of changes, and no state endures for you, you must descend to the other side.

Thus the deficiency in a person's hopes in life is an amulet guarding blessings, and whatever defect or flaw is in him repels the envy of the envier, as the poet said in praise:

"The eyes of people have turned towards your perfection; so seek refuge from the evil of their eyes in a single defect."

That is: the eyes are fixed upon you, so turn them away, even with one defect which people mention and busy themselves with.

In the countryside some peasants live by their natural disposition: if one of them has a beautiful, handsome son who attracts people's attention, you find them deliberately neglecting his appearance and cleanliness, or they put a "fasukha" on him to ward off envy and the evil eye.

So too the woman who entered upon the Caliph and said: "May Allah complete His blessing upon you and gladden your eye." The attendees understood she was supplicating for him. When she left, the Caliph said: "Did you understand what the woman said?" They said: "She prays for you." He said: "Rather, she prays against me, for by her saying 'May Allah complete His blessing upon you' she wants its removal, since when a blessing is completed nothing remains for it but to vanish; and her saying 'May Allah gladden your eye' means: make it still from movement."

So: do not be angry if they say about you that you are deficient in something; this deficiency is the amulet of perfection, and Allah wants it for you for your own benefit.

And since man is a son of changes, he must inevitably be heedless of the way of Allah, so there will be lapses and slips that need forgiveness. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And indeed I am Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does righteousness, and then remains guided﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:82).
