Therefore they are cited as a proverb for permanence, as in the saying of the Truth, glorified: ﴿And they have planned their plan, but their plan is with Allah, even if their plan was such that the mountains would be moved by it (46)﴾ (Ibrahim).

So the mountains are a manifestation of permanence. Thus one may ask about this firm, stable creation: what will Allah do with it?

1 Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/427): (That is, most people have no knowledge except of the world and its gains, affairs and what is in it; they are clever and astute in acquiring it and in the ways of earning it, while they are heedless of matters of religion and what benefits them in the Hereafter, as if one of them were a fool with no mind and no thought).
2 Al-ahilla: plural of hilal. The hilal: the moon at its first appearance at the beginning of the Arabic month. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/305).
3 Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7288) and al-Daraqutni in his Sunan (2/281) with the wording "da'uni", and it was reported by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/313, 482, 495), and Muslim in his Sahih (1337) with the wording "dharuni", from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿So He will leave it a smooth, level plain﴾:

﴿A smooth, level plain (106)﴾ (Ta-Ha): a level, smooth ground with no vegetation and no buildings. The pronoun in ﴿So He will leave it… (106)﴾ (Ta-Ha) refers to the earth, not to the mountains, because the mountains cannot be a smooth, level plain. Rather, the earth in place of the mountains becomes smooth and level, with no buildings and no mountains in it. The earth is one thing, and the mountains above it are another thing.

Among the same examples is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed on it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask (10)﴾ (Fussilat).

The pronoun in ﴿and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance… (10)﴾ (Fussilat) does not refer to the earth, but to the mountains. For the mountains in reality are the storehouses of sustenance and the source of fertility for the earth, which is the source of sustenance. Man was created from the earth, and the preservation of his life comes from the earth; vegetation is sustenance for man and for animals, and vegetation and animals are sustenance for man.

Therefore: the earth must have a fertility that supports it and supplies it with the elements of nourishment. Had the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, made the earth as one single layer containing the fertilizing elements, that layer would have been exhausted after several years, and the earth would have become barren thereafter.

Therefore: God created the mountains for a wisdom, and made them a source of fertility that supplies the earth with continuous and sustained supply as long as life remains on the earth. From here the wisdom of the Creator, glorified be He, becomes clear in that the mountains are solid, deaf rock; when they are exposed to the agents of erosion over the course of years, the outer layer crumbles away as a result of the changing climatic conditions of heat and cold.

Then the rains come and work on the rock like a file, forming what is called silt (al-ghareen) (4). They carry these fragments to the valleys and riverbeds and spread them over the surface of the earth, increasing its fertility gradually every year. Otherwise, if the mountains were brittle and not cohesive, they would collapse within a few years and would not fulfil this purpose. Therefore we say: the mountains are the source of sustenance, not the earth.

Do you not see that the fertility of the valley and the delta came from the Nile's silt, and the alluvium that the water carries from the highlands of Africa? This alluvium that is eroded from the mountains is what causes the increase in the area of dry land, and you can observe this phenomenon in cities overlooking the sea: after they were on its shore, they are now inland.

We have previously illustrated the mountain as a triangle whose base is downward, and the valley as a triangle whose base is upward; every erosion of the mountain is an increase in the valley, as though the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, made this phenomenon to be proportionate to the increase of population on the earth.

The returning pronoun has been omitted in ﴿So He will leave it… (106)﴾ (Ta-Ha), relying on the listener's mind and his perceptiveness that it can only be that, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is God, One (1)﴾ (al-Ikhlas). The pronoun's referent ("He") is not mentioned, because when it is said it can only refer to the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, even though His name has not preceded it.

And as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿until it was hidden behind the veil (32)﴾ (Sad). The intended meaning is the sun, which had set, so that Solomon, peace be upon him, missed the prayer; the verse does not mention anything about the sun.

Likewise in: ﴿He leaves not upon its back any creature… (45)﴾ (Fatir): i.e., upon the earth, though the verse does not mention it. Similarly here ("He will leave it") means the earth.

1 The "ṣafṣaf" earth: the smooth, level ground. Al-Farra' said: ṣafṣaf is that which has no vegetation (Lisan al-'Arab – root ṣ-f-ṣ-f).
2 Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/93): (That is, Sunday and Monday).
3 Qatada and Mujahid said: He created in it its rivers, trees and animals. As-Suddi and al-Hasan said: the provisions of its people and their welfare. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 9/6007).
4 Al-ghareen: the mud which the torrent carries and which remains on the surface of the earth, moist or dry. Al-Asma'i said: al-ghareen is when the flood comes and settles on the earth; when it dries you see a thin mud on the surface of the earth that has cracked. (Lisan al-'Arab – root gh-r-n).
5 Mentioned by al-Suyuti in his book al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an (3/186) among the examples of "omission of the agent" in the section "Types of omission", and he said: (It is not permitted except for the agent of a verbal noun).

Meaning: it is as though it is level according to the water-level (mizan al-ma'), with no crookedness visible in it and no "amt" (mizan al-ma') — that is, no lowness or height — so it is perfectly level, just as we do with a wall, striving for its evenness.

Therefore, we see that when an engineer wants to take over a building from the contractor, he relies either on a beam of light, because it is straight and reveals to him the slightest defect in the wall, or on particles of dust, because they settle in a straight line. After a few days, one can observe from the dust particles any twists or bumps in the wall.

Then the Exalted Lord says: ﴿On that Day they will follow the summoner, with no deviation from him, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾.

Al-Da'i: the caller, the one who proclaims, like the muezzin who often calls people to the presence of God, the Exalted, for prayer. Some of them answer the call, and some of them refuse and turn away. As for the summoner in the Hereafter, who is the one who blows the Trumpet (al-Sur), no one will refuse him, and no one will be able to abstain from answering him.

His saying: ﴿with no deviation from him﴾ (Ta-Ha 108): This is because we see the caller of this world, when he calls out to a gathering of people, turning right and turning left, and turning around so that he can be heard in every direction. If his voice does not reach every ear, he uses a loudspeaker, for example. As for the summoner in the Hereafter, there is no deviation from him here or there, because he is heard by all, and his voice reaches every ear, without deflection or inclination.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾ (Ta-Ha 108). This whisper is what He spoke of in the preceding verse: ﴿They will whisper among themselves...﴾ (Ta-Ha 103). We know that in every large gathering it is impossible to control the noise of voices, so how much more so in a gathering like the gathering of the Resurrection, from Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour is established. Yet ﴿voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾ (Ta-Ha 108). Why, then, have these voices been silenced, voices that had so often said what they desired and that had so often been full of clamour and uproar?

The situation now is different, and the terror is immense. No one, out of terror, dares to raise his voice, and everyone is preoccupied with his own state, pondering what is coming upon him. If they speak, they speak secretly and in low voices: What has happened? What has occurred?

And likewise, in times of hardship we cannot speak aloud about them, as happened when Sa'd Zaghloul died, may God have mercy on him. Ahmad Shawqi was then in Lebanon, and he heard people whispering and speaking in low voices to one another that Sa'd had died, and no one dared to announce it openly because of the terror this event caused in souls. So Shawqi said:

It treads upon the ears in whispers and upon the lips.
I said: O people, gather your dreams.
Every soul, in its veins, its shroud...

1. He is Sa'd Pasha ibn Ibrahim Zaghloul, leader of Egypt's political renaissance. Born in Ibyana, one of the villages of al-Gharbiya, in 1857 CE. He entered al-Azhar in 1874 CE and associated with Sayyid Jamal al-Din al-Afghani. He held the post of Minister of Education, then Minister of Justice. In 1919 CE he was elected head of the Egyptian delegation demanding independence, and the English exiled him to Malta. He died in 1927 CE at the age of 70. (Al-A'lam by al-Zirikli, 3/83).

2. He is Amir al-Shu'ara' Ahmad Shawqi, the most famous poet of the modern age. Born in Cairo in 1868 CE, he grew up in the shadow of the ruling house of Egypt. He studied law in France and treated most forms of poetry: panegyric, love poetry, elegy, and description. He then took up political events. He died in 1932 CE. (Al-A'lam by al-Zirikli, 1/137).

On that Day, intercession will not benefit anyone except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and with whose speech He is pleased. (20:109)

Intercession (shafa'ah) presupposes one on whose behalf intercession is made, who is the human being; and an intercessor, who is the one of higher rank; and one with whom intercession is made. The one with whom intercession is made does not allow intercession in this manner, as you might improvise it on your own. Rather, he must grant you permission for it and place you in the station and rank of intercession, and this is a condition on the intercessor.

As for His saying, ﴿and with whose speech He is pleased﴾ (Ta-Ha): this applies to the one on whose behalf intercession is made, that he should say a word with which Allah is pleased, even if he falls short in other respects. The best thing a servant can say, with which Allah is pleased, is: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." This is an utterance acceptable to Allah, and it is the hope to which one clings and the glad tidings for the people of sin, for it is sufficient to bring them within the intercession of the Prophet (ﷺ).

So if you have a bad habit, or a point of weakness in your history that you see as an obstacle, do not despair. Look to another aspect of yourself that is stronger, and multiply good deeds through it, for good deeds erase bad deeds.

Meaning of ﴿what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot encompass it in knowledge﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:110): what is before them, and He knows what is behind them, whereas you cannot encompass it in knowledge, and you do not know except what He informs you of, unless there are preliminaries (muqaddimat) from which you can deduce it. This is because much of what the Truth has concealed in the universe has preliminaries that God has placed for it, so whoever attains these preliminaries reaches it.

Nevertheless, it is not said of him that he "knows the unseen" (ghayb). Rather, he has discovered something unseen through preliminaries that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has given him, just as we give a student a geometry exercise, mention the given data to him, and he deduces the required result from the given data.

The universe is full of things and phenomena which, when we contemplate and investigate them and do not turn away from them, we find in them many secrets. Through examining the phenomena of the universe they discovered the age of steam and made movement easy for people; through examining the phenomena of the universe Archimedes discovered the law of floating bodies; and they discovered penicillin, and so on.

All of these are phenomena present in God's universe, awaiting someone who will search for them and uncover them. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, reproaches us: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ (Yusuf 12:105).

Had they given them true attention, they would have benefited from them.

However, there are things which God, exalted is He, has kept exclusively to His knowledge; He may give them to whom He loves of His servants and make them aware of them, or they remain in God's knowledge, and no one knows them.

The Most High then says: ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all; and he who carries wrongdoing will surely fail.﴾

The face is the most noble and honoured thing in the make-up of a human being, and it is what gives a person his distinctive appearance. For this reason a person protects it and guards it. Do you not see that if dust, earth or mud should strike your face, you wipe it with your hand, and all you have done is move what was on your face onto your hand? Why? Because it is the most noble thing in you.

Therefore, prostration to Allah the Exalted in prayer is a sign of submission, humility, lowliness and abasement before Him, the Mighty and Majestic. You are content to place the most noble part of you upon the ground and to let it touch the dust. A person does not lower his face except before one whom he firmly believes deserves this prostration, and that prostration to Him alone protects him from prostrating to anyone else, as the poet said:

"And the prostration you dislike among the thousands of prostrations is, in it, salvation."

So prostrate to the One, and it will suffice you from prostrating to others; work for the One Face, and it will suffice you from all other faces.

As for His saying: ﴿And he who carries wrongdoing will surely fail﴾ (Ta-Ha): "ḥamala" (carried) means he took it as a heavy burden upon himself. And "ẓulm" (wrongdoing) in its origin is that you take something good that does not belong to you, so that you may benefit from it and increase what you have. So you appear to yourself to be increasing, but in reality you are carrying upon yourself a burden and a heavy load, under which you will stagger, and you have increased in sin rather than good.

Wrongdoing has ranks and degrees. The lowest of them is that you take what is not yours, even if it is trivial and of no value, or that you wrong another by attacking his honour. Then wrongdoing rises until it reaches its peak, which is associating partners with Allah, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great wrongdoing﴾ (Luqman, 13).

It is great because you have taken a right that belongs to Allah the Exalted and given it to another.

So, strive to be safe from this calamity, for Allah has said concerning it: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills...﴾ (An-Nisa', 48).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 112:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, will neither fear injustice nor diminution.﴾

Al-salihat (the righteous deeds): these are the actions that bring good to you or to others. The least of faith in righteous action is that you leave the righteous thing in its own state of goodness and do not corrupt it, such as finding a well from which people drink, and not filling it in or polluting it. If you elevate the righteous action, you can increase its goodness, by building a wall around it to protect it, or by making a cover for it... etc.

Among God's mercy upon us is that when He, glorified is He, urged us to righteous deeds, He said: ﴿of the righteous deeds...﴾ (Ta-Ha, 112). Here "min" (of) is for partiality (tab'id), so it suffices that you do some of the righteous deeds, because the capacity of a human being cannot contain all the righteous deeds nor is he able to bear them. It is enough for you to take a portion of them, and another takes a portion, and when all these portions of righteous action from the creatures are gathered together, they form for us complete righteousness.

As we have previously mentioned, none of us can gather the Muhammadan perfection in his character, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Goodness is truly in me and in my community until the Day of Resurrection."(1)

So in every individual of the community there is a trait of goodness, such that when the traits of perfection in character are gathered together, they give us the Muhammadan perfection.

As for His saying: ﴿and he is a believer...﴾ (Ta-Ha, 112): because faith is a condition for the acceptance of righteous action. If righteous action comes from a non-believer, he receives his reward in this world in the form of mention, fame, and the perpetuation of his memory, for he acted so that it would be said, and it was said, and the matter ended.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿then he will not fear injustice nor diminution﴾ (Ta-Ha, 112). Injustice here is other than the injustice in His saying: ﴿and he has indeed failed who carries injustice﴾ (Ta-Ha, 111). The injustice here is from a person toward himself or toward others. Rather, ﴿he will not fear injustice nor diminution﴾ (Ta-Ha, 112) means: injustice befalling him, by his not having his right for his deed withheld. In other words, we do not punish him for an evil he did not do, and we do not waste for him the reward of a good deed he performed, because the Truth, glorified is He, does not wrong people the weight of an atom.

﴿Nor diminution﴾ (Ta-Ha, 112): diminution (al-hadm) means shortfall, so we do not diminish his wage and reward. From it comes the expression "hadm al-ta'am" (digestion of food): the quantity of food we eat is digested and then absorbed, and transforms into a blood-like fluid, so it occupies less space. From it we say: "So-and-so is one whose right is diminished" (mahdum al-haqq), meaning: he had a right and did not receive it.

But what is the benefit of conjoining "diminution" (hadman) to "injustice" (zulman), since negating injustice entails negating diminution? We say: because injustice sometimes entirely nullifies the reward, and at other times reduces the recompense for the reward.

1 Al-'Ajluni said in Kashf al-Khafa' (1/476): (In al-Maqasid it says: our shaykh said: I do not know it, but its meaning is correct, referring to the hadith: "A group from my community will not cease to be victorious.")..

Then the Truthful, Glorified be He, says: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, and We have varied in it some of the warnings, that perhaps they may fear Allah, or it may produce for them a reminder.﴾ (113)

"Thus" (kadhalika): that is, like the sending down that We sent to the earlier nations. Just as We sent messengers to them, We have sent messengers to the nations contemporary with you. However, the difference between the messages is that they were sent for a limited time and in a limited place, whereas you were sent to all mankind and for all time until the Hour comes.

From the word ﴿We sent it down﴾ (113) (Ta-Ha) we understand that the one who sends down is higher than the one to whom it is sent down; sending down comes from something elevated. It is as if the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, draws our attention and raises our aspirations, saying: Do not descend to the level of earthly legislation, because it legislates for the present, is ignorant of the future, and is governed by whims, so things escape it and it needs to be corrected.

Therefore, when He calls us to His lofty method, He says: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite...﴾ (151) (al-An'am). That is: rise up and take your method from above, not from the earth.

﴿Qur'anan﴾ (113) (Ta-Ha): meaning "that which is recited," as He said: ﴿Kitaban﴾ (10) (al-Anbiya') meaning "that which is written," so that it may be preserved in hearts and in lines of writing. And He said ﴿Qur'anan 'Arabiyyan﴾ (113) (Ta-Ha), although the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to all people across time and place, and the Qur'an was revealed as a miracle for everyone.

They said: Because he (ﷺ) is the one who directly addresses this Arab nation, which will receive his first call, so the miracle must come in its tongue. Yet the miracle of the Qur'an is not for the Arabs alone; rather, it is a challenge to humans and jinn across time and place.

As the Most High said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like...﴾ (88) (al-Isra').

So the Qur'an is a challenge to all peoples: the Russian, the American, the Japanese, and the whole world, and with them the jinn as well. But why are the jinn included in the scope of the challenge?

They said: Because the Arabs of old believed that every poet or eloquent orator had a devil who supplied him and inspired him; therefore the jinn were also included in this domain.

Someone may say: How can the Qur'an be a challenge to non-Arabs when it is in Arabic? It is a proof against the Arabs alone, not others.

We say: Is the inimitability of the Qur'an only in its Arabic style and its eloquent expression? No. The aspects of the Qur'an's inimitability are many, and languages do not differ over them. Do languages differ over legislating for the good of society? Did the Qur'an not bring a method to an illiterate Bedouin nation that overcame the two greatest contemporary civilizations, the civilization of Persia in the East and the civilization of Byzantium in the West? Was this phenomenon not worthy of reflection and research?

Then there are the cosmic matters that the Qur'an spoke of more than fourteen centuries ago, which modern science is only now discovering.

Therefore, it is natural that the Qur'an came in Arabic, because it was revealed to an Arab messenger and in an Arab nation. The Most High says: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, to make clear to them...﴾ (4) (Ibrahim).

They are the ones who receive the call, are moved by it, are convinced by it, and then spread out with it throughout the far corners of the earth. Remarkably, through the call of the Qur'an they convinced a world that does not know Arabic, convinced it with the principles and methods the Qur'an brought, because these are principles and methods over which languages do not differ.

Then the Most High says: ﴿And We have varied in it some of the warnings...﴾ (113) (Ta-Ha). That is: whenever the Qur'an warns of something, this warning is varied in different ways and the warning is repeated to alert the heedless.

That is, We have diversified in it all methods of promise and threat, so that each method meets the desire in the soul of one of the recipients. It addresses all desires at all their levels: the scholar, the ignorant, and the average thinker, each finds in the Qur'an what suits him, because it legislates for everyone, for the philosopher and for the common man. Thus the Qur'an must contain variation in all kinds of faculties in order to convince everyone.

In the Qur'an there is promise and threat, and each has its people. Whoever is not moved by the enticement of good is moved by being restrained through force and might, as the poet said:

"Patience; if it does not suffice, then after it a threat follows, and if that does not suffice, then its resolutions suffice."

And in a report: "Indeed Allah restrains with the authority what He does not restrain with the Qur'an."

Warning and intimidation are a blessing from Allah, as mentioned in Surat al-Rahman, where the Most High says: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side (19). Between them is a barrier they do not transgress (20). Then which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? (21)﴾ (al-Rahman). These are blessings from Allah.

As for His words: ﴿There will be sent against you a flame of fire and copper, and you will not be victorious (35). Then which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? (36)﴾ (al-Rahman): what is the blessing in the fire and the flame?

The blessing is that Allah warns you of it and cautions you against it before you fall into it, admonishes you by it while you are still in the period of respite and opportunity for correction, so He does not seize you unawares nor leave you in your heedlessness. Just as you warn your son: if you neglect your lessons you will fail the examination, your classmates will despise you, and such-and-such will happen to you. Does he not leave his son in heedlessness and negligence until the examination overtakes him and failure surprises him? Is this not a blessing? Is it not an important advice?

"Taṣrīf" (variation): meaning the transformation and change by diverse methods so as to suit the reception of different temperaments when the Qur'an is revealed, perhaps it will meet awareness and concern ﴿that perhaps they may fear Allah, or it may produce for them a reminder﴾ (113) (Ta-Ha).

﴿That perhaps they may fear Allah﴾ (113) (Ta-Ha): taqwa is usually for evil and destructive sins, or it may produce for them remembrance, honour and elevation through doing good deeds, and this is among the ascents of obedience.

This is because obligation has two parts: one part forbids you from disobedience, and another part commands you to obey. It forbids you from drinking wine and commands you to pray. They guard against the first, and it produces for them a remembrance that urges them to perform the second. And since the Qur'an descends from above, He must say after it:

﴿Exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge (114).﴾

1 That is: We have clarified what it contains of intimidation, threat, reward and punishment. (Said by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 6/4425).
2 Al-wazʿ: restraining the soul from its desires. The meaning of the report: whoever is restrained from committing great sins by fear of the authority is more numerous than those restrained by fear of the Qur'an and of Allah the Most High; thus those restrained by authority from sins are more numerous than those restrained by the Qur'an through command, prohibition and warning. (Lisan al-Arab, root w-z-')

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 114:

﴿Exalted...﴾ (20:114): He is far exalted and transcends everything that resembles what is originated (ḥādith). He is exalted in His essence, so there is no essence like His essence; and He is exalted in His attributes, so there is no attribute like His attribute. If you find in creation an attribute that resembles an attribute of the Creator, glorified is He, then take it in the light of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (42:11).

The Truth, glorified is He, does not begrudge His servant calling himself a creator (khāliq) if he brings something into existence from non-existence. Rather, when He spoke of His own creation, He said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ (23:14).

You are a creator, but your Lord is the best of creators. You create from something that already exists, whereas your Lord, mighty and majestic, creates from nothing. You create a thing that remains solid in one state, whereas Allah creates a living, growing creation that senses, moves and multiplies. We have already given an example of this – and to Allah belongs the highest likeness – of the glassmaker who makes glass cups from sand, and we explained the difference between one kind of creating and another.

As for His saying: ﴿Exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth...﴾ (20:114): it draws our attention to the necessity of looking upward in legislation. What compels you to take legislation from a servant like yourself? And why does he not take your legislation? Therefore, the legislator must be higher than the one to whom the legislation is addressed.

Among the words of glorifying Allah that are said only to Him, glorified is He, is the phrase (Subḥān Allāh). Have you ever heard a human say it to a human? Here there are disbelievers, atheists, deniers of divinity and obstinate people, yet none of them has ever said it in praise of anyone.

Likewise, the words (taʿālā and tabāraka) are said only to Allah. We say: (Tabārakta Rabbanā wa-taʿālayta), meaning: You alone, with no partner.

So His saying: ﴿Exalted is Allah...﴾ (20:114) means: His rank is lofty, and His transcendence is elevated to a height that cannot be reached. As for exaltedness among humans toward one another, it is a despised matter; but the exaltedness of the Truth, glorified is He, is for the benefit of creation. The people of the countryside express this insight, saying: (Whoever has no elder, let him buy himself an elder), because the elder is the one who will take the weak by the hand, and the tyranny of the strong is restrained by him. If we have no elder, we will disagree and be lost.

Therefore, it is in the interest of the whole universe that Allah be exalted. The Truth is not exalted over us; rather, He is exalted for our sake and for our benefit. Any haughty or tyrannical human, when he knows that Allah is higher than him, will see his tyranny and arrogance crumble; and any weak person who knows he has a higher support that no one can reach will be reassured and live in safety. In this way, social balance comes about among people.

We love our servitude to Allah, mighty and majestic, although servitude is a hateful, disliked word when it is the servitude of creatures to creatures, where the master takes the best of his servant. Yet servitude to Allah is honour and dignity, because the servant of Allah is the one who takes the best of his Master. I am the servant of Allah, and my servitude to Him is for my own benefit; I will not add anything to His dominion, and He will not benefit from anything I do. For He, glorified is He, exercised His dominion and authority over the universe before He created creation. By His power and majesty He created, and before you existed, O human, rebellious and tyrannical, He brought the whole universe into being with all that is in it.

So by your faith you will add nothing to the dominion of Allah, as came in the sacred hadith: (O My servants, you will never attain to benefiting Me so as to benefit Me, nor will you attain to harming Me so as to harm Me...)(1). So if I dispose of you, it is for your benefit; nothing returns to Me from that.

As for His saying: ﴿the King, the Truth...﴾ (20:114): because there are many kings, Allah affirmed kingship for them and called them kings, as He said: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me..."﴾ (12:50), and He said: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship...?﴾ (2:258).

So: in this world there are kings, but they are not kings in truth. The true King is Allah, because the kings of this world are kings over a dominion bestowed upon them by Allah; it may slip away from them, or they may lose the kingship. And what kind of kingship is it that its holder does not truly own?

What kind of kingship is this that can be stripped from you by a coup or a bullet?

So the true kingship belongs to Allah; and when He grants some creatures dominion over others, it is for their benefit. He, glorified is He, is the One who bestows kingship, and He is the One who removes it if He wills: ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty from whom You will, and You honour whom You will, and You humble whom You will...﴾ (3:26).

So the Truth, glorified is He, has true kingship, and He bestows of His dominion upon whom He wills; yet the kingship and what it possesses remain in the grip of Allah, because He, glorified is He, is the Self-Subsisting Sustainer over His creation, and no one leaves His self-subsistence.

We may hear someone who reviles kings and presidents, and who meddles in their affairs, while he does not know that their kingship is from Allah. It is He, glorified is He, who gave them kingship and entrusted it to them, and no one has taken kingship from them against the will of Allah. So do not object to the choice of Allah; respect the one whom Allah has entrusted with your affairs, and know that in this lies the benefit of the lands and their people. Who knows, perhaps the tyrant among them will tomorrow become one of the subjects.

So: the Truth, glorified is He, is the King: He has made some people's affairs subject to others. This one disposes of that, and that one owns this, so that the movement of the universe may proceed. Then, when the Resurrection comes, He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ (40:16). This is the true kingship.

Among His greatness in exaltedness is that He Himself gives you rest through His action for you: He says to you, "Sleep to your heart's content, for I am not seized by drowsiness or sleep; sleep, for you have a Lord, the Self-Subsisting, standing over your affairs, who cares for you and guards you."

Among the meanings of ﴿the King, the Truth...﴾ (20:114) is: the Established, who does not change. Every manifestation of strength in the universe changes, except the strength of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He. Therefore He casts His commands while certain that they will be carried out, because He, glorified is He, is the true King, in whose hand is the forelock of all affairs. If He were not so, how could He say to a thing, "Be," and it is? No one disobeys Him, and no creature goes out of His obedience; He says to something, "Be," and it does not come to be.

So the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, sent down the Qur'an in Arabic and varied in it the threats, so that they may be God-fearing or that it may bring them remembrance; because it is His right to have that, since He is the true King who has no desire in what He legislates. Therefore you must accept His legislation. Legislation is not challenged except when it proceeds from desire: if a capitalist legislates, he gives privilege to the capitalists; if a poor man legislates, he gives privilege to the poor. But Allah, mighty and majestic, does not side with anyone at the expense of anyone.

Also, the legislator must have knowledge of future developments, so that no one can correct a law and change it, as happens with us now, when events force us to change the law because, at the moment we enacted it, these events were absent from us and we did not anticipate them. Therefore there is never any correction to the law of heaven.

Since the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is ﴿the King, the Truth﴾ (20:114), it is necessary that He guarantee for creation that the Book and the method reach them as He said, without any alteration in it. Therefore He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ (15:9).

It is We who will preserve it, because humans have tried to preserve the methods of heaven and were not trustworthy over them: they altered the Torah and the Gospel and the sacred books, either by concealing some of what Allah revealed or by forgetting some of it; and what they did mention they did not leave in its original state, but distorted it. Even if this is accepted from them, it is not accepted that they lie against Allah, composing from themselves and saying: ﴿It is from Allah,﴾ when it is not from Allah (3:78).

That is because the preservation of the method was entrusted to humans as an obligation, and an obligation is liable to be obeyed or disobeyed, as Allah said: ﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah...﴾ (5:44).

That is, He asked them to preserve it through this commanded duty, but they disobeyed through forgetting, concealment, distortion and addition. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, took upon Himself the preservation of the Qur'an, because it is the final Book, upon which there is no correction, and He, glorified is He, guaranteed for the Qur'an that it would not be distorted in any of the forms of distortion.

So be assured that the Qur'an, the Book of Allah that is in your hands, is the Word of Allah, which came from His knowledge, mighty and majestic, in the Preserved Tablet, concerning which He said: ﴿In a Book well-guarded (78) which none touches except the purified (79)﴾ (56:78-79).

Then it was brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit, who is entrusted with it and did not alter it; then it descended upon the heart of the Master of the Messengers, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿And if he had made up about Us some sayings (44), We would have seized him by the right hand (45)﴾ (69:44-45).

So: the preservation of the Qur'an was in knowledge in the Preserved Tablet, and preservation in the trust of the one who brought it down from heaven, and preservation in the one who received it, who is the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Thus there is no proof left for us after the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has gathered for the Qur'an every form of preservation.

Therefore, it was necessary that when Allah sent down the Qur'an upon His Messenger, He would say to him: ﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth (114)﴾ (20:114). There is no reality after this, and nothing is as firmly established as the Truth, glorified is He, and exalted.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you...﴾ (20:114). These are preliminaries to reassure the Messenger of Allah concerning the preservation of the Qur'an; for when revelation came down upon him, he would try to repeat it word by word. If the revelation said, for example: ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me..."﴾ (72:1), he would begin repeating it inwardly and echoing it behind Gabriel, peace be upon him, fearing that he would forget it, out of his intense eagerness for the Qur'an (3).

So Allah forbade him this haste: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an...﴾ (20:114). That is: do not rush, and do not preoccupy yourself with repetition and recitation; its maturity will come to you when it is complete, so do not fear that some of it will escape you, since I have taken upon Myself its preservation. Therefore He says to him in another place: ﴿We will make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ (87:6).

So be reassured and do not be anxious about this matter, for your preoccupation with memorising one word may cause you to miss another.

Haste is bringing a thing out before its maturity, like plucking fruit before it ripens and before its time; when you eat it, you find it has not yet become sweet, or you hasten to pick it while it is small and cannot satisfy even one person, whereas if you had left it until its time, it would have been enough for several people.

The Qur'an is speech of a high level of eloquence, not ordinary speech that would be easy for him to memorise; therefore he was eager for memorising and steadfastness.

In another verse, Allah, glorified is He, clarifies this matter: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it (16). Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation (17). So when We have recited it, follow its recitation (18)﴾ (75:16-18). That is: once the verses are complete, you may recite them as you wish.

This is one of the miracles of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: a prophet upon whom several parts of the Qur'an, or a whole surah, would be sent down, and then when the revelation withdrew from him he would repeat it exactly as it was revealed. If you were to bring the person most capable of memorising, and recite to him for, say, ten minutes from any book or any speech, then ask him to repeat what he heard, he would not be able to do it.

As for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he would command the scribes to write the Qur'an, then dictate it to them as he had heard it, without changing a single letter; and he would dictate the verses to their places in the different surahs, saying: (Place these in such-and-such surah, and this in such-and-such surah)(4).

Had a surah been sent down whole at once, the matter would have been somewhat easier; but the verses were sent down separately. When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited in prayer, for example, a single surah whose verses had been sent down separately, one part sent down today and another yesterday, and so on, yet he would recite them in order, verse by verse.

As for His saying, counting it: ﴿Then indeed upon Us is its explanation﴾ (75:19). And He addressed the Prophet in another verse: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them...﴾ (16:44). So the explanation (bayān) is from Allah, and the clarification (tabyīn) is from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

As for the meaning of ﴿before its revelation is completed to you﴾ (20:114): that is, wait until it comes to you calmly. But how would the Messenger know that? How would he know that the state that overtakes him at the descent of revelation has passed? The Companions describe the state of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, at the descent of revelation upon him, saying: "We would hear around his head like the drone of the..."

2. The verse ﴿in a Book well-guarded (78)﴾ (56:78). It was said: it is the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: it is the Qur'an, which the believer preserves either written down or preserves in his heart memorised. (al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm 2/176).
