Also related by al-Tirmidhī in his Sunan (5/272), and al-Ḥākim in his Mustadrak (2/221, 330).

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no firm resolve.﴾

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is consoling His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and easing for him what he suffers from the disbelief and obstinacy of his people, by saying to him: Accept them with their shortcomings, for they are the children of Adam, and disobedience is something that occurs among them. A covenant was previously made with their father, and he forgot. So if these forget, then accept from them, for they are the children of forgetfulness (nisy).

Therefore, when you entrust someone with doing something and he does not carry it out, do not become angry; return the matter to this consideration and seek an excuse for him.

As for His saying ﴿We had taken a covenant with Adam…﴾ (Ta-Ha 115): that is, We commanded, enjoined, admonished, and told him everything.

As for ﴿from before…﴾ (Ta-Ha 115): this word has a role in the Qur'an, and it has settled for us several positions. Among them His saying here about Adam, and the meaning is: take for them an example from their father, whom Allah charged directly, not through a messenger, and charged with a single command. Then He also forbade him from one thing: "Eat from every part of the Garden except this tree." This is the obligation, and despite this Adam forgot what he was commanded.

Thus, when the obligation comes through a messenger and with many matters, then whoever among the children of Adam forgets, we must excuse him and seek an excuse for him. And because of the frequency of forgetfulness among the offspring of Adam, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed I am Most Forgiving (ghaffar)…﴾ (Ta-Ha 82): with emphasis, because all are subject to forgetfulness and subject to error, so the matter then requires much forgiveness.

Likewise "from before" came in His saying: ﴿Why did you kill the prophets of Allah before?﴾ (Al-Baqarah 91).

It had a role and a purpose. For if the Truth, glorified is He, had said merely: "Why do you kill the prophets of Allah?", perhaps it would have emboldened them to transgress against the Messenger of Allah by killing him, or the Messenger of Allah might have understood from it that he was exposed to killing as happened to his predecessors among the prophets. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, restricted it and made it something of the past that will not recur; this is something from before, and this is not its time.

As for His saying: ﴿but he forgot, and We found in him no firm resolve﴾ (Ta-Ha 115): that is, he forgot the covenant; this is one point. ﴿And We found in him no firm resolve﴾ (Ta-Ha 115): he did not have a strong determination that would help him to press on and remain steadfast in the matter.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants to give us an idea: when He commands you with something beneficial to you, you rush toward it; but if He commands you with something that restrains your desires, you refuse and disobey. From here, the obligation requires a strong resolve that helps you to proceed with it and remain steadfast upon it. If you approach a matter that opposes your desire, look at it and reflect: how it gives you a fleeting immediate desire, but it is followed by a lasting humiliation later. So resolve (ʿazm) here is that desire should not deceive you.

Do you not see that Allah the Exalted named the messengers, the bearers of the great calls and missions in human history, ﴿the possessors of resolve (ulu al-ʿazm)﴾ (Al-Ahqaf 35), because they would bear hardships and difficult tasks that require steadfastness and patience in the obligations.

Among this also is His saying: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾ (Al-Baqarah 63): that is, with a resolve that drives to obedience and restrains from sins.

And the matter of a servant forgetting the prohibitions that carry punishment and torment has raised among people a problem concerning qadar (divine decree). You hear some say: "Since Allah has written this act upon me, why does He punish me for it?"

We are surprised at this statement. Why do they not also say: "Why does He reward me for this act, since He has written it upon me?" Why did they stop at the first and "swallow" the other? Obviously, because the first is not in your favor. So, you must deal with your Lord with one standard, and measure matters by one measure.

The covenant that Allah took from Adam was that he should eat freely from every bounty of the Garden as he wished, except one tree, from the mere approach to which He warned him, both he and his wife: ﴿And do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers﴾ (Al-Baqarah 35).

This matter draws our attention to the fact that the permitted things are numerous beyond counting, whereas the prohibited things are few, limited and enumerable. Therefore, when the Truth, glorified is He, speaks to us about obligation, He says: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you…﴾ (Al-An'am 151). So the prohibitions are those that can be enumerated, whereas the permitted things are beyond the scope of enumeration.

We also observe that when Allah warns us about prohibited things, He does not warn us merely against committing them, but against merely approaching them: ﴿And do not approach this tree…﴾ (Al-Baqarah 35), and He did not say: "Do not eat from it," so that a person may remain far from the zone of danger and the likelihood of the act.

And when our Lord speaks to us about His limits that He has set for us, He says regarding the permitted limit: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them﴾ (Al-Baqarah 229), and regarding the forbidden limit He says: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them﴾ (Al-Baqarah 187). That is because whoever grazes around the sanctuary is about to fall into it.

The scholars have said much about what Adam, peace be upon him, forgot. Some of them said: he forgot ("do not approach this tree") ... and according to this opinion Adam did not forget, because he carried out the command by eating from what Allah had permitted him; as for his eating from the tree that Allah had forbidden him, there is no forgetting in this either, because Iblis reminded him of this prohibition when he said: ﴿Your Lord only forbade you this tree, lest you become angels or become of the immortal﴾ (Al-A'raf 20).

So when Adam ate from the tree, he was not forgetting what Allah had forbidden him.

Then: what is meant by forgetting here?

What is meant is that Adam, peace be upon him, forgot what Allah had informed him of concerning the enmity of Iblis, may Allah curse him, when He said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you from the Garden, and [thus] you will be distressed﴾ (Ta-Ha 117).

Human thought must miss some matters, and if a person had alertness and caution, he would not have been deceived by Iblis's trickery. You see him reminding Adam of the prohibition, yet not leaving him in his heedlessness, then trying to persuade him: "If you both eat from this tree, you will become angels or become of the immortal."

And since you, O Iblis, are of such cleverness, why did you not eat from the tree yourself and become an angel or become of the immortal? Why did you shrink until you became a hare, saying: ﴿Reprieve me until the day they are resurrected﴾ (Al-A'raf 14)?

So this is an example of Iblis's deception of Adam and his offspring after him, which Allah the Exalted draws our attention to, saying: Be alert and beware, for his enmity toward you has been established since everyone prostrated to Adam in honor, and he refused to prostrate.

It was incumbent upon Adam to beware of his enemy, and to guard himself by suspicion of him, examining his words, reflecting on his speech, and scrutinizing his suggestions.

Some say that Adam's error resulted from forgetfulness; it was an unintentional error, and forgetfulness is lifted, as in the noble hadith: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for my community error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do."(1)

Was forgetfulness formerly not lifted, and then lifted for this community as an honor to it? Those who hold this view seek to excuse Adam, peace be upon him. But how, when his Lord charged him directly, and charged him with a single command? The matter does not admit of forgetfulness; if Adam forgot despite the singleness of the command and that it came from Allah directly, this is in any case a transgression.

1 Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2045), al-Daraqutni in his Sunan (4/170), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/198), who declared it sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, from Ibn Abbas; but the isnad of Ibn Majah is discontinuous.

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, relates to us the story of Adam with Iblis:

﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused (116).﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted, relates to us the story of Adam, peace be upon him. But we notice that He, glory be to Him, gave us the summary and brief outline of the story in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination (115).﴾ (Ta-Ha). The original story and its natural order is that He, glory be to Him, says: "I created Adam with My Hand and shaped him, and such and such; then I commanded the angels to prostrate to him, then I said to him: such and such..."

Presenting the story in this manner is one of the methods of suspense (tashwiq), which writers and authors today use in their stories, giving us at the beginning of the story a snapshot of its ending, in order to arouse the desire to follow its events; then it returns to present the story to you in detail from its beginning. So this is a kind of excitement, suspense and alerting.

Among this is the Qur'an's method in the story of the People of the Cave, where it mentioned the story briefly, saying: ﴿Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs a wonder? (9) When the youths retreated to the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance." (10) So We struck over their ears within the cave for a number of years (11). Then We awakened them that We might know which of the two parties was most precise in computing what they had remained in time (12).﴾ (Al-Kahf).

Then it began to present it in detail: ﴿We relate to you their story in truth... (13)﴾ (Al-Kahf).

This method appears frequently in the stories of the Qur'an. In the story of Lot, peace be upon him, it begins with the end of the story and what befell them of punishment: ﴿The people of Lot denied the warnings (33). Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot; We saved them before dawn (34).﴾ (Al-Qamar).

Then it returns to detail the events: ﴿And he had already warned them of Our seizure, but they disputed the warnings (36). And they had solicited him against his guests, so We obliterated their eyes, "Taste My punishment and warning" (37).﴾ (Al-Qamar).

Among the most prominent of these instances is His saying, exalted is He, in the story of Moses and Pharaoh: ﴿Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, but they wronged themselves thereby. So see how was the end of the corrupters (103).﴾ (Al-A'raf). That is: after the procession of messages to Pharaoh and his establishment, they wronged themselves therein; so see how was the end of the corrupters. This is the summary of the story; then he begins to narrate the events in detail: ﴿And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds (104).﴾ (Al-A'raf).

Thus is the Qur'an's method in the story of Adam, peace be upon him: it gives us the summary of the story, then details it: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated (116).﴾ (Ta-Ha). That is: mention when We said to the angels: ﴿Prostrate to Adam...(34)﴾ (Al-Baqarah).

Before we delve into the story of our father Adam, peace be upon him, we must point out that it has been repeated frequently in the Qur'an. But this repetition is intended for a wisdom, and does not mean repeating the events; rather they are snapshots of different aspects of a single event, which gather in the end to give you the complete story from all its angles.

Also, the purpose of the Qur'an's stories is to strengthen the Prophet (ﷺ), because he will pass through many events and hardships, and in each of them he will need strengthening; and this purpose is not achieved if we recount the story once, as in the story of Joseph, peace be upon him, for example.

As for His saying: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated...(116).﴾ (Ta-Ha): Some object, saying: how do the angels prostrate to a human? Yes, they prostrated to Adam, but they did not prostrate on their own initiative; rather by the command of God to them. So the matter is not prostration to Adam so much as obedience to the command of God. To the one who says this: "Are you more royal than the King?" That is: "Are you more Lord-like than the Lord?"

And what is the meaning of prostration (sujud)? Prostration means submission, as in His saying: ﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down to him prostrating... (100).﴾ (Yusuf). That is: a prostration of honour and submission, not a prostration of worship.

Adam, peace be upon him, is the vicegerent of God on earth, but he is not the only one on it. On the earth there are many creatures, among them the perceptible, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, the air, the water, the earth and the mountains, and everything in it that is of benefit to this vicegerent; and among them is what is hidden, such as the angels who manage the hidden side of this universe, among them the guardians and the recorders, and among them those charged with the wind and with the rain, and other matters that serve creation. So all must necessarily submit to this one who is served, who came after.

Some may like to say: "We have wronged Adam when he disobeyed his Lord, so we were expelled from Paradise to earth." We say: we must understand from God, for the Truthful, blessed and exalted, did not create Adam for the Garden, which is the abode of eternity; rather He created him to be His vicegerent on earth, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah)...(30).﴾ (Al-Baqarah).

So the first message from God about Adam is that He created him for the earth, not for the Garden. The Garden, although it is used for the abode of eternity and the abode of otherworldly bliss, is also used for the gardens and orchards of this world, as in the saying of the Truthful, glory be to Him:

﴿Indeed, We tested them as We tested the companions of the garden, when they swore to pick its fruit at morning (17).﴾ (Al-Qalam).

And His saying: ﴿And present to them an example: two men, for one of them We made two gardens of grapevines...(32).﴾ (Al-Kahf).

So: "garden" is applied to something in this world that contains everything the soul seeks and desires; and it is called a garden (jannah) because its trees and density cover those who enter it, or a garden because it suffices a person and does not make him need anything other than it.

So do not wrong Adam by saying that he expelled you from the Garden; for it was not the Garden of eternity, but a place which God prepared for him, and He wished to give him a lesson in this place, and to train him for carrying out his mission in life and his vicegerency on earth.

Have you seen what we now do in establishing training camps in various fields of life, where we take charge of the trainee's livelihood, lodging and care?

They are places prepared for training in various tasks, sports, scientific, or military, etc.

Thus was Adam's garden a place of training for him before he began his mission as God's vicegerent on earth; so God placed him in this practical applied experiment, and gave him in it a model of being charged with command and prohibition, and warned him against his enemy who would lie in wait for him and his offspring after him, and revealed to him some of his methods of misguidance and seduction.

This is the essence of God's method on earth, and there is no messenger but who came with this same method: command, prohibition, obligation, and warning against Satan and his whispering until he removes us from God's command and prohibition.

And after this training "course" in the Garden, Adam learned by practical application that Satan is his enemy, and that he would deceive and trick him; then after this experience God sent him down to begin his mission on earth, so that he would be mindful and wary of his enemy.

Some stand at length over the matter of Adam's disobedience: how does he disobey God while he is a prophet? They cite His saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred (121).﴾ (Ta-Ha).

We say: since Adam, peace be upon him, is God's vicegerent on His earth, and from him all people descend until the Hour is established, and from his offspring are the prophets and non-prophets, from his offspring are the messengers and those to whom they were sent. So he by himself represents all the creation that follows, in all its kinds, the infallible and the non-infallible.

Also, Adam, peace be upon him, went through this experience before he was made a prophet, and went through it after he was made a prophet, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred (121). Then his Lord chose him, so He turned to him in forgiveness and guided him (122).﴾ (Ta-Ha).

So choosing and infallibility came after the testing. Then when Adam and his enemy were sent down to earth, his Lord addressed him: ﴿So whenever there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance will have no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve (38).﴾ (Al-Baqarah).

Thus began a new phase in the life of Adam, peace be upon him, and Adam played two roles: the role of infallibility and prophethood after his Lord chose him, and the role of the ordinary human who is not infallible and who is subject to forgetfulness and disobedience like any person among the people of the earth.

It is therefore necessary that we understand that Adam was created for the earth and its cultivation, and God prepared it for Adam and his offspring after him, and furnished it with all the necessities of life and the necessities of the continuation of the species; so whoever desires the luxury of life, let him employ his mind upon these necessities and derive from them what he wants.

We have mentioned that in the universe there is malak and malakut: the malak is the apparent that we see and witness, and the malakut is what is hidden from us behind this malak; and among the malakut are things that carry out their task in our lives without our seeing them. For example, the phenomenon of terrestrial gravity, which intervenes in many matters in our lives, was behind the veil of the malakut; we did not see it nor know anything of it, then when minds were guided to it and discovered it, we knew that there is what is called gravity.

And among the malakut are the angels assigned, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿For him are successive angels before and behind him, guarding him by the command of God... (11).﴾ (Al-Ra'd).

And among them are the recorders: ﴿Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer, ready (18).﴾ (Qaf).

So when God created Adam, and created the angels assigned to his interests on earth, He commanded them to prostrate to him, because they would be in his service; so prostration was obedience to the command of God, and submission to the vicegerent who would cultivate the earth.

As for His saying: ﴿Except Iblis; he refused (116).﴾ (Ta-Ha), and in another verse:

﴿Except Iblis; he refused and was arrogant... (74).﴾ (Sad).

And the Truthful, glory be to Him, has clarified the reason for Iblis's refusal to prostrate to Adam in His saying: ﴿Have you become arrogant, or were you among the haughty? (75).﴾ (Sad).

That is: there is no cause for your refusal except arrogance towards prostration, or that you were among the haughty, i.e., the angels whom the command to prostrate did not include. It is as though the command was for particular angels, those assigned to serve Adam; as for the haughty ones, they are the exalted angels, who have no connection with Adam, and perhaps do not know of him.

Among the expressions that have stirred debate about the eloquence of the Qur'an among the orientalists is His saying: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating... (75).﴾ (Sad), and His saying in another place: ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating... (12).﴾ (Al-A'raf). Which of the two expressions is eloquent? And if one is eloquent, the other is not eloquent.

All this results from a deficiency in understanding the language of the Qur'an, and the absence of the Arabic linguistic faculty among these people. There is a difference between your wanting to prostrate and someone coming to you and saying, "Do not prostrate," and between a person persuading you not to prostrate.

So His saying: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating... (75).﴾ (Sad): you wanted to prostrate and someone prevented you. And His saying: ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating... (12).﴾ (Al-A'raf) means: your command was not to prostrate, and he persuaded you, and you were persuaded.

Among the questions raised about this story: was Iblis one of the angels, so that the command to prostrate included him? And how could he be of the angels, when they do not disobey God in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded? And if he was not an angel, then what brought him into the command?

To clarify this matter we say: God created the two weights, the jinn and mankind, and made them free in many matters and subject to compulsion in some matters, to establish the absolute power of His, exalted is He, over His creation. If you are free in matters of obligation, and you are able to obey or to disobey, your choice does not extend to whether you are healthy or sick, tall or short, poor or rich, and your choice does not extend to whether you live or die.

And the Truthful, blessed and exalted, does not obligate you with "do this" or "do not do that" unless He has made you fit both for doing and for not doing. This applies to matters of obligation; everything else is matters of compulsion in which you have no choice, which are the matters of decree (qadariyyat).

Therefore we say to those who have become accustomed to rebellion and have grown used to going outside God's rulings in obligations: why do you not also rebel against the matters of decree, since you have become accustomed to disobedience? So you are compelled and a slave against your will.

Therefore, if the one who has choice is obedient, binding himself to the method of his Lord, and even surrenders his choice to God's choice, then his rank with God is great, and he is better than the angel, because the angel obeys...

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and your wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden and [thus] you will suffer.﴾

The Exalted's words: ﴿And your wife...﴾ (Ta-Ha 117). The word "zawj" (spouse) does not mean two, as some suppose. "Zawj" is a single individual with its like alongside it. So it is not correct to say "tawam" (twin) for the pair; rather it is "tawamani" (twins), each of them being a twin to the other. Therefore He, Exalted, says: ﴿And of everything We created pairs (zawjayn)...﴾ (adh-Dhariyat 49).

Another point in His words: ﴿So let him not drive you both out of the Garden...﴾ (Ta-Ha 117). The address is to Adam and his wife, warning them of the seduction and scheming of Iblis. Then He says: ﴿...and you will suffer﴾ (Ta-Ha 117), in the singular form, and He did not say "fatashqaya" (you two will suffer). Why? Because the burden of toil and movement belongs to the man, whereas the woman is the comfortable repose that refreshes the one who moves. This is contrary to what we see in our society of eagerness for women's employment under the pretext of helping to bear life's burdens.

Indeed, We have prepared Paradise for you, placed in it everything you need, permitted you all its delights, and forbade you only one thing from it.(1) And upon Us is this for you: ﴿That you will not hunger therein nor be unclothed﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:118). So you will not go hungry therein, for in it are all kinds of fruits: ﴿And eat from it freely, wherever you wish﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:35).

Here we notice that Allah, exalted is He, guaranteed for them something apparent that fulfils an apparent instinct, namely clothing and covering, and a hidden instinct, namely the instinct for food.

(1) This is the tree of which the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿And do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:35). Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir (1/79), cited six opinions about this tree, saying:
It is the grapevine; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi and al-Sha'bi.
It is wheat; the Jews claim this.
It is the ear of grain (sunbulah); this was said by Ibn 'Abbas.
It is barley (al-birr); this was also said by Ibn 'Abbas.
It is the date palm; this was said by Abu Malik.
It is the fig tree; this was said by Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Jarir.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And that you will not thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun's heat.﴾

(تظمأ) means: you will not thirst. (تضحى): that is, you will not be exposed to the scorching blaze of the sun. Thus their Lord guaranteed for them both an inner instinct, which is thirst, and an outer instinct, which is that the heat of the sun shall not scorch you.

Then the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾

We note that the Truth, glorified is He, chose for the act of Satan a name that suits enticing someone toward a thing. That word is "al-waswasah" (whispering, insinuation), which originally means the sound of ornaments (al-huli), i.e., the gold with which women adorn themselves, just as we say: "naqiq al-difda'" (the croaking of frogs), "sahil al-khayl" (the neighing of horses), "khuwar al-baqar" (the lowing of cattle), "nahiq al-hamir" (the braying of donkeys), "tha'a' al-shah" (the bleating of sheep), "kharir al-ma'" (the babbling of water), and "hafif al-shajar" (the rustling of trees).

Likewise, al-waswasah is the name for the sound of ornaments that draws the ears and entices one to look toward it, as though the Truth, glorified is He, is warning us that Satan will enter upon us by way of enticement and embellishment.

So what did he whisper to Adam?

﴿"O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ (Ta-Ha).

And we marvel at Iblis: if you know the tree of eternity and the kingdom that does not decay, why did you not eat from it yourself and obtain this privilege?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 20, verse 121:

Meaning: after they both ate from this tree, their private parts (sawat) became apparent to them. The sawah is the 'awrah, that is, the place a person is ashamed to have exposed, and what is intended is the front and rear passages in both man and woman. Each of the front and rear passages has a function, and through them the body rids itself of waste: water, by way of the kidneys, the ureters and the bladder, through the front passage; and the remnants and waste of food resulting from the movement of digestion and the process of metabolism, which exit through the rear passage.

But when did Adam and his wife become aware of their private parts: after eating in general from the trees of Paradise, or after eating from this particular tree?

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, linked the appearance of the 'awrah to eating from the tree He had forbidden them: ﴿So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them...﴾ (20:121). Thus, before eating from this tree they did not know their 'awrah, and did not know this process of elimination, because the food was prepared for them by their Lord, who gave them power and life without leaving any waste in the body.

But when they disobeyed and ate from the tree, the food began to ferment and the process of digestion that we know took place within it. So this was the first time Adam and his wife noticed the matter of waste and turned their attention to their 'awrah: "What is this that comes out of it?"

Here is a symbolic matter that deserves attention: when you see an 'awrah (exposure of what should be covered) in society, know that one of Allah's methods has been disabled.

So, Adam and his wife did not know food waste and what results from it of wind and other repulsive, filthy things except after the disobedience, and then they were bewildered: what should they do? They had nothing but the leaves of the trees: ﴿and they began to fasten upon themselves some leaves of Paradise...﴾ (20:121).

That is, they began to stick leaves onto their 'awrah to cover it, thus by nature. Otherwise, what made these two openings an 'awrah rather than other openings of the body, such as the nose and the mouth, for example?

They say: because the front and rear passages are where something filthy and disgusting comes out, which a person is keen to conceal. And it is remarkable that man, being a rational animal, has been favored by Allah; when he eats, he eats by choice, whereas the animal eats by its instinct. Yet man exceeds the limit in his eating and drinking: he eats various kinds, eats more than his need, and eats after he is full, unlike the animal, which is governed by instinct.

Therefore you find the smell of human waste foul and repulsive, with no benefit in it at all, whereas the waste of animals is hardly smelled, and it can be put to use, as they make it fuel or natural fertilizer. And after that we accuse the animal and say: it is bahim (dumb)... etc.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾ (20:121): that is, before prophethood, in the stage of training. In this stage a person is liable both to be right and to be wrong. If he errs in this stage, you do not strike him but rather correct his error, like a student during the period of study: if he errs, the teacher corrects him; but in the examination, he is held to account.

The meaning of ﴿fa-ghawa﴾ (and so he erred): that is, he did not hit upon the truth, just as they say of one who has wandered lost in the desert that he is ghawin, that is, lost. Then comes the next stage: the stage of infallibility (ismah).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: "Then his Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him" (20:122).

So: Adam's role was that of an ordinary human being who obeys and disobeys, and who listens to the words of Satan. Yet his Lord prescribed repentance for him, as He, glorified is He, said: "Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He turned to him in forgiveness..." (2:37).

So: Adam disobeyed while he was an ordinary human being, not while he was a prophet, as some people claim.

His words, "Then He chose him..." (20:122), mark the beginning of the stage of prophethood in the life of Adam, peace be upon him. "Then" (thumma) denotes sequence with a gap in time. "Chose him" (ijtabahu) means He selected him, and his Lord.

The Truth, glorified is He, did not say "Then Allah chose him," but rather "his Lord chose him" (ijtabahu rabbuhu), because the Lord (al-Rabb) is the One who undertakes upbringing and nurture, and completing upbringing includes preparing for the task. Among the preparation of Adam for his mission was that he should pass through this experience, and this arrangement took place in the Garden.

"And guided him" (wa-hada): the meaning of the guidance is His saying: "He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others. Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will not go astray, nor will he be distressed" (20:123).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 123:

That is: "Go down to the earth and proceed in it in the light of past experience, and know that there is a command, a prohibition, and an enemy who whispers, adorns, and misleads until he exposes your nakedness." It is as though He, Mighty and Majestic, gives Adam sufficient immunity for himself and his offspring after him, so that the movement of life may be upright for them under the obligations (al-taklif). For obligations are either a command or a prohibition, and Satan is the one who corrupts these obligations for us.

Nevertheless, we must not forget another party, which is the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammara), which moves you toward disobedience and transgression. Therefore, your enemy is not Satan alone, so that you make him a scapegoat upon whom you hang all your sins. There are sins into which Satan does not enter except through the soul. Otherwise, when Iblis went astray, who led him astray? And who whispered to him?

As for His words, ﴿Go down...﴾ (20:123): in the dual form, it is a command to two: Adam, in whom his offspring are contained, and Iblis, in whom his offspring are contained. So His words ﴿Go down...﴾ (20:123) indicate the origin, and His words elsewhere, ﴿Go down...﴾ (2:38), indicate what branches off from this origin.

As for His words ﴿some of you are enemies to others﴾ (2:36): that is, some are enemies to the others. The word "some" (ba'd) has a great role in the Qur'an, and the meaning is: you are an enemy of Satan if you are obedient, and Satan is your enemy if you are obedient. But if you are disobedient, there is then no enmity, because Satan wants you to be disobedient. When "some" is not specified, the enmity is mutual, since "some" is common to all.

As in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees...﴾ (43:32). So who is raised, and who is raised over? People of superficial outlook understand that the rich are raised above the poor.

But the meaning is far broader than this. All creation, in relation to the Truth, Glorified is He, is equal, and the great matters of life require many capacities and diverse talents. Therefore talents do not gather in one person while another is deprived of them; rather, the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, distributes talents among His creatures. This one excels at something, and that one excels at something else, so that people need one another and the members of society are bound together, and the harmony necessary for the movement of life arises between them.

So: every part of existence is raised in one thing and raised over in another. Let a person be courteous in the movement of his life, not exalting himself over others because he has excelled in something. Let him look at what others have excelled in and what they have distinguished themselves by, so that no people mock another people, for perhaps they are better than them, and perhaps they have talents that you do not possess.

But since "some of you are enemies to others," that is: Adam, in whom his offspring are contained, and Iblis, in whom his offspring are contained, then who will be the judge? The judgment between them is the method of God: ﴿Then, when there comes to you guidance from Me...﴾ (20:123). So beware lest you make guidance come from yourselves, for if guidance came from you, it would not benefit and would not prosper.

﴿Whoever follows My guidance, he will not go astray, nor will he be distressed﴾ (20:123). It is as though God's guidance and His method are the "manual" (catalogue) of human well-being and the law of its maintenance. Do you not see that the human maker, when he supplies his product with a "manual" containing instructions for its operation and maintenance, if you follow these instructions, the machine serves you and performs its task for you without malfunction?

Just as this "manual" is placed only by the maker of the machine, so too the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, does not place His law and guidance for His creatures except Himself, Glorified is He. If another sets it, this is an usurpation upon God, Mighty and Majestic, as if you went to the butcher and said to him: "Provide me with the necessary instructions for maintaining the microphone!!"

Therefore: corruption in the universe occurs whenever we depart from God's method, transgress His law and His legislation, and accept a guidance other than His guidance. For this reason, He, exalted is He, says after it: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be distressed﴾ (Ta-Ha). If this is the outcome for those who follow God's guidance and the consequence of walking His path, then what is the consequence for those who turn away from it?

And i'raD (turning away) means turning aside, and that you give it the back of your shoulders, as we mentioned before.

As for His saying: ﴿a constricted life...﴾ (Ta-Ha): ḍankā (constricted) is the severe narrowness from which you try to escape here or there but cannot. This constricted life comes to those who turn away from God, because whoever believes in a God, if the means become scarce for him, life never becomes narrow for him, because he knows that he has a Lord who will bring him out of what he is in.

As for the non-believer, when the means become constricted for him and overpower him, he finds no one to turn to, and so he commits suicide. The believer says: "I have a Lord who provides for me and relieves my distress," as the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of God. Verily, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾ (ar-Ra'd).

For this reason they say: "There is no distress when You are Lord." If a child does not carry worry while his father is present, and he has a father who spares him the hardships and burdens of life, so that he knows nothing of crises or rising prices and carries no worry about anything, how much more so one who has a Lord?

We have already given an example, and to God belongs the highest example. We said: suppose you have a pound with you and it falls from your pocket or gets lost from you; you will grieve over it if you have nothing else with you, but if you have something else with you, you will not grieve over it. If you have an account in the bank, it is as if nothing happened. Likewise, the believer, in his faith in his Lord, has the highest reserve that compensates him for everything.

And the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, gave us an example of this faith-based reserve in the story of Moses, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh, when Moses and his people were surrounded, with the sea before them and Pharaoh with his armies behind them, and the people became certain that they would be overtaken. What did the Prophet of God, Moses, say?

He said: ﴿By no means! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ (ash-Shu'ara'). Thus, with his whole mouth he says it, as one certain, although it is a statement that could be proven false after moments; but it is the faith in which hearts find rest, and the reserve in which every believer trusts.

Therefore: whoever believes in God and follows His guidance will never be in constriction or hardship, and if hardship befalls him, it will not take his resolve away from contentment and from turning to his Lord.

And among the signs of the Qur'anic miraculousness regarding the matter of constriction is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whomever God wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight, as if he were climbing up into the sky...﴾ (al-An'am).

From where did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, know that one who climbs into the sky has a constricted chest? Did anyone ascend into the sky at that time and test this matter? The meaning of constriction of the chest is that the space of the lungs, which are the organ of breathing, narrows due to illness, excessive exertion, or other causes. Do you not see that if you climb a steep staircase, you pant (1)? That means the lungs, which are the reservoir of air, do not find sufficient air commensurate with the movement being exerted, and then the rate of breathing increases to compensate for the lack of air.

And now, after the conquest of space, we have come to know the matter of shortness of breath in the upper layers of the atmosphere, which forces them to take oxygen tubes and other breathing apparatus.

1 al-nahj and al-nahij: the breath coming in rapid succession due to intense movement. (Lisan al-'Arab, root: n-h-j).

The word *a'ma* (blind) appears in His saying, ﴿Whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and even more astray from the way﴾ (al-Isra, 72).

The meaning of blindness is that one does not perceive what is visible. Visible things may exist while one does not turn to them with sight, so it is as if you were blind and could not see. Likewise, one who turns away from the signs and does not reflect upon them is blind to them and does not see them.

Therefore, in the Hereafter, He says, ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection, on their faces, blind, mute, and deaf﴾ (al-Isra, 97). When the disbelievers are raised, they are terrified by the Resurrection that they used to deny, and they become agitated with great turmoil. Each of them tries to find an exit and a way to salvation, but it is far-fetched, for God has deprived them of all avenues of perception and has blocked before their faces every path to deliverance. A person finds his way by himself and with his eyes. If he is blind, he can still call out to someone who will take his hand. If he is also mute, he may still hear someone calling to him, warning him, and guiding him. But if he is also deaf, what then?

Thus, every means of salvation is closed before him. He is blind and cannot see the way to salvation by himself, mute and cannot cry out to someone who might rescue him, and deaf and cannot hear anyone who volunteers to guide or warn him.

Many skeptics have found in this verse an apparent point with which to criticize the style of the Qur'an. Here He says, ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind, while I had been seeing?"﴾ (Ta-Ha, 125), and in another place He says, ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and assume they are going to fall into it﴾ (al-Kahf, 53). Thus He negates sight for them in one verse and affirms it in another.

But these quibblers overlooked that a person passes through several stages after resurrection. At the moment they are brought forth from their graves, they are blind so that they cannot find the way to salvation. Afterwards, however, God shows them the most painful torment with which they will be punished, namely the Fire.

What befell them is a fitting recompense for what they had done. In this world they had themselves brought about blindness, deafness, and muteness. So when the Messenger called them to God, they stopped their ears and covered themselves with their garments.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 126:

﴿He said: "Just so. Our signs came to you, but you forgot them; and so today you are forgotten."﴾

That is: We shall deal with you as you dealt with Us, so We shall forget you as you forgot Our signs.

The word "āyāt" (signs) is the plural of "āyah," which means a wondrous matter. It is applied to the cosmic signs (al-āyāt al-kawniyyah) that draw attention to the One who brings things into being, glory be to Him, and it is applied to the miracles (al-mu'jizāt) that confirm the messengers and establish the truth of their conveyance from God. Although the cosmic signs draw attention to the power of the Creator, glory be to Him, and His wisdom, it is the Messenger who guides people to this power and to the One possessing this wisdom and power, which the intellect seeks.

O believer, this power is God, and God wants from you such-and-such. If you obey Him, then for you is such-and-such a reward, and if you disobey Him, then your punishment is such-and-such. Then He confirms the Messenger with miracles that show his truthfulness in conveying from his Lord.

The word "āyāt" is also applied to the verses of the Book that carry the rulings (aḥkām) and the method (manhaj).

You denied all these signs and did not heed them, so when you forgot the signs of God, your recompense was forgetting, a fitting recompense. The "forgetting" here means abandonment; otherwise, the forgetting that is the opposite of remembering is pardoned, and the one who suffers it is excused.

As for His words: ﴿And so today you are forgotten﴾: that is, you will be forgotten in bliss and in Paradise, but you will not be forgotten in punishment and recompense.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And thus do We recompense him who transgresses and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus...﴾ (Ta-Ha 127): that is, like this recompense. ﴿We recompense him who transgresses...﴾ (Ta-Ha 127). And al-israf (extravagance, excess) is exceeding the limit in a matter that has a reasonable limit. Eating, for example, Allah made for sustaining life; if one exceeds this limit, it is extravagance.

What Allah has made easy for you of your income you must spend within limits, then save the remainder so that you may advance by it in life. If you spend it all, you have been extravagant, and you will not be able to elevate yourself amid the luxury of life.

For this reason the Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils...﴾ (al-Isra' 27).

Islam has a mindful outlook on economics. The Truth wants you to spend, and wants you not to be extravagant; between these two limits the wheel of society turns and the machinery of life revolves. If one goes to extremes in either of them, the movement of life is halted, society is thrown into disorder, and goods go unsold.

The Almighty has clarified this outlook in His saying: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever moderate between that.﴾ (al-Furqan 67).

So your Lord wants you to combine the two matters, because stinginess and withholding halt the movement of life, while extravagance freezes life and deprives you of advancement and of pursuing the means of luxury. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So you will sit reproached and destitute.﴾ (al-Isra' 29).

Extravagance may also come from another direction: your Lord, mighty and majestic, created you, created for you the means of your life, and set for you the lawful and the unlawful. If you try to increase in the domain of the lawful what Allah has forbidden you, this is extravagance on your part and a transgression of the limit your Lord has set for you. You have exceeded the limit both in what He made lawful for you and in what He forbade you.

Extravagance may also come from yet another direction: a thing in itself may be lawful, but you take it from other than its lawful source.

If we carry the matter over to the obligations (al-taklif), we find that Allah, exalted is He, made some things lawful and forbade others. So do not transfer anything of what is forbidden to what is lawful, nor anything of what is lawful to what is forbidden, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ (al-A'raf 32).

And He addressed His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ (al-Tahrim 1).

Thus: your Lord does not constrict you, and forbids you to constrict yourself and to forbid yourself what He has made lawful for you, just as He blames you for making lawful what He has forbidden you, because that is for your benefit.

Just as extravagance occurs in food and drink, which are among the means of sustaining life, so it occurs likewise in sustaining the species through marriage and procreation until the Hour comes. Allah, the Truth, has set for sexual intercourse limits that secure offspring and lawful enjoyment; whoever transgresses these limits has been extravagant.

From His mercy, exalted is He, is that He forgives those who have been extravagant against themselves, on condition that they are believers: ﴿Say: O My servants who have been extravagant against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah...﴾ (al-Zumar 53).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus do We recompense him who transgresses...﴾ (Ta-Ha 127): Here He placed extravagance in a station following unbelief; therefore He said after it: ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord...﴾ (Ta-Ha 127), because when he turns the lawful into the unlawful, or the unlawful into the lawful, it is as if he has nullified the signs of Allah.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾ (Ta-Ha 127). So the discourse here is about this world; do not suppose that Allah defers all punishment for the disbeliever. There are things that are hastened upon him in this world and are not deferred.

The first thing that Allah does not defer but hastens in this world is the punishment for wrongdoing. It is not possible that the wrongdoer should die before the wronged one sees what Allah has done to him; otherwise, those who do not believe in the Resurrection or in recompense would have committed corruption among creation and spread mischief in the earth. Thus it is among the wisdom of Allah that we see for every wrongdoer a fall, so that the movement of life may be set right, even if the person is not a believer.

When the Almighty wishes to punish, His punishment is proportioned to His power, exalted is He, just as the blow of a child differs from the blow of a strong young man. So what he receives of punishment in life is light, because it comes from people; but the punishment of the Hereafter is another matter, because it is a punishment from Allah, proportioned to His power, exalted is He.

﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾ (Ta-Ha 127): "more lasting" because the punishment of this world ends with death, or with the one punished being pleased with you and showing mercy, or someone may intercede for you and remove the punishment from you. But in the Hereafter there is none of that; there is no escape from the punishment and no refuge.

1 Qatara al-rajul ʿala ʿiyalihi: he restricted them in spending. Qatr, iqtar and taqtir all have one meaning: restriction, which is the opposite of israf. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/100).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect.﴾

Al-hidayah: guidance, clarification and explanation; and "tahdihi" means: it guides him, i.e., shows him the way to good.

The interrogative in ﴿Has it not become clear to them...﴾ (Ta-Ha): the interrogative sometimes comes so that you learn what you do not know, or it comes to affirm what you have done.

So the meaning is: Did they not look at the earlier nations and at what befell them when they denied the messengers of Allah? As He said in another verse: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ (al-Saffat).

And He, glorified is He, said: ﴿By the dawn; and by ten nights; and by the even and the odd; and by the night when it passes. Is there in that an oath for one of understanding? Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the land, and Thamud who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh, owner of stakes?﴾ (al-Fajr).

Do you not see all these signs concerning the deniers? Do you not see that Allah supports His messengers? He, glorified is He, would not have sent them and then abandoned them and left them to their fate, as He said: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they will be the victorious﴾ (al-Saffat), and He said: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ (al-Hajj).

After all this, the deniers still present themselves as though they had seen none of these signs.

When you see (kam), know that it is for a great quantity that exceeds counting, as you say to your companion: "How many times I have given you, and how many times I have helped you," meaning: many times. It is as though you have entrusted him to answer himself, and you do not ask him except when the answer is certainly in your favour.

So the meaning of ﴿Has it not become clear to them...﴾ (Ta-Ha) is: it shows them and guides them to the many towns that denied their messengers, and what happened to them and what punishment befell them, and they should have taken heed, learned a lesson from them and not turned away from them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿...through whose dwellings they walk﴾ (Ta-Ha), is like His saying: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ (al-Saffat). It is not a history that is recounted; rather it is a present reality that you see with your own eyes, and walk among its ruins. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ (Ta-Ha): i.e., wonders for one who has a mind that reflects.

The word (al-nuha) is the plural of nuhya, which is intellect, and this word resolves for us many difficulties regarding disbelief. Some think that Allah created the intellect for us so that we may roam freely in the fields of thought as we wish, and slip out of every restraint.

But intellect comes from "al-iqal," the cord with which a camel is tied so that it does not escape from you. Likewise your intellect restrains you and organizes your movement, so that you do not walk through existence according to your whims. Intellect is given to you so that you may comprehend matters, and say: "This is right, and this is wrong," before you undertake them.

If the thief had reasoned about what he was doing, he would not have proceeded to steal from people. What do you think if we permitted all people to steal from you, while you are one individual and they are a multitude?

When your intellect restrains your sight from extending to what is forbidden to you, do not say: "It is restricting me," for He commanded others to lower their gaze from your forbidden things, and others are more numerous than you. Therefore, you are the beneficiary. If you wish to rampage over people's honour, then permit them to rampage over yours.

When a young man came to the Prophet ﷺ complaining of his inability to restrain his sexual desire, wishing to be permitted fornication, may Allah protect us, the Prophet ﷺ wanted to teach him a lesson that would turn him away from this sin. So what did he say to him?

He said: (O brother of the Arabs, would you like this for your mother? Would you like this for your sister? Would you like this for your wife?) And the young man would say each time: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, may I be your ransom." You can imagine what seizes one of us if he hears of his mother, his sister or his wife in this situation.

Then the Prophet ﷺ said to the young man, after shaking him with this powerful jolt: (Likewise, people do not like this for their mothers, nor for their wives, nor for their sisters, nor for their daughters).

Here the young man said: (By Allah, my soul never inclined to any of this without my remembering my mother, my wife, my sister and my daughter).

[Hence], intellect is the balance; it runs the equation and weighs things against one another. Likewise, if it comes with the meaning of restraint (nuha) or core understanding (lubb), they carry the same sense: "nuha" derives from "nahy" (prohibition) of a thing, and "lubb" means the reality and origin of a thing, not superficial thinking that wanders from here to there.

1 Al-hijr: intellect, because it restrains its possessor and keeps him from what is unfitting for him. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/144).
2 Jabahu yajuubuhu: he cut it. Jabu: i.e., they cut the rock, hewed it, and made their houses and idols from it. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/135).

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term.﴾

The discussion concerns the signs of Allah regarding those who denied the messengers and what punishment befell them. These people have passed by these signs without taking heed from them, without being deterred, or fearing that their end would be like the end of those before them. Perhaps these people say: "Here we are, in the state we are in, and no punishment has befallen us: no thunderbolt, no transformation, no wind. So with what do you threaten us?"

Therefore, Allah, glorified and exalted, clarifies this matter for them: "Nothing has prevented Us from doing to you what We did to your predecessors who denied the messengers. Nothing has prevented Us from humiliating and destroying you except one thing: a word that preceded from Allah."

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term.﴾ (Ta-Ha)

So what is this word that preceded from Allah and withheld punishment from them?

The word is His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ (al-Anfal)

This is the word that preceded from Me, which has withheld My punishment from you. The Messenger (ﷺ) clarifies this matter, saying: "Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins someone who will worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him."¹

If someone says: Allah threatens those who denied Muhammad (ﷺ) that He will bring down upon them what He brought down upon the deniers of the earlier nations, and yet here are the disbelievers of Makkah denying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without anything happening to them.

We say: because they have two securities from punishment: the word that preceded, and the specified term with Allah. ﴿And a specified term (Ta-Ha)⟩ so each one has a known term.

The meaning of ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizaman)﴾ (Ta-Ha): that is, it would have been inevitable that what befell the earlier nations would befall them.

¹ Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3231, 7389), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1795), from the hadith of Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her).

Then the Exalted One says: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased﴾ (20:130).

Since these people deny the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they are secure from punishment, they will certainly persist in their denial and continue in their obstinacy towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore, the Exalted, may He be glorified and exalted, turns to the other side and grants His Messenger (ﷺ) the fortitude necessary to confront this situation: ﴿So be patient over what they say..﴾ (20:130), for you have, for every act of patience, a reward commensurate with what you endure.

Patience may be easy and smooth in some situations, and it may be severe and difficult, requiring striving (mujahadah). Sometimes the Truth says to His Messenger (ﷺ): "Be patient" (isbir), and sometimes He says: "Persevere" (istabir) (1).

So what are the sayings over which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) must be patient? Their saying about him: "He is a sorcerer." Their saying: "He is a poet," and their saying: "He is possessed," and "a soothsayer," just as they said about the Qur'an: "Confused dreams." And they said: "Fables of the ancients." So be patient, O Muhammad, over all of this; for every one of their sayings carries within it the proof of their lie.

As for their saying about the Messenger of Allah that he is a sorcerer: who, then, has he bewitched? He has bewitched the believers in him. So why did he not bewitch you too, and the matter would end? Thus, your remaining in his opposition and disbelief in him is proof of his innocence from this accusation.

As for their saying: "He is a poet." How can that be, when they are a nation whose craft is speech, and the arts of speech, both its poetry and its prose, are theirs? How could the style of the Qur'an be hidden from them? In their view poetry is measured and rhymed speech; is the Qur'an like that? Had this accusation come from others than you, it would have been acceptable. But that it should come from you, O you who make markets for speech and exhibitions like the exhibitions of crafts today, this is not acceptable from you.

We have already said: if you read an article, for example, and a line of poetry passes by you, your ear senses it, and you feel that you have moved from prose to poetry, or from poetry to prose. Take, for example, the words of Ibn Zaydun (2):

("This blame has good consequences; this eclipse is a passing cloud that will clear. My lord's gift will not disturb me if its flow is slow, or if its aid is late, not stingy in its wealth. The buckets that fill slowest pour out the most, and the heaviest clouds move most slowly... With today comes tomorrow, and for every term there is a book. He has the right to reproach, and there is no blame on him for neglect.

If the deed that displeased was one,
then his deeds that pleased are thousands.")

Immediately your ear senses that you have moved from prose to poetry.

But when you read in the Qur'an, for example, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And women in the city said, "The wife of al-'Aziz is seeking to seduce her servant boy from himself. He has affected her with love. Indeed, we see her in manifest error." So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said, "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands and said, "Full of glory is Allah! This is not a human; this is none but an honorable angel." She said, "That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I did seek to seduce him, but he refused...﴾ (12:30-32).

Did you sense a shift of style from prose to poetry, or from poetry to prose? Yet if you measured ﴿Fa-dhalikunna alladhi lantunni fihi..﴾ (12:32), you would find it has a poetic metre.

And His saying: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (15:49).

If you wanted to make it a line of poetry, you would say: "Nabbi' 'ibadi annii anal-ghafurur-rahim." Yet when you read it in its context, you do not feel that it is poetry, because the style is unique of its kind. This is among the greatness of the Noble Qur'an: a speech unmatched in itself, unlike the speech of humans.

As for their saying "possessed" (majnun): the possessed person does not know what he does, does not reason about his conduct, and is not held to account for it. We cannot accuse him of anything and say, for example, that he is a liar or ugly, because his faculty of choice is inoperative, and he has no consistency in his conduct. He may smile in your face and then strike you at the same moment; he may give you something and then spit in your face.

The possessed has no character, while the Truth addresses His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe, you are not, by the favor of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted. And indeed, you are of a great character﴾ (68:1-4).

Character (khuluq) is the settled disposition toward good. How could Muhammad be a madman, when he is of great character? Moreover, have you ever tested him in anything that madmen do?

As for their saying that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fabricated this Qur'an: how can that be, when you have never heard from him before the mission any poetry or sermons, and he never said anything like this? How could he fabricate a style this miraculous, when he does not possess the craft of speech? And if Muhammad fabricated the Qur'an, why do you not fabricate the like of it and oppose him?

﴿Say, "Then bring forth a surah like it"﴾ (10:38).

Thus, from their very own sayings, the proofs of their lying and their false claims against the Messenger of Allah are established.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting..﴾ (20:130).

Glorification (tasbih) is the declaration of God's transcendence, and it is an attribute of God that exists before He creates anyone who glorifies and transcends Him. Therefore the Exalted says at the opening of Surat al-Isra': ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night..﴾ (17:1), because the event is contrary to the logic of laws; so He said: declare the transcendence of God's act above your acts.

Thus, "subhan" means that transcendence is established for God, even if no one were there to transcend. When God created the universe, the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them glorified God.

If glorification is established for God before the glorifier exists, then He was glorified by the first of His creation, and they continue to glorify Him. So you too, glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High. That is: declare Him transcendent, in His essence, attributes, acts and words, above what you see of creatures.

As for the meaning of ﴿with His praise..﴾ (20:130): because it is among the requirements of creation that it be varied in whims, aims and interests, contending and fighting one another over a fleeting thing, some being oppressors and some oppressed, some strong and some weak.

Thus there must be One in whom none of these attributes exists, to set the law and the straight balance that organizes the life of creatures. So this transcendence above resembling all temporal things, and above these deficiencies, is a blessing for which we must thank God and praise Him, praising Him that "there is nothing like Him." That makes the whole universe obedient; whereas if something were like Him, it might refuse obedience in ("Be, and it is").

Glorification and transcendence mean that the measure that governs the world is not the measure of the world, but is better and stronger, and this is to your benefit. So whenever you glorify God, remember that glorification is a blessing; thank God that there is nothing like Him. Glorify with praise of your Lord, for His transcendence returns good to those He created, and this is a blessing deserving your praise.

An example of this, and to God belongs the highest example, is the head of a household: this great, wise man, who speaks the word of truth and justice among its members, and who commands awe among them. You see them all praising God for his presence among them, because he preserves the balance of the household and organizes relations among its members. Do we not say in proverbs: "Whoever has no elder, let him buy himself an elder"?

Even if this elder is haughty, since his loftiness serves the members of his household, as each of them is kept within his limits.

Therefore among the names of God the Exalted are "al-Muta'ali" (the Exalted) and "al-Mutakabbir" (the Majestic). And this attribute, though detestable among people because it is baseless, is beloved to God, the Exalted, because it makes everyone other than Him a servant to Him. So His majesty and exaltedness are in truth: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (36:82).

Thus, the balance in the universe is preserved only by a power different from creation.

And His saying: ﴿before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾ (20:130).

That is: glorification constant and continuous, just as God's blessings upon you are continuous and never end. Every movement of yours is a blessing: sleep is a blessing, waking is a blessing, eating is a blessing, drinking is a blessing, sight and hearing; every movement of the events is a blessing deserving praise, and each of these blessings contains within it other blessings.

Take, for example, the movement of the hand with which you grasp. Consider how flexible and obedient it is to you as you wish, without any thought on your part: your fingers gather and hold things without your feeling the movement and coordination of the muscles. A person may not notice God's power in the movement of his hand until it is struck with paralysis, God forbid; then he knows it is a difficult process that none can accomplish except the Creator, Mighty and Majestic.

Therefore, the Truth, glorified and exalted, gives us the time of glorification and makes us live it at all times: ﴿before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day..﴾ (20:130).

"Ana'" (hours) is the plural of "inan," which is a part of time, and this part rises according to your awareness of glorifying and praising. So the meaning of glorification "during the hours of the night" is the parts of the whole night. Does this mean that a person has no task but glorification?

The logicians say of a part of time that it is "predicated by gradation" (maqul bil-tashkik): you may divide the night into hours and glorify in each hour, or rise higher and glorify each minute, or rise higher and glorify each second, and so on according to the stations and states of the one who glorifies and praises.

There are servants of God who do not slacken in their glorification for a single moment; you see them glorifying God in every movement of theirs, because they know they do not perform it by their own essence, as is evident from the fact that it may be taken from them at any time.

Thus the parts of time differ according to differences in stations and states. Do you not see that in measuring by a unit they measure by the meter, then by the centimeter, then by the millimeter? And in measuring time, the Japanese have reached devices that register a part of seven thousand parts of a second.

Then He says: ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾ (20:130): so that it encompasses all time, its night and its day, and all stations and states. Therefore some of the knowers say in their counsels that secure the soundness of the movement of life:

("Make your vigilance toward the One from whose gaze you are never free, for He is the one worthy of vigilance; let a person be attentive to this matter, so that his vigilance is not toward one who neglects him, or turns away, or sleeps.")

("And make your thanks to the One whose blessings never cease from you. So when you drink a cup of water, say: Praise be to God who has quenched me. When you feel its vigor within yourself, say: Praise be to God. And when you expel it as sweat or urine, say: Praise be to God. Thus is the continuity of praising God and perseverance in thanking Him.")

("And make your obedience toward the One you cannot do without; so long as you cannot do without Him, He is the most worthy of your obedience.")

("And make your submission toward the One whose dominion and authority you cannot leave; otherwise, where could you go?")

But why did He release the time of glorification at night, saying ﴿during the hours of the night﴾ (20:130), and specify it in the day, saying ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾ (20:130)?

They said: because the day is usually the place of work and striving, and glorification might distract you from your work, while your Lord commands us to walk in the earth and take part in the movement of life; and work helps one glorify, helps one obey, and helps you answer the call: "God is greater."

Do you not read the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in Surat al-Jumu'ah: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, hasten to the remembrance of God and leave trade. That is best for you, if you only knew. And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God; and remember God often that you may succeed﴾ (62:9-10).

That is because the movement of life is what helps you perform the obligation your Lord has laid upon you.

For example, in prayer you need to cover your nakedness. Look at this garment with which you cover your nakedness: how many hands have contributed to it, and how many movements of life have combined to bring it out in this form?

But at night you are at rest; you can devote yourself to glorifying God at any time from

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that which We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.﴾ (20:131)

After the Truthful, glorified is He, said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿So be patient over what they say...﴾ (20:130), He warned him not to look at these tyrants and obstinate ones as if they were in blessing, so that his eye would extend toward it. The meaning of extending the eye (madd al-ayn) is not to be limited to a mere glance within its capacity; rather, it directs it with desire and widens it so that it sees more than it should. Extending the eye always comes after occupying the soul with a blessing and aspiring toward it. It is as if God is saying: Do not occupy yourself with the bliss they are in, for it is the splendor of the world that swiftly passes away.

His saying: ﴿toward that which We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them...﴾ (20:131): "pairs" (azwaj) here does not mean man and woman; it means the associated kinds, as in His saying: ﴿And We appointed for them companions, who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them...﴾ (41:25).

Each one has a devil who accompanies him and does not leave him. This is the intended pairing; likewise in His saying: ﴿A speaker among them will say: Indeed, I had a companion [who used to say]...﴾ (37:51).

The "splendor" (zahrah) indicates the swiftness of its end and the brevity of life. It is the splendor of the life of this world, and what description of it is less than being "worldly"? This worldly provision which We have given them, which is passing, so they began to exult in it, is nothing but a trial and a test: ﴿that We may test them therein.﴾ (20:131). Testing occurs through good as it occurs through evil. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as trial.﴾ (21:35).

He, the Exalted, also says: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by honoring him and giving him favor, he says: My Lord has honored me.﴾ (89:15).

And he says: ﴿But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says: My Lord has humiliated me.﴾ (89:16).

Here the Truthful, glorified is He, corrects this notion for them. He says: Both of you are lying in this statement. Blessing is not a proof of honor, nor is its removal a proof of humiliation: ﴿No! Rather, you do not honor the orphan. And you do not urge one another to feed the poor. And you consume the inheritance, devouring all.﴾ (89:17–19).

So suppose God gave you a blessing but you did not render its thanks and its due; then what honor is in it?

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.﴾ (20:131). That is: Do not preoccupy yourself with what God has given them, for He, glorified is He, will give you something greater than this. The provision of your Lord is better than this passing bliss, more enduring and more lasting, for it is everlasting and never cut off in the abode of permanence, which neither escapes them nor escapes you. As for these people, their bliss is limited: either it will leave them through poverty, or they will leave it through death.
