Then the Almighty says: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you, and the good end is for piety﴾.

Here Allah, blessed and exalted is He, gives us a method for reforming society and ensuring its harmony. It is a method that begins with the first unit, the head of the family. He must first reform himself, then look to the second unit, which is the immediate cell closest to him, namely his household and family. He is the centre of the circle, so when he reforms himself, he must reform the other circles directly connected to him.

As for His saying: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family..﴾: so that the first unit in the construction of the universe may be upright. When the first unit in the construction of the universe is sound, and each person enjoins prayer upon his family, the whole universe becomes upright and the condition of everyone is set right.

The matter here is not limited to mere command, such that his responsibility ends at that point. Rather, ﴿and be steadfast in it..﴾: because prayer involves hardship that requires patience. Prayer needs time that you take from the movement of life, which is the cause of good and benefit for you, so there must necessarily be patience in it.

There is a difference between اصبر (iṣbir) and اصطبر (iṣṭabir). Iṣbir is the ordinary verb, whereas iṣṭabir here is intensive, meaning: put yourself to effort even in patience, and deliberately intend it.

Among this is that you be keen to perform the prayer in front of your children, so as to fix in their minds the importance of prayer. For example, you enter the house and find the food has been brought, and you say to your children: "Wait for me a few minutes until I pray." Here the children notice that prayer is more important even than eating, and it plants in their souls a sense of awe of the obligation, respect for the obligatory prayer, and the eagerness to place it before any other deed, whatever it may be.

Our master ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to stand in the night and pray as much as Allah willed for him, until the call to the dawn prayer was made. Then he would wake his family for prayer, and if they refused, he would sprinkle water on their faces.(1) For prayer is better than sleep. Sleep at such a time brings rest to the body, but prayer is better and greater, and it is enough that you are in the presence of Allah, the Exalted, through it.

Suppose the head of the family had been absent from them for a month or a year, and then suddenly they were told: "Your father has come." You would see them all hastening to him. And to Allah belongs the highest likeness: if He calls you, do not hold back from His call, but hasten to Him and be quick to answer His summons. You may imagine someone calling you while you do not respond or answer him; I think that is unacceptable, and your friend would not be pleased with it.

Therefore, you must train your children to respect this call, and as soon as they hear "Allahu Akbar" they should answer the call, not placing anything else before it. Allah does not bless a deed that distracts you from the call of "Allahu Akbar," because you have become occupied with the blessing rather than the Bestower, Mighty and Majestic is He.

So, if you wish to know the best elements of society, look at which of them are the quickest to answer the call of "Allahu Akbar." And if you wish to know who is highest in rank among them, look at who is the last to leave the mosque, not the one who comes to prayer late and hurries to leave the moment the salam is given.

It is narrated that our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reproached one of the Companions for hastening to leave the mosque after the salam. On one occasion the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) deliberately called out to him and said: "Are you averse to us?"

Is there anyone who would be averse to seeing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and sitting with him? The man said: "No, O Messenger of Allah, but I have a wife at home who is waiting for this garment of mine so that she may pray in it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then prayed for him, and the man went off to his wife. She said to him: "You have been delayed by the length of so-and-so of tasbih." He said: "The Messenger of Allah detained me, and such-and-such happened." She said to him: "Did you complain of your Lord to Muhammad?"

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you..﴾.

So: what is it that preoccupies you from the presence of your Lord? As for provision: ﴿We do not ask you for provision..﴾: for the one who cannot work, we direct to him from the wealthy one who knocks on his door and gives to him. Wealth is a condition of the poor man's faith, but it is not a condition of the rich man's faith.

It is as though Allah, glorified is He, gives us a sign of the necessity of seeking out the poor and knocking on their doors to give them their right from the wealth of the rich, not waiting for them to ask and shed the dignity of their faces while seeking one of their rights in a society of faith.

As for His saying: ﴿We provide for you..﴾: that is, We do not ask you for provision and then abandon you; rather, We do not ask you, and then We provide for you. So be at peace concerning this matter.

﴿And the good end is for piety﴾: because when the affairs of life become constricted for you, you turn to Allah, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) would, when a matter distressed him, say: "Turn us to the prayer." The constriction of affairs comes when we lose the means that Allah has granted, and when the means are lost and one's devices are exhausted, nothing remains but to turn to the One who causes all causes, glorified is He, as He says in another verse:

﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out (2), and will provide for him from where he does not expect..(3)﴾ (al-Talaq).

1 Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (336) from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who rises at night and prays, and wakes his wife so that she prays; if she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face. May Allah have mercy on a woman who rises at night and prays, and wakes her husband so that he prays; if he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face."

Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾

We have already encountered *lawlā* (لولا) in His saying: ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord...﴾ (Yunus 10:19). There it means the prevention of punishment because of the presence of the word. Here, however, *lawlā* means *halla* (هلا), "why not," used to urge and demand, as in: ﴿Why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, "What Allah wills [happens]"...?﴾ (al-Kahf 18:39).

It is as if the Qur'an does not impress them, even though they are a people of eloquence and clear expression, and a people of fluency and speech. The Qur'an puts them to shame by its eloquence and rhetorical power. So what sign do you want after this Qur'an?

﴿And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?"﴾ means a sign as proof of the truth of what he conveys from Allah, like the sensory miracles that occurred for the messengers before him. As He says: ﴿And they said, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines and cause rivers to gush forth within it in force, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as guarantors, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (al-Isra' 17:90–93).

So the signs come from Allah; I have no part in them and do not choose them. Here is the Qur'an before you, informing you of what happened to the earlier nations. ﴿So ask the people of remembrance, if you do not know﴾ (al-Nahl 16:43).

And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses﴾ (al-A'la 87:14–19).

And He says: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah...﴾ (al-Nisa' 4:163).

Therefore, after this, He says: ﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:133).

The Qur'an came comprehensive and dominating over the previous books, and in it is mention of everything that occurred in them of sensory miracles. Did these people witness the miracle of Jesus (peace be upon him) in healing the blind and the leper? Did they see the staff of Moses or the she-camel of Salih?

They knew these miracles when the Qur'an related them to them, so they became reports among reports, not things seen. A sensory miracle happens once; whoever witnesses it believes in it, and for whoever does not see it, it is a report. Had the Qur'an not related them, none of them would have believed them.

But these people want a sensory miracle that accompanies the message of Muhammad, which is general for all time and place. Had Muhammad's miracle been sensory, it would have been only for those who witnessed it. Allah, glorified is He, wills it to be a lasting miracle extending across time and place. So to whoever believes in Muhammad we say: this is his lasting miracle, which will remain until the Hour comes.

Therefore, the Qur'an is a miracle for all centuries. Had the Qur'an expended its miracle once, for its contemporaries only, the coming centuries would have received it without any miraculous quality. But the will of Allah decreed that the inimitability of the Qur'an be a secret hidden within it, and each century discovers some of its secrets in proportion to their attention to it and their reflection upon it. Thus the message remains guarded by the miracle.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it [the Messenger], they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: I have established the proof against them, because if I had destroyed them during a gap between messengers, they would have said: "Why did You not let us live until a messenger came to us? Then, had a messenger come to us, we would have believed in him before we fell into humiliation and disgrace." So the meaning of: "And had We destroyed them with a punishment before the Qur'an came, they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we would have believed in him and been guided."

This is merely a word that its speaker utters, as the Truth, glory be to Him, said about them: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden; indeed they are liars﴾ (al-An'am). That is: it is merely a word that rescues them from the difficulty.

As for their saying: ﴿before we are humiliated and disgraced﴾ (Ta-Ha): al-dhull (humiliation) is what befalls a living being that results in its being broken after it had been haughty. Humiliation comes first through defeat, and more humiliating than defeat is capture, because one may be defeated and then flee; and more humiliating than both is killing. Thus, humiliation occurs in this world, before those who witness it and those contemporary with the breaking of one who was once exalted.

As for al-khizy (disgrace): "nakhza" means "disgrace befalls us," and it is the collapse of the self after it had been elevated. From this they say: "You were disgraced (kharyta)," meaning: you were waiting for something and found the opposite of it.

From this is His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection...﴾ (Al 'Imran). So if humiliation is hastened for them in this world, disgrace is deferred to the Hereafter, so that their shame is exposed before the witnesses, as they say ("a scandal with bells"), where their disgrace is witnessed by all the people of the gathering.

There is a amusing incident connected with this word "disgrace" from the time when we were children memorizing the Qur'an at the hands of our master, the honourable Shaykh Hasan Zaghlul — may Allah have mercy on him — who was blind, and we would "trick" him. When we found an opportunity, we would turn away from him and flee from having our memorized tablet corrected, for whoever memorizes alone in this way from the mushaf is exposed to error.

From this is what actually happened with a classmate of ours named Shaykh Muhammad Hasan Abd al-Bari. The school principal suddenly arrived and wished to hear us, and Shaykh Abd al-Bari had not corrected his tablet from which he was to recite. So he recited: "Indeed, whoever You cause to enter the Fire, You have truly disgraced him" (إنك من تدخل النار فقد أخزيته), reading it with the letter ra (ر) instead of zay (ز). The Shaykh laughed for a long time — may Allah have mercy on him — and said: "My son, the meaning is correct, but the transmission is not like this."

We would take this against Shaykh Abd al-Bari, so whoever wanted to annoy him would say: "Indeed, whoever You cause to enter the Fire..." and stop! !

Then Allah the Exalted willed that each of us be exposed to a similar situation for which he would be taken to task. I was taken to task in this way when I recited without correcting my tablet the beginning of Surah al-Shura: "Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf," and I had known "Ha Mim" but "'Ayn Sin Qaf" had not come to me, so I recited "Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf" with connection. So whenever I said to the Shaykh Abd al-Bari, "Indeed, whoever You cause to enter the Fire...", he would say: "Ha Mim."

We said: "Glory be to Allah! Whoever lives long enough to be surprised by something will not die until he sees it," (من يعب يوما بشيء* لم يمت حتى يراه).

So the saying of these people: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we would follow Your signs before we are humiliated and disgraced﴾ (Ta-Ha) — it is an excuse of theirs. The meaning: "If only You had sent a messenger to us, we would have followed him before we were humiliated in this world through defeat, captivity, or killing, and disgraced in the Hereafter through public exposure before the witnesses of the gathering."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 20, verse 135:

At-tarabbus (waiting in readiness, watching for an opportunity): the state of being prepared for something to befall another. You say: "So-and-so waits for me" (yatarabbasu bi), meaning: he watches me and follows me, awaiting from me a slip or an error. So His saying: ﴿Say: "Each is waiting, so wait; and you will know..."﴾ (Surah Taha) means: each of us waits for the other to stumble, and watches what will happen to him, because we are enemies.

Allah, exalted is He, has also clarified the waiting, from Him and from them, in another verse: ﴿Say: "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things?"﴾ (Surah At-Tawbah, 52).

Meaning: What do you await for us except one of the two best outcomes? Either we die in fighting you as martyrs, or we triumph over you and humiliate you. So whatever waiting befalls us is an honour for us: either victory or martyrdom. Both are good outcomes (husna). We, on the other hand, await for you that Allah strike you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. Both are evil (saw'ah) for you.

Since the matter is so, then wait as you wish, and we wait for you as we wish, because our waiting for you pleases us, and your waiting for us pains and grieves you.

As for the meaning of ﴿Say...﴾ (Surah Taha, 135) here: the saying "each is waiting" is not from Muhammad. He does not hold the reins of the universe, nor does he know the unseen. Rather, it is the speech of Allah, who said to him "Say" (qul), O Muhammad: "Each is waiting, so wait."

Therefore: it was spoken by One who holds the reins of affairs and their bridles, and nothing goes outside His will, exalted is He. Perhaps, if I said it to you on my own, you would say: "This is the speech of a human being who possesses nothing of affairs." Therefore take it not by the measure of human speech, but by the measure of One who holds the reins of all the decrees of mankind.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So you will know who are the companions of the even path and who has been guided﴾ (Surah Taha, 135). When will this happen? At the hour when the Hour arises, where the departure is either to a Garden or to a Fire. At that time you will know who are the companions of the even path: we or you? But it will be a knowledge that benefits not and avails not, for it comes after the opportunity has passed. It is the time of reckoning, not the time of working and making amends for errors.

It is a knowledge that brings no work that could save you, for the time of work has ended. Thus it becomes a knowledge that increases their regret, harms them, and does not benefit them.

As-sirat: the straight path. As-sawiyy: the straight that has no crookedness in it and no deviation.

He then said: ﴿and who has been guided﴾ (Surah Taha, 135). This is because the even path may exist while no one walks it. So the intended meaning is: the even path, and whoever was guided to it and walked it.

Someone may suppose that this matter of waiting will be prolonged, so the Truth, exalted is He, cuts off this supposition with His saying at the beginning of the following Surah al-Anbiya: ﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near for them﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya, 1).

Thus the two surahs harmonize, and the meaning connects between the verses.
